title: Matching a `ref`-scrutinee enum and using a non-i64-word payload (String / bool / narrow int / float) miscompiles: the via-ptr fast path binds the leaf directly at the i64 payload WORD, so `*binding` / a method call deref-loads the wrong shape. A String payload → codegen PANIC `into_struct_value` "Found IntValue … expected the StructValue variant" (`%s.deref = load i64`) at the `.push_str(s)` dispatch; a bool payload → module-verify `Branch condition is not 'i1' type! br i64 %b.deref`.
detail: Minimal repro (panics on `karac build` AND `karac run` JIT): `enum E { S(String), N(i64) } fn render(e: ref E, out: mut ref String) { match e { S(s) => { out.push_str(s); } N(n) => { out.push_str("num"); } } }`. Root cause: `bind_pattern_values_via_ptr`'s `TupleVariant` arm (`src/codegen/pattern_binding.rs`) took a `ok_padded_primitive` fast path (meant for `Option[i64]`'s over-wide 3-word slot) whenever the FIRST payload LLVM word was primitive — but every heap aggregate flattens to `{ptr:i64,…}` so its first word IS i64, and narrow scalars sit in an i64 slot too. It then `emit_ref_leaf_binding_at_ptr(s, field_ptr, field_ty=i64)` bound the leaf as a `ref i64`. The value-source (copy-shim) path already reconstructs payloads at their true type (narrowing bool→i1, rebuilding String/Vec), so the fix is to DEFER to it.
source: dogfood:examples/json.kara (recursive JSON enum, `match v { Num(n) => out.push_str(n), Bool(b) => if *b … }`)
resolution: FIXED 2026-07-11. In the via-ptr `TupleVariant` arm, added `declared_mismatches_word`: look up the leaf binding's recorded surface type (`pattern_binding_types`) → `llvm_type_for_name`, and if it isn't the i64 payload word, `return Ok(None)` to defer to the value-source path. Covers String/Vec (struct ≠ i64), bool (i1), narrow ints (i8/i16/i32), char (i32), f64 — while `Option[i64]` (name "i64" == i64 word) keeps the fast path. Type-info-absent bindings keep the legacy heuristic (no regression). Generalizes the B-2026-07-09-6 struct-payload guard to every non-word payload. Regression tests/codegen.rs::test_e2e_ref_enum_string_and_bool_payload; 2130 codegen + 587 asan green.

title: A `Vec[struct]` bound as an enum payload loses its element TypeExpr, so `for e in entries { e.field }` binds the element without a struct type and the field read returns garbage (`i64 0`) → codegen PANIC at the `push_str(e.field)` dispatch. A `Vec[i64]` enum payload iterates fine (primitive elements need no field GEP), and a plain `let es: Vec[Ent]` local field-access works — only the intersection (Vec-of-struct AS an enum payload) breaks.
detail: Minimal repro: `enum J { N, Obj(Vec[Ent]) } struct Ent { key: String } fn ser(v: ref J, out: mut ref String) { match v { N => {out.push_str("n");} Obj(entries) => { for e in entries { out.push_str(e.key); } } } }`. Root cause: the value-source enum-payload binding (`src/codegen/pattern_binding.rs`, the `"Vec"|"VecDeque"` arm) registered `vec_elem_types[name]` (the LLVM element type — enough for a for-loop over a `Vec[i64]` payload) but NOT `var_elem_type_exprs[name]` (the element TypeExpr that struct-field GEP resolves through). A plain local gets both via `register_var_from_type_expr`; the payload path got only the former, so a struct element had no TypeExpr and `e.field` fell through to an i64 read.
source: dogfood:examples/json.kara (`Obj(entries: Vec[Entry]) => for e in entries { escape_into(e.key, out); ser_into(e.val, out) }`)
resolution: FIXED 2026-07-11. The `"Vec"|"VecDeque"` payload-binding arm now also `self.var_elem_type_exprs.insert(name, inner_te.clone())` alongside `vec_elem_types`, so the for-loop element carries the struct TypeExpr and `e.field` GEPs correctly — identical to a plain `let es: Vec[Ent]`. Regression tests/codegen.rs::test_e2e_ref_enum_vec_struct_payload_field_access; 2130 codegen + 587 asan green.

title: `?` on a `Result[<concrete user enum>, E]` truncates the multi-word Ok payload to its first word: `let v = pv()?` where `pv() -> Result[Json, String]` and `Json` is a wide (>1-word) enum yields `v` typed as a bare `i64` (the tag/first word), not the full enum aggregate. A later use (`Entry { val: v }`, method call) then mis-types it → module-verify `Invalid InsertValueInst operands! insertvalue { …, {i64,i64,i64,i64} } …, i64 %v, 1` (an i64 inserted where the 4-word enum struct is expected). Explicit `match pv() { Ok(x) => x, Err(e) => return … }` works — ONLY the `?` sugar truncates.
detail: Minimal repro (`karac build` / JIT fail; interpreter fine): `enum Json { Null, Str(String), Obj(Vec[Entry]) } struct Entry { key: String, val: Json } fn pv() -> Result[Json, String] { Result.Ok(Json.Null) } fn po() -> Result[Json, String] { let mut es: Vec[Entry] = Vec.new(); let v = pv()?; es.push(Entry { key: "k", val: v }); Result.Ok(Json.Obj(es)) }`. ROOT CAUSE (precise): `reconstruct_question_ok_payload` (`src/codegen/exprs.rs`) rebuilds a multi-word Ok payload only when its type is found in `string_typed_exprs` (String) or `enum_inst_type_exprs` (generic `Named`); otherwise it `return Ok(w0)` — truncating to one word. `enum_inst_type_exprs` is populated in `src/lowering.rs:~498` with a `Type::Named { args } if !args.is_empty()` filter, which EXCLUDES a concrete (arg-less) user enum like `Json`. So `?` on `Result[Json, …]` can't find `Json`'s type and truncates. String/Vec[T]/generic payloads work because they land in one of the two tables. FIX DIRECTION: give `reconstruct_question_ok_payload` the concrete-enum Ok payload type — either a dedicated `?`-Ok-payload TypeExpr table (populated from `tc.expr_types` at the `?` span, which already holds the unwrapped type per the fn's own comment), or broaden the `enum_inst_type_exprs` filter to include arg-less enums (verify the other consumer — the Some-payload heap-vs-word decision — is unaffected). The failure-path (`Err`) already reconstructs wide payloads via `rebuild_value_from_payload_words`; the Ok-path needs the same type resolution for concrete enums.
source: dogfood:examples/json.kara (`let v = self.parse_value()?; entries.push(Entry { key: k, val: v })` in parse_object)
tracker: examples/json.kara (blocks the JIT/build path; interpreter-verified via KARAC_RUN_JIT=0)
investigation: Minimally reduced from the full JSON parser through ~10 repros: eliminated recursion, ref-vs-value match, Vec-of-enum, Vec-of-struct field access (those were B-2026-07-11-6, fixed), Result-Ok binding via match (works), and struct-construction-with-enum-field-from-identifier (works). The ONLY trigger is the `?` operator on a Result whose Ok type is a concrete multi-word enum. Interpreter (tree-walk) is correct throughout.
resolution: FIXED 2026-07-11. Two-part fix. (1) TYPE: added a lowering-derived `concrete_named_type_exprs` table (src/lowering.rs) — the arg-less-Named complement of `enum_inst_type_exprs` — keyed by span, consumed ONLY by `reconstruct_question_ok_payload` (src/codegen/exprs.rs) so it can resolve a concrete user enum/struct Ok-payload's type that the generic-only table dropped. (2) WORD SPAN: an enum's LLVM layout is flat i64 words (`{i64 tag, i64…}`), so reconstruct now FLAT-COPIES all the enum's words verbatim from the Result's payload fields, sidestepping `rebuild_value_from_payload_words`'s 3-word cap (which truncated a 4-word heap-bearing enum, dropping `cap` -> invalid free). Memory-safe (ASAN green) for borrow, move-out, and wide tuple-variant payloads. examples/json.kara now `karac build`s to a native binary matching the oracle byte-for-byte. Regressions: tests/codegen.rs::test_e2e_question_on_result_concrete_enum + tests/memory_sanitizer.rs::asan_question_on_result_heap_enum_no_leak_or_double_free.

title: [NOT A BUG — REVERTED, misdiagnosis] The interpreter prints an `Error return trace:` block to output for an error that was HANDLED (caught by a `match`/`if let`), not just for one that escapes to the top. A program that uses `?` internally and handles every error (e.g. `match parse(x) { Ok(v) => …, Err(e) => println(e) }`) still dumped a stale `?`-propagation trace at exit, polluting program output.
detail: Repro: any program with a `fn helper() -> Result[T,E]` that a caller invokes with `?`, whose error is ultimately caught by a `match`, and where no LATER successful `?` runs. `cmd_run` (`src/cli.rs:~5005`) printed the `?`-error-return trace whenever the ring buffer was non-empty at exit, unconditionally. The buffer (`error_trace`) gets a frame pushed per `?` that re-propagates an `Err` (`eval_expr.rs` Question arm) and is CLEARED only by a later successful `?` (Ok/Some) — never when a propagated `Err` is caught by a match. So a handled `?`-error left stale frames that printed as an `Error return trace`. Only the LAST `?`-propagated error's frames survive (each Ok-`?` clears), which is why it looked intermittent (only errors reaching the top via `?` with no trailing Ok-`?` showed a trace).
source: dogfood:examples/json.kara (its 3 error round-trips all handled via `match parse(x) { Err(e) => … }`, yet the last printed a trace)
resolution: REVERTED 2026-07-11 — MISDIAGNOSIS, not a bug. The `?`-error-return trace is written to STDERR (never stdout) and INTENTIONALLY prints for a HANDLED error too: a debug diagnostic recording the last error's propagation path, cleared only on a subsequent successful `?`. tests/codegen.rs::test_e2e_question_trace_single_frame_on_err exercises a `?`-error caught by a `match` and asserts the trace IS present. The originally-committed interpreter gate (cli.rs) + a codegen main-exit-clear were both reverted; examples/json.kara's stdout oracle was always clean (2>/dev/null), so there was never a real problem. Lesson: the trace lives on stderr and is handling-agnostic by design.

title: RC-fallback false-positive on a loop accumulator moved out via an early `return`: an accumulator built in a loop and returned from a branch inside that loop (`loop { items.push(parse()?); if done() { return Result.Ok(Json.Arr(items)); } }`) fires a `perf[rc-fallback]` on `items`/`out`/`entries`. The ownership analysis treats the loop-branch `return` (consume) and the fall-through `push` (use) as a potential reuse-after-consume, though the `return` is terminal and the two are mutually exclusive.
detail: SURFACE NOTE: ergonomics — Repro: `fn f() -> Result[Json,String] { let mut items = Vec.new(); loop { items.push(parse()?); if done() { return Result.Ok(Json.Arr(items)); } } }` -> `perf[rc-fallback] ... 'items' (direct re-use after consume)`. The RC fallback is CORRECT-but-suboptimal (the program runs), so this is an analysis-precision / diagnostic-quality item, not a miscompile: a value moved on a terminal early-return path and mutated on the fall-through path of the same loop is single-owner and needs no RC. FIX DIRECTION: teach the RC-fallback pass that a move at a loop-body `return` is terminal, so it doesn't alias the fall-through mutation. NOTE: the original filing ALSO claimed 'no Iterator.collect()' -- that was WRONG (author error: called `.len()` directly on the `Iterator`, never tried `.collect()`). `Iterator[T].collect() -> Vec[T]` is fully implemented (typechecker src/typechecker/stdlib_iter.rs, interpreter + codegen); `s.chars().collect()` and `(0..n).collect()` both work. examples/json.kara now uses it directly, dropping the unnecessary `to_chars` helper.
tracker: backlog (ownership RC-fallback precision on loop early-return)

title: Pushing an empty `Vec.new()` into a `Vec[Vec[i64]]` does not infer the inner element type from the receiver/method signature — `out.push(Vec.new())` where `out: Vec[Vec[i64]]` fails typecheck with "expected 'Vec<i64>', found 'Vec<?T0>'", requiring an explicit `let empty: Vec[i64] = Vec.new(); out.push(empty)`. The expected argument type of `push` (Vec[i64]) is statically known, so a more complete bidirectional inference would propagate it into the empty `Vec.new()` literal (Rust infers the analogous `v.push(Vec::new())`). LOW severity / ergonomics only: it is a CLEAN, actionable typecheck error (not a cryptic message, not a run/build divergence), and the one-line type annotation is idiomatic rather than a contortion — so the kata was NOT routed around, just annotated. Surfaced while adding the Gosper's-hack bitmask variant, whose k==0 case pushes the single empty combination; the DFS solvers never hit it because their empty combination comes from `path.clone()` of an already-typed empty `path`. REPRO: `fn main(){ let mut out: Vec[Vec[i64]] = Vec.new(); out.push(Vec.new()); println(f"{out.len()}"); }`. FIX DIRECTION: thread the expected type from the call argument position into the `Vec.new()` associated-call inference (expected-type propagation for empty container constructors in argument position), then the annotation becomes unnecessary. FIXED 2026-07-11 (this commit): the `push` special-case arm in `src/typechecker/expr_method_call.rs` inferred the argument in synthesis mode, then unified the receiver element type (`Vec[i64]`) with the arg (`Vec[?T0]`) — correctly binding `?T0 = i64` — but only TOP-LEVEL-resolved (`resolve_type_var_top`) before the assignability check, so the arg's NESTED `?T0` stayed stale and `check_assignable(Vec[i64], Vec[?T0])` reported a spurious `expected 'Vec<i64>', found 'Vec<?T0>'`. FIX: deep-resolve BOTH the receiver element type and the arg type through the substitutions the unify just populated (`resolve_type_vars` with empty name-maps) before `check_assignable` — mirroring how the general generic-call path (`check_call_args_with_substitution_full` pass 2) resolves slots. The empty-constructor push now infers without the `let empty: Vec[i64] = Vec.new()` annotation, and codegen builds+runs correctly (`out.len()` == 1). This reuses the unify's binding rather than threading an expected type into `Vec.new()`'s associated-call inference (the original FIX DIRECTION) — same user-visible result, smaller blast radius; the scalar `v.push(5)` receiver-var pinning path is preserved. Test: tests/typechecker.rs::test_push_empty_vec_new_into_nested_vec_infers_element.

RUN-vs-BUILD divergence: `karac run` (JIT-default) cannot execute a `gpu.dispatch` program. `#[gpu] fn double(x: f32) -> f32 { x*2.0 }` + `gpu.dispatch(double, buf)` runs correctly two ways — `karac build` (auto-selects libkarac_runtime_gpu.a, links Metal, dispatches on the real GPU) and `karac run` with `KARAC_RUN_JIT=0` (tree-walk interpreter, element-wise CPU) — both byte-identical `[1,2,3,4]f32 -> 2 4 6 8`. But the DEFAULT `karac run` (JIT, since the Slice-6c JIT-default flip) fails: `JIT session error: Symbols not found: [ _karac_runtime_gpu_map ]` then `lookup_address("main"): Failed to materialize symbols`. The in-process JIT runner's runtime rlib is not built with the opt-in `gpu` feature, so the dispatch symbol is absent and `main` cannot be materialized.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: GPU slice-0 spine live-verification on Metal (Slipstream GPU-status audit; docs/dogfooding.md + phase-10-targets GPU-LBM breakdown) — Repro (macOS/Metal, 2026-07-10): gpu_slice0.kara = `#[gpu] fn double(x: f32) -> f32 { x * 2.0 }` + `fn main(){ let buf: Vec[f32]=[1.0,2.0,3.0,4.0]; let out=gpu.dispatch(double,buf); for v in out { println(f"{v}") } }`. `karac build gpu_slice0.kara && ./gpu_slice0` -> `2 4 6 8` (otool shows Metal.framework). `KARAC_RUN_JIT=0 karac run` -> `2 4 6 8`. Default `karac run` -> `Symbols not found: [ _karac_runtime_gpu_map ]`. ROOT CAUSE: the `gpu` feature (wgpu/Metal backend, libkarac_runtime_gpu.a) is opt-in and NOT enabled for the JIT runner's runtime rlib, so the LLJIT dlsym generator cannot resolve `_karac_runtime_gpu_map`. The Slice-6c JIT-default flip collides with the slice-0 GPU spine (docs/spikes/gpu-wgsl-slice0.md). WORKAROUND: `KARAC_RUN_JIT=0` (interp CPU fallback) or `karac build` the program. FIX OPTIONS: (a) feature-gate the gpu runtime symbols into the JIT runner rlib + add to `__preserve_no_mangle_symbols` (cf. the env.set FFI keep-list gotcha in the JIT-default work); or (b) route `#[gpu]`/`gpu.dispatch` programs in `karac run` to the tree-walk interpreter regardless of KARAC_RUN_JIT. Does NOT affect the shipped AOT path or the interpreter; scoped to the experimental gpu.dispatch surface.
tracker: docs/implementation_checklist/phase-10-targets.md Track C (GPU); memory project_gpu_dispatch_jit_gap; relates to project_jit_default_flip_blocked (__preserve_no_mangle_symbols keep-list)
resolution: Fixed in 05d72ed via FIX OPTION (b): `cmd_run` (src/cli.rs) now detects a `#[gpu]` kernel (`program_declares_gpu_kernel` — any top-level `#[gpu] fn` or `#[gpu]` impl method) and routes such a program to the tree-walk interpreter (element-wise CPU) instead of the LLJIT, regardless of the Slice-6c JIT-default. The interpreter needs no GPU backend, so `karac run gpu_slice0.kara` now prints `2 4 6 8` like `karac build` and `KARAC_RUN_JIT=0`. Chose (b) over (a) [feature-gate the gpu symbols into the JIT runner rlib] because (a) drags the heavy wgpu/naga/objc2 dep tree (+~4.5 MB) into every JIT run for an experimental surface, whereas (b) is a contained driver-side gate. Kernel detection is a sound superset of detecting an actual `gpu.dispatch` call (a `#[gpu]` fn is only reachable through dispatch; the interpreter runs every program, so a declared-but-never-dispatched kernel routes there harmlessly). Non-GPU programs stay JIT-default; the `--interp` / `KARAC_RUN_JIT=0` escape hatches still work. Reproduced on x86-64 Linux (no GPU needed — the interpreter path is CPU) and verified all three run forms agree. Regression: `tests/cli.rs::test_run_gpu_dispatch_routes_to_interpreter`. The AOT `karac build` GPU path is untouched.

source: dogfood:gpu_gate1 (surfaced building the CG-4 struct-SoA gpu.dispatch demo / GPU-GATE-1)
title: Reading a field from a LITERAL-constructed SoA binding segfaults under codegen. `let world: Vec[Particle] = [Particle{..}, Particle{..}]` with `layout world: Vec[Particle] { group gp { pos } group gv { vel } }`, then `world[1].pos` (any SoA field/index read) → SIGSEGV (exit 139) in the compiled binary; the tree-walk interpreter (KARAC_RUN_JIT=0) computes it correctly (run-vs-build divergence + memory unsafety on a valid program). Narrowly isolated: SoA-literal + `world.len()` works; PUSH-built SoA + `world[1].pos` works; plain AoS (no layout) literal + read works — ONLY literal-construction × SoA field/index read crashes. Likely the SoA collection-literal builder allocates the SoA vec header (ptr-per-group + len/cap) but does not allocate/populate the per-group backing-array pointers the way the push/index-store path does, so the read derefs a garbage/uninitialized group pointer. RESOLVED 2026-07-11 (e86942e): SoA let-binding path (stmts.rs) handled only Vec.new()/with_capacity and layout-returning calls, so a collection-literal RHS fell through to AoS construction — the AoS {ptr,len,cap} header was stored into the SoA slot and every later world[i].field read decoded it as the multi-group SoA struct -> garbage group-ptr deref -> SIGSEGV. FIX: soa_literal_elems detects a [..]/Vec[..] RHS and compile_soa_let_from_literal (exprs.rs) builds an empty SoA header then replays each element through the compile_soa_method push decomposition. Test test_e2e_soa_literal_construction_field_read; codegen 2140.
detail: Repro (macOS, `karac build`): `struct Particle { pos: f32, vel: f32 }` · `layout world: Vec[Particle] { group gp { pos } group gv { vel } }` · `fn main(){ let world: Vec[Particle] = [Particle{pos:0.0,vel:1.0}, Particle{pos:5.0,vel:2.0}]; println(f"{world[1].pos}"); }` → exit 139. Diagnostic matrix (same struct+layout): (A) literal + `world.len()` → 2 (ok — header allocated); (B) `let mut world = Vec.new(); world.push(..); world.push(..); world[1].pos` → 5 (ok — push builds group buffers); (C) no layout block, AoS literal + `world[1].pos` → 5 (ok). Failing intersection = SoA-literal-construction × SoA-field-read. PRE-EXISTING SoA collection codegen (src/codegen/collections.rs / declarations.rs); NOT touched by the CG-4 GPU work that surfaced it (that diff adds only gpu.dispatch code — the repro uses no gpu.dispatch). Blocks the literal-init variant of the GPU-GATE-1 kata; the gate kata builds `world` via push instead. FIX DIRECTION: make the SoA collection-literal builder allocate + populate each group's backing array from the literal elements (scattering each field into its group), exactly as the SoA push/index-store path does — diff literal-construction lowering vs push in collections.rs. Verify under guardmalloc/ASan (garbage-pointer deref).
tracker: docs/implementation_checklist/phase-10-targets.md (CG-4 / GPU-GATE-1 gate kata builds `world` via push pending this); src/codegen/collections.rs SoA literal construction

title: A function whose value is a top-level `if`-expression with FLOAT type miscompiled: `fn relu(x: f32) -> f32 { if x > 0.0 { x } else { 0.0 } }` failed codegen with module-verify error "Function return type does not match operand type of return inst! ret i64 0 / float". `compile_if`'s value phi-merge (src/codegen/control_flow.rs) built a phi only when both branch LLVM types agreed, and `unify_int_branch_widths` reconciled only INTEGER width artifacts. A float literal (`0.0`) lowers at the default f64 width; beside an f32 sibling branch (a param / typed expr) the phi operands disagreed (f32 vs f64), the merge fell through to the `i64 0` placeholder, and the fn tail emitted `ret i64 0` against its `float` return type. The i64/int if-return worked (int harmonizer); float-specific. Any float `if`-return with a literal branch was affected — not gpu-specific.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: GPU-LBM-4 (surfaced allowing `if` in #[gpu] scalar kernels; the bug is general) — Repro (`karac build`, no gpu): `fn relu(x: f32) -> f32 { if x > 0.0 { x } else { 0.0 } } fn main(){ println(f"{relu(3.0)}"); println(f"{relu(-2.0)}"); }` → codegen error (i64 control: `fn pick(x:i64)->i64{ if x>0 {x} else {0} }` compiled + printed 3/0 fine). ROOT CAUSE: compile_if's `(false,false)` (neither arm diverges) branch built the phi under `tv.get_type()==ev.get_type()` after `unify_int_branch_widths`, which is int-only; a float f32-vs-f64 mismatch fell to the const-`i64 0` placeholder (same fall-through the int-width fix addressed for self-hosting #7). FIX (514ee12c): added `unify_float_branch_widths` + `fptrunc_branch_value_in_pred` (sibling of the int helpers) — fptrunc the f64 literal branch down to the sibling f32 in its predecessor before the phi. Sound: the typechecker unified both branches to one Kāra float type, so the f64 side is always the literal-default artifact (an f64-returning fn never hits the mismatch, its literals are already f64), and the truncation is value-preserving. Regression tests/codegen.rs::test_e2e_float_if_return_phi_width; full codegen suite 2138 passed 0 failed (no if/match/float regression). Surfaced by GPU-LBM-4 enabling scalar `#[gpu]` control flow (`if x>0 {x} else {0}` → WGSL `select`), whose #[gpu] fn is also codegen'd as a regular LLVM function and hit this.
tracker: src/codegen/control_flow.rs compile_if / unify_float_branch_widths; float sibling of the int-width fix (self-hosting #7)

title: `.push()` (and other Vec/String methods) unsupported on a non-identifier receiver — a nested place expr like `self.scopes[i].names.push(x)` / `o.inners[0].xs.push(v)` fails codegen
detail: A method call whose receiver is a NESTED place expression (index-then-field, `o.inners[0].xs`) falls through method dispatch: `codegen: no handler for method 'push' on non-identifier receiver (add a dispatcher arm in compile_method_call)`. `self.field.push(x)` (one-level field receiver, e.g. `Parser.loop_labels.push`) works; `self.field[i].field.push(x)` does not. LOUD error (not silent), so it fails the build rather than miscompiling. MINIMAL REPRO: `struct Inner { xs: Vec[i64] } struct Outer { inners: Vec[Inner] } fn main() { let mut o = Outer { inners: Vec.new() }; o.inners.push(Inner { xs: Vec.new() }); o.inners[0].xs.push(5); println(o.inners[0].xs.len()); }` => build error. Surfaced by the phase-12 Resolver port Slice 1 (`selfhost/src/resolver.kara`), which wanted a nested `Vec[Scope]{ names: Vec[NameBinding] }` and had to be restructured to a FLAT `binds: Vec[NameBinding]` tagged with scope id so every `.push` lands on a single `self.field` vec. FIX AREA: `compile_method_call` — the receiver-place lowering handles Identifier and (some) field receivers but not a general place expression; extend it to compute the receiver pointer via the place-chain walker (the same one field/index assignment uses) before dispatching Vec/String builtin methods.
resolution: Fixed in fc50a89. ROOT CAUSE: `lower_field_access_ptr`'s `Index` arm (src/codegen/calls.rs) required the indexed container to be a bare `Identifier`; a FieldAccess container (`o.inners` in `o.inners[i].xs.push`) returned `Ok(None)`, so the receiver-pointer resolution fell through to the non-identifier-receiver dispatch error. FIX: extend the `Index` arm to hoist a FieldAccess container to a synthetic Vec identifier before indexing — resolve the field to its storage pointer + declared element registries (recursively, so the base may itself be a place chain), register a synth binding via `register_var_from_type_expr`, index that, then tear the synth down via the new shared `unregister_synth_container` helper. Sibling of the B-2026-07-09-1 FieldAccess-container hoist in `compile_indexed_receiver_method`. The field pointer aliases the parent storage so the mutation writes back through the whole chain (verified by read-back). Works for plain- and shared-struct elements and a `mut ref self` root, and generalizes to deeper index+field chains (`o.a[i].b[j].c.push`); pure double-index `a[i][j].method` stays rejected (MR5/FR5, a distinct path). Full codegen (2144) + selfhost oracles green; regression tests `codegen::test_e2e_nested_receiver_push_index_then_field`, `codegen::test_e2e_nested_receiver_push_shared_struct_element`, and ASAN/LSan `memory_sanitizer::asan_nested_receiver_push_string_field_no_leak`. The resolver's flat-`binds` workaround can now be replaced with the natural nested `Vec[Scope]{ names: Vec[NameBinding] }` if desired.

title: SILENT: `match ref_struct.field { Some(g) => ... }` on an Option/enum FIELD of a `ref`-bound struct binds the payload as an EMPTY/zeroed shallow copy — its Vec/heap fields read empty
detail: Matching an Option (or enum) payload OUT OF A FIELD of a `ref`-bound struct (`fn f(h: ref Holder) { match h.w { Some(g) => for x in g.items {..} } }`) binds `g` as a zeroed/shallow copy: `g.items` (a `Vec` field) reads LENGTH 0 even when the source has elements. SILENT wrong result (no error) — the dangerous kind. DISCRIMINATOR: matching a `ref Option[T]` PARAM directly (`fn f(w: ref Option[Wrap]) { match w { Some(g) => .. } }`) is CORRECT; the bug is specific to a FIELD-of-a-ref scrutinee (`h.w`). REPRO A (BUG, prints 0, want 3): `struct Wrap { items: Vec[i64] } struct Holder { w: Option[Wrap] } fn count(h: ref Holder) -> i64 { let mut c = 0; match h.w { Some(g) => { for x in g.items { c = c + 1; } } None => {} } c } fn main() { let mut items: Vec[i64] = Vec.new(); items.push(1); items.push(2); items.push(3); let h = Holder { w: Some(Wrap{items:items}) }; println(count(h)); }`. REPRO B (CLEAN, prints 3): same but `count(w: ref Option[Wrap])` matching the param directly. Surfaced by the phase-12 Resolver Slice 1: `match f.generics { Some(g) => for p in g.params {..} }` over `f: ref FnDefNode` silently skipped every generic param (T undefined, no dup). WORKAROUND used in resolver.kara: walk the whole AST BY VALUE and destructure (the ast_render idiom) so the scrutinee is an owned value, never a field-of-ref. FIX AREA: the match-scrutinee lowering for a field-access place through a `ref` — the payload extraction (`bind_pattern_values` / `reconstruct_payload_value`) reads the field's payload words from a wrong/zeroed base when the scrutinee root is a borrow + field-access; likely the same place-chain-through-ref base-pointer gap as B-2026-07-11-11. Because it is SILENT it can miscompile arbitrary user code, not just selfhost — high severity despite low current blast radius.
resolution: Two independent gaps, both fixed in af0cc9d. ROOT CAUSE (not the base-pointer gap hypothesised in FIX AREA): (1) `typechecker/fields.rs infer_field_access` returned `Type::Error` for a field read through a `ref`/`mut ref` STRUCT — only unions were peeled; the struct-through-ref path was deliberately dark (`self`-receivers dodged it by being typed as the bare value, so only `ref`/`mut ref` PARAMS hit it). With the scrutinee typed Error, the `Some(g)` payload binding never recorded its surface type, so codegen's `pattern_payload_word_count` fell to the 1-word default and truncated the 3-word `Wrap` (Vec) to its data pointer — `g.items` read len 0. FIX: peel the borrow for any `Named`/`Shared` inner and resolve the field's declared by-value type (generic-arg substitution was already borrow-aware via `field_type_with_receiver_args`). (2) Once sized correctly, the value-path payload binding aliases the borrowed buffer but got an owned scope-exit drop -> double-free against the caller's storage. FIX: `control_flow_match.rs scrutinee_is_readonly_borrowed_place` classifies a field/element read rooted at a `ref`/for-borrow/borrow-accessor binding as a borrow (drop suppressed) ONLY when no arm moves a payload out — escaping payloads (`match self.toks[i].tok { Id(s) => s }`) stay on the owned move-out path, which the borrow clone-on-escape net does not cover for user enums. Full codegen (2138) + memory_sanitizer (593, ASAN/LSan) + all 4 selfhost oracles green; regression test `codegen::match_scrutinee_field_of_ref_struct_payload_binding` covers both the non-escaping (prints 3) and escaping (prints hello) shapes. B-2026-07-11-11 (nested-receiver `.push()` on `a.b[i].c`) is a DISTINCT method-dispatch gap, still open — this fix surfaces it (`o.inners[0].xs.push(5)` now type-resolves but hits 'no handler for method push on non-identifier receiver').

title: `String.chars()` random-access/length ergonomics (the gap-1 half of B-2026-07-11-9, which was marked fixed for gap 2 — the rc-fallback — only). Materialization and random access already worked by this point: `s.chars().collect()` yields a `Vec[char]` (codegen materializes chars eagerly to a `Vec[char]`, B-2026-06-18-1/-5) with native `.len()` and `[i]` indexing. The remaining holes were the iterator-LENGTH conveniences: `s.chars().count()` TYPECHECKED but FAILED codegen with 'no handler for method count on non-identifier receiver' (the `count` terminal had a typechecker arm but no codegen arm for a method-chain receiver), and `s.chars().len()` was REJECTED at typecheck with 'no method len on type Iterator' (only `count` was a recognized terminal) — even though codegen's len/is_empty method-chain intercept would have serviced it. FIX (B-2026-07-11-13): (1) codegen — add `count` to the len/is_empty method-chain intercept in `src/codegen/method_call.rs` (both the Vec-struct and slice-header receiver arms), so `<chars-materialized Vec>.count()` extracts the Vec's `len` field (count == len for the eager snapshot); (2) typechecker — accept `len` as an alias for the `count` terminal on `Iterator` (`src/typechecker/stdlib_iter.rs`), both returning i64; (3) interpreter — alias `len` to `count` in the iterator terminal dispatch (`src/interpreter/method_call_iter.rs`, drain-and-count). All three phases now agree: `s.chars().count()` and `s.chars().len()` return the char count under `karac check`/`build`/`run`, empty string → 0, and `v.iter().count()` on a plain Vec is unaffected. Verified E2E (codegen build+run and interpreter both print 5/5/0). No hand-rolled `Vec[char]` materialization loop is needed for random-access char parsing anymore. Requested by the owner; found via the B-2026-07-11-9 JSON dogfood.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: B-2026-07-11-9 gap 1 (JSON dogfood: random-access char parsing); closes the chars-ergonomics remainder that stayed unfixed when B-2026-07-11-9 was marked fixed for gap 2 only

title: LEAK: a user method on a FRESH-TEMP shared-struct receiver (`make().count()`) leaks the RC box + heap fields under LSan — a regression on `main`, the pinned test `memory_sanitizer::asan_freshtemp_shared_struct_method_no_double_free` fails (288 bytes / 3 allocations)
detail: `tests/memory_sanitizer.rs::asan_freshtemp_shared_struct_method_no_double_free` FAILS under Linux LSan: `make().count()` in a loop (where `make() -> Bag`, `shared struct Bag { items: Vec[String] }`, `count(self) -> i64`) leaks 288 bytes / 3 allocations (the RC box + the two Vec[String] field buffers). The fresh-temp materializes into `__urecv_tmp` and is meant to be drop-tracked as ONE scope-exit RcDec (`track_rc_var`) that drives rc->0 and frees the box + fields — but that dec is NOT firing (or the temp isn't tracked), so the box leaks each iteration. REGRESSION, not new: BISECTED to the origin/main range 21a9e8c..2877a73 (fails at 2877a73, i.e. BEFORE any of this session's B-2026-07-11-11/-12 work — confirmed by checking out 2877a73 clean and reproducing). Prime suspect: `687df6c fix(ownership): don't RC-fallback an accumulator moved out via a terminal return (B-2026-07-11-9 gap 2)` — an RC-fallback change that plausibly dropped the fresh-temp shared-receiver's RcDec tracking; needs confirmation by reverting/bisecting that commit against this test. IMPACT: the Linux-CI `memory-sanitizer` gate is RED on current `main` (cd2f6b7+). REPRO: run `cargo test --features llvm --test memory_sanitizer asan_freshtemp_shared_struct_method_no_double_free`. Not caused by and orthogonal to the nested-receiver / field-access-through-ref fixes filed same day; filed on discovery per the never-route-around-it rule while fixing B-2026-07-11-11.
resolution: Fixed in fbf97df. ROOT CAUSE (bisected to 2877a73 'String.chars().count()/.len() ergonomics', NOT the suspected ownership commit 687df6c — that one passes): 2877a73 added `count` to the non-identifier-receiver `len`/`is_empty` method-chain intercept in `src/codegen/method_call.rs`. That intercept speculatively `compile_expr(object)`s the receiver, then services it only when the value is a Vec/String/slice struct. For a `make().count()` receiver whose result is a user struct/enum (here the `shared struct Bag` with a user `fn count(self)`), the value is a handle/pointer — neither a Vec struct nor a slice header — so the intercept fell through WITHOUT freeing the just-materialized temp, and the real user-method dispatch re-evaluated `object`, leaking the discarded RC box + its heap fields (288 B / 3 allocs over the 3-iteration loop). Latent for `len`/`is_empty` since the intercept was first added; `count` newly collided with a common user method name. FIX: gate the intercept on the receiver's type NOT declaring its own `len`/`is_empty`/`count` method — when `dispatch_key` names an emitted `<Type>.<method>` fn (or a generic one), defer to user-method dispatch instead of speculatively compiling the receiver. Iterator/collection chains (`s.chars().count()`, `make_vec().len()`) declare no such fn, so they still take the intercept (the B-2026-07-11-9 feature is unchanged: chars count/len still 5/5/0). Bonus: a user `make().len()` now returns the user method's value instead of a mis-read collection length. Full codegen (2145) + memory_sanitizer (594, ASAN/LSan) green; regression `codegen::e2e_user_len_family_method_on_freshtemp_dispatches_to_user` locks the dispatch value and the pinned ASAN gate `asan_freshtemp_shared_struct_method_no_double_free` now passes.

title: LEAK: `with_capacity(n)` with a runtime `n == 0` orphaned a 1-byte heap buffer. `karac_alloc_or_panic(0)` deliberately normalizes `0 -> 1` and returns a real, non-null buffer (a non-null result is its success signal, alloc.rs), but the zero-capacity constructor stamped `cap = 0` into the collection aggregate `{data, len=0, cap=0}`. The load-bearing `cap > 0 <=> owned heap` drop convention (clone_drop.rs: String SSO / static-literal rodata views / borrowed slices all use `cap == 0` to mean DO-NOT-FREE) then SKIPPED freeing that non-null buffer at scope exit -> a 1-byte leak per construction. Latent for any explicit `Vec.with_capacity(0)` / `String.with_capacity(0)`, but the presize.rs pass (phase-7-codegen 7.3 lever #1) makes it COMMON: it rewrites `let mut v = Vec.new(); while i < k { v.push(..) }` to `Vec.with_capacity(k)`, so any counted-fill loop whose bound evaluates to 0 at runtime (the VM's `run(prog, 0)` with no local slots) leaked once per call. LeakSanitizer on Linux CI (memory-sanitizer job) is the authoritative gate; a local macOS asan run misses it (no LSan). FIX (B-2026-07-11-15): in src/codegen/assoc_call.rs, guard the buffer allocation for all zero-capacity constructors so a zero byte-count yields a NULL data pointer with no malloc, making `with_capacity(0)` bit-identical to `Vec.new()` (`{null, 0, 0}`) — the drop then no-ops and the first push grows from null (`realloc(null, _) == malloc`). New helper `with_capacity_buffer_or_null` handles the panicking `Vec`/`VecDeque`/`String.with_capacity`; new helper `fallible_with_capacity_buffer` handles `try_with_capacity`, where the zero case must resolve to `Result.Ok({null,0,0})` and NOT a spurious `Err(OutOfMemory)` (a null buffer is only OOM when an allocation was actually attempted). For a compile-time-constant nonzero capacity LLVM folds the `== 0` test away, so the common `with_capacity(<literal>)` keeps its single unconditional allocation. Verified ASAN/LSan-clean: the VM example, the narrowed presize repro, and a dedicated regression exercising all three constructors at zero cap plus the nonzero grow-after path. Found via the vm.kara dogfood (feedback_katas_are_bug_finders).
detail: SOURCE NOTE: vm.kara dogfood (stack-based bytecode VM): `run(prog_arith(), 0)` — a program run with zero local slots — leaked one byte per call under LeakSanitizer. Narrowed to `let mut v = Vec.new(); while i < n { v.push(..) }` with a runtime `n == 0`.

title: Module-level `let` binding with a COMPUTED / cross-referencing initializer (e.g. `let DOUBLED: i64 = COUNT * 2;` referencing another module binding, or any non-literal/non-composite RHS) is not emitted by codegen: `module_binding_init` (src/codegen/module_bindings.rs) returns None for an Identifier/BinaryOp RHS, so the binding is silently skipped and a later read fails with `codegen: Undefined variable 'DOUBLED'`. Only literal + composite (Tuple/Array/Repeat/Struct/enum-unit) initializers are handled today (the module_binding_init doc explicitly defers computed shapes to 'slice 10 or a future widening'). The INTERPRETER now evaluates these correctly (B-fixed 2026-07-11: register_items ModuleBinding arm), so run succeeds (prints 84) while build errors — a LOUD run-vs-build divergence (build refuses to compile; not a silent miscompile). FIX DIRECTION: const-fold a module-binding initializer that references already-declared module globals — evaluate the RHS against the const values of prior bindings (a small const-evaluator over the module-binding dependency order), OR route computed initializers through the existing `finalize_module_binding_static_init` runtime static-init pass. Surfaced while closing the module-level-let interpreter run-parity gap; the literal + composite + `let mut`-reassignment surface now has full run==build parity.
fix: this commit — computed module-binding initializers routed through __karac_static_init (declare zero placeholder global + compile_expr the initializer in the prologue, storing before main). Annotated computed/cross-referencing inits (let DOUBLED: i64 = COUNT * 2) now run==build. Follow-up (same day): UN-annotated computed inits (let DOUBLED = COUNT * 2) also closed — lowering threads the typechecker's inferred value-expr type into a new Program.module_binding_types side-table (keyed by binding name), and declare_module_bindings sizes the placeholder global from it when there is no `: TYPE`. The typechecker stays the single source of truth for the type (codegen never re-infers). Both i64 chains and an i32 binding are covered by test_e2e_modbind_computed_unannotated_initializer + interpreter parity. Module-binding run==build parity is now COMPLETE (literal, composite, let mut, annotated-computed, un-annotated-computed).

title: `fold(init, |acc, x| body)` on a fused iterator chain had no codegen terminal. The sequential iterator engine in `src/codegen/method_call.rs` (`try_compile_iter_adaptor_collect_to_vec`) only supports `collect` as a terminal; a chain ending in `fold` (`v.iter().map(f).filter(p).fold(0, |a,x| a+x)`) fell through the whole dispatcher to the loud 'no handler for method \'fold\' on non-identifier receiver' error, so ANY `fold` on an iterator chain failed `karac build` and the default JIT `karac run` (the interpreter handled it — a run-vs-build divergence). FIX (B-2026-07-11-17): new `try_compile_iter_chain_fold`, wired into `compile_method_call` next to the `collect` entry, gated on an iterator-chain receiver (a MethodCall or Range — `Column`/`Tensor.fold` on a variable receiver is intercepted earlier by `try_compile_column_method`, so it never reaches here). It reuses the collect desugar's map/filter element-threading (bind-or-elide when the current element already IS the stage param) but emits an ACCUMULATE sink instead of a `push`: it peels the map/filter adaptors down to a base source the `for`-loop already iterates correctly (`X.iter()`/`iter_mut`/`into_iter`/`chars`/`bytes`/`keys`/`values`, or a range) and builds `{ let mut __facc = init; for <elem> in <base> { <filter as if, map as let-rebind>; let <acc_p> = __facc; __facc = <fold_body> }; __facc }`, compiled via `compile_expr`. Materializing no intermediate Vec sidesteps the fused chain's element-type recovery problem (codegen has no lowering-derived side-table entry for a SYNTHETIC `collect`). Fails CLOSED (Ok(None) -> the loud dispatch error, never a silent wrong answer) for any shape it can't lower: a non-map/filter adaptor in the chain (enumerate/take/zip/scan), a non-single-Binding closure, or a base that is itself an unrecognized adaptor MethodCall. Verified interp==JIT==native across bare-iter/map/filter/filter+map/if-body-max/nonzero-init/empty-source/range folds, and ASAN/LSan-clean over heap-String-field records. Found via the pipeline.kara dogfood (feedback_katas_are_bug_finders). The broader iterator-terminal gaps this dogfood also surfaced (for-over-chain silent miscompile; sum/reduce/for_each/any/all) are B-2026-07-11-18 and B-2026-07-11-19.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: pipeline.kara dogfood (functional log-analytics pipeline): every aggregate query (`iter().filter(..).map(..).fold(init, |acc,x| ..)`) failed `karac build`/JIT while the interpreter ran fine.

title: SILENT MISCOMPILE: `for x in <iter-chain-with-map/filter>` iterates ZERO times in codegen (interpreter iterates correctly) — wrong answer, no error.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: Found while building the pipeline.kara dogfood + fixing B-2026-07-11-17 (fold): probing `for x in <iter-chain>` shapes. — `for x in v.iter().map(|x| x*10) { s = s + x }` and `for x in v.iter().filter(|x| x>2) { .. }` run the loop body ZERO times under `karac build` / the default JIT `karac run`, silently producing the pre-loop state (e.g. sum stays 0), while the tree-walk interpreter iterates correctly. No diagnostic. `compile_for` (src/codegen/control_flow_for.rs) has explicit peel arms for `.iter()`/`.into_iter()`/`.chars()`/`.bytes()`/`.enumerate()` and ranges — each added to fix a PAST silent-miscompile of the same shape (the arm comments cite chars, bytes, indexed-Vec[String]) — but a `.map(..)`/`.filter(..)` adaptor iterable has NO arm and falls through to the dispatcher's silent `_ =>` arm, so the body never runs. This is the dangerous class (silent wrong result). WORKS: bare `for x in v.iter()`, `for x in v` by-value, `for (i,x) in v.iter().enumerate()`, and the MATERIALIZED form `for x in v.iter().map(..).collect()` (routing through the working `collect` engine). REPRO (prints 0, want 100): `fn main(){ let v: Vec[i64] = [1,2,3,4]; let mut s = 0; for x in v.iter().map(|x| x*10) { s = s + x; } println(f"{s}"); }`. SUGGESTED FIX: add `compile_for` arm(s) that route a map/filter (fusible-adaptor) iterable through the same fused desugar the collect engine uses, with the loop body as the sink — the same generalization B-2026-07-11-17's fold terminal wants (both need 'fused chain with a custom per-element sink'; a shared, sink-parameterized fusion engine would fix both and subsume the fold desugar). Filed on discovery per the never-route-around-it rule; the pipeline.kara dogfood avoids the shape (uses `.collect()` then `for p in slow`).
resolution:
Fixed. `compile_for` (src/codegen/control_flow_for.rs) now routes a `map`/`filter` adaptor iterable through the SAME map/filter fusion as the fold terminal (B-2026-07-11-17), with the USER'S loop body as the per-element sink. The fold fix's front half was extracted into two shared helpers in src/codegen/method_call.rs: `peel_fused_map_filter_chain` (peels map/filter down to a for-iterable base source, validating it — fail-closed on any other shape) and `build_fused_chain_body` (threads the element through the adaptors — `if ` for filter, `let

= ` for map, with bind-or-elide — ending in a caller-supplied sink closure). `try_compile_for_iter_chain` uses both with a sink that binds the user pattern to the adapted element and inlines the user body, emitting `for in { ; let = ; }` compiled via compile_expr. The user body inlines into the base for-loop, so `break`/`continue`/labels target it correctly. Gated in compile_for on the outermost method being `map`/`filter` (empty-adaptor / bare-source iterables keep their existing arms). Verified interp == JIT across map / filter / filter+map / struct-element / nested / break / continue, and ASAN/LSan-clean over Vec[String] map/filter chains. Full codegen (2152) + memory_sanitizer (598) green; regressions test_e2e_for_over_iter_chain + asan_for_over_iter_chain_heap_elems_no_leak. This is the sink-parameterized fusion generalization proposed in the original filing; it subsumes the fold desugar (both now share peel + build_fused_chain_body).

title: FIXED (last gap c964b29). Rollup of the sequential-iterator terminal/adaptor codegen+typecheck gaps the pipeline.kara dogfood surfaced. All tracked sub-items now build == run (interp == JIT == AOT): sum / reduce / for_each (typecheck+interp+codegen), any / all codegen terminals, `|_|` wildcard closure params in a chain, `let it = v.iter()` materialized-iter-let codegen, and `reduce` codegen (was deferred) — these landed across earlier slices. The LAST gap, `count()` as a fused-chain terminal (`v.iter().count()` / `.filter(...).count()` / `.map(...).count()` failed under codegen — the receiver was caught by the materialized-collection `len`/`count` intercept which tried to compile the chain as a Vec and fell over on the `map`/`filter` adaptor, while the interpreter ran it), is fixed in c964b29: an iterator-chain `count` arm before that intercept desugars to `fold(0, |acc, _| acc + 1)` via the shared peel, failing closed so `s.chars().count()` still uses the intercept. Verified across bare/filter/map/filter+map chains, empty source, `range().count`, and `chars().count()`; valgrind-clean. Test: `test_e2e_iter_chain_count_terminal`. (Out of this rollup's scope: other terminals — `min`/`max`/`product`/`find`/`position`/`nth`/`last` — are separate future work, not tracked here.)
detail: SOURCE NOTE: Surfaced while building pipeline.kara + fixing fold (B-2026-07-11-17): probing the sequential iterator terminal/adaptor support matrix. — A tracking rollup of the remaining sequential-iterator gaps the pipeline.kara dogfood surfaced (fold itself is fixed in B-2026-07-11-17; the for-over-chain silent miscompile is B-2026-07-11-18). Each is independently fixable; grouped here to avoid scattering one-line entries. (1) TYPECHECK rejects `v.iter().sum()`, `.reduce(|a,x| ..)`, `.for_each(|x| ..)` with 'no method X on type Iterator' — not in the accepted terminal set in src/typechecker/stdlib_iter.rs (which DOES list all/any/collect/count/fold/map/filter/…). (2) `v.iter().any(|x| x>3)` / `.all(|x| x>0)` TYPECHECK but hit the loud codegen 'no handler for method any/all on non-identifier receiver' — no codegen terminal (interpreter runs them). (3) A `|_|` wildcard closure param in a chain (`v.iter().map(|_| 7).collect()`) makes the fused-chain codegen bail, surfacing as 'no handler for method collect on non-identifier receiver' — a named param works. (4) `let it = v.iter(); it.fold(..)` fails codegen with 'Vec/String method iter is not yet supported in codegen' — `iter` only works FUSED into a chain, not materialized to a `Value::Iterator` variable (interpreter supports it). All four are codegen/typecheck completeness gaps, not miscompiles (loud failures except none are silent). Most naturally fixed alongside the sink-parameterized fusion engine proposed in B-2026-07-11-18: `sum`=fold(+), `reduce`=fold-first, `for_each`/`any`/`all` are sink variants. `count` on a chain already works via the len/is_empty/count intercept.
progress: any/all FIXED (this thread, 71a34fa): the short-circuit boolean terminals now have codegen terminals (src/codegen/method_call.rs `try_compile_iter_chain_any_all`), reusing the shared map/filter fusion (peel_fused_map_filter_chain + build_fused_chain_body, B-2026-07-11-17/-18) with a short-circuit sink (result seeded false/true, flipped + `break` on the deciding element). Typecheck + interpreter already accepted them, so this was codegen-only. Verified interp==JIT across any/all true/false, empty-source edges (any->false, all->true), adapters-before-terminal (filter+any, map+all), heap-String elements, and ranges; ASAN-clean over a map->heap-String chain that short-circuits mid-stream. Tests: codegen::test_e2e_iter_chain_any_all_terminal, memory_sanitizer::asan_iter_chain_any_all_short_circuit_no_leak. STILL OPEN: (a) sum/reduce/for_each rejected at typecheck (not in the Iterator method set in src/typechecker/stdlib_iter.rs) AND unsupported in the interpreter (method_call_iter.rs only has fold/any/all/count/collect) — each needs a 3-phase add (typecheck + interpreter + a codegen sink: sum=fold(+), for_each=for-loop, reduce=fold with Option result); (b) `|_|` wildcard closure param makes the fused-chain codegen bail; (c) `let it = v.iter(); it.fold(..)` (iter materialized to a Value::Iterator variable) unsupported in codegen. || `|_|` WILDCARD PARAMS FIXED (bd709ac): the collect/fold/any/all fused-chain codegen required a `PatternKind::Binding` and bailed on a `_` param (`map(|_| 7).collect()` -> loud 'no handler'; the interpreter already accepted it — a run-vs-build divergence). Codegen now binds a `_` to a fresh throwaway name in both the map/filter ADAPTERS (try_compile_iter_adaptor_collect_to_vec + peel_fused_map_filter_chain) and the TERMINAL closures (shared `closure_param_name` helper — covers `fold(0, |a, _| a + 1)` count, `any(|_| ..)`). Verified interp==JIT across adapter + terminal wildcards; test codegen::test_e2e_iter_chain_wildcard_closure_param. || `for_each` RECLASSIFIED: not merely a 3-phase add — its natural use `for_each(|x| acc = acc + x)` is exactly the capture-MUTATING shape that diverges under the unimplemented `mut ref` closure capture (B-2026-07-11-23). Deferred to that fix. || STILL OPEN: sum/reduce (typecheck+interp+codegen; sum needs a typed zero from the element type, reduce an Option result seeded by the first element), and `let it = v.iter(); it.fold(..)` (iter materialized to a Value::Iterator variable) in codegen. || `sum` FIXED (this thread): the numeric `sum()` terminal now lands across all three surfaces. TYPECHECK (src/typechecker/stdlib_iter.rs `"sum"` arm) accepts it, validates a numeric element (is_numeric || type_param_has_numeric_bound; a String element is rejected with 'requires a numeric element type'), records the yielded element TypeExpr span-keyed in a new `iter_terminal_elem_types` side-table (typechecker -> ast::Program -> codegen, wired through lowering.rs like `temp_recv_elem_types`), and returns the element type. INTERPRETER (method_call_iter.rs `"sum"` arm) drains the iterator, adding each element to an accumulator seeded from the first (empty -> Int(0)). CODEGEN (src/codegen/method_call.rs `try_compile_iter_chain_sum`) desugars to the fold engine with a synthesized `(0 as <elem>)` cast init (a width-correct zero for every numeric type incl. isize/usize/f32/f64 without an IntSuffix spelling) and an `acc + x` body, reusing the shared map/filter fusion; fails closed (Ok(None) -> loud dispatch error) when the element type wasn't recorded. Verified interp==JIT==AOT across iter().sum, map().sum, filter().sum, filter().map().sum, f64 sum (zero must be 0.0), empty (0), and range sum. Tests: codegen::test_e2e_iter_chain_sum_terminal, interpreter::test_iter_sum_terminal, typechecker::test_iter_sum_rejects_non_numeric_element. STILL OPEN: `reduce` (Option result seeded by the first element; the general-element case needs a non-numeric-safe accumulator seed, unlike sum's typed zero) and `let it = v.iter(); it.fold(..)` (iter materialized to a Value::Iterator variable) in codegen. || `reduce` LANDED interp-first (this thread): TYPECHECK (stdlib_iter.rs `"reduce"` arm) accepts `reduce(f: Fn(A,A)->A) -> Option[A]` (was rejected as 'no method reduce'), records the element TypeExpr in `iter_terminal_elem_types`. INTERPRETER (method_call_iter.rs `"reduce"` arm) folds with the first element as the seed, returns Some(acc) / None (empty). Verified under `karac run`: sum-reduce 10, max-reduce 4, empty None, map().reduce 20. CODEGEN is INTENTIONALLY DEFERRED with a loud, actionable error (method_call.rs: '`Iterator.reduce()` is not yet supported under karac build … re-run with --interp, or use .fold(init, f)') rather than the generic no-handler fall-through: its `Option[A]` result would need a synthetic accumulator + per-element match/Some/None whose Option layout depends on typechecker-supplied payload sizing the fused desugar can't rederive without a typecheck pass on the synthetic nodes (unlike `sum`, whose desugar is pure arithmetic). No silent wrong answer. Tests: interpreter::test_iter_reduce_terminal, typechecker::test_iter_reduce_accepts_and_yields_option. STILL OPEN: `reduce` CODEGEN (needs an Option-layout-aware terminal or a typecheck pass over synthetic desugar nodes), and `let it = v.iter(); it.fold(..)` (iter materialized to a Value::Iterator variable) in codegen. || `for_each` LANDED across all three surfaces (this thread, now unblocked by the B-2026-07-11-23 mut-ref capture fix): TYPECHECK (stdlib_iter.rs `"for_each"` arm) accepts `for_each(f: Fn(T) -> ()) -> ()` (param seeded from T, return inferred freely like `map`, result discarded). INTERPRETER (method_call_iter.rs `"for_each"` arm) drains the iterator invoking `f` per element for side effects, returns unit; a capture-mutating body now propagates via the Rule 2 shared-cell capture. CODEGEN (method_call.rs `try_compile_iter_chain_for_each`) desugars to a `for` loop over the peeled base with the closure body INLINED as the loop body (reusing peel_fused_map_filter_chain + build_fused_chain_body), yielding unit — the body inlines so capture-mutation propagates and no closure value is built (the stored-mut-ref-closure refusal never applies). Verified interp==JIT==AOT across bare for_each (capture-accumulate 10), map().for_each (30), filter().for_each (6), and range for_each (10). Gates: fmt, clippy, non-llvm, codegen (2198) green. Tests: interpreter::test_iter_for_each_terminal, codegen::test_e2e_iter_chain_for_each_terminal. STILL OPEN on B-19: `reduce` CODEGEN and materialized `let it = v.iter(); it.fold(..)` in codegen. || `reduce` CODEGEN landed for SCALAR elements (this thread): `try_compile_iter_chain_reduce` (src/codegen/method_call.rs) desugars a scalar `reduce(|a,x| body)` to an `Option[A]` accumulator seeded `None`, folded per element via a synthetic `match __racc { None => Some(x), Some(a) => Some(body) }` — the type-erased 4-word Option layout lets the synthetic `Some(...)`/`None` construction (coerce_to_payload_words) and the tag-dispatched match (a bare `None` binding is recognized as a unit variant by tag) compile with NO typecheck pass over the nodes; the `Option[A]` accumulator annotation supplies A for the `Some(acc)` payload binding. Two AST-shape gotchas resolved empirically: the `Some` ctor callee must be a bare `Identifier` (a `Path` form miscompiled to all-None), and the element must be trivially-copyable. HEAP-element reduce (String/Vec/struct) is GATED OUT (`is_trivially_copyable_te`) — its synthetic `Some(acc) => Some(f(acc,x))` double-frees the payload (extracted acc consumed by f AND the old accumulator dropped); it falls through to the loud `--interp` deferral (interpreter runs it correctly). Verified interp==JIT==AOT for scalar reduce (sum 10, max 4, empty None, map().reduce 20, filter().reduce 9); heap reduce interp a-b-c / build loud-defers (no crash, no silent wrong). Gates: fmt, clippy, non-llvm, codegen (2202) green. Test: codegen::test_e2e_iter_chain_reduce_scalar_terminal. STILL OPEN on B-19: heap-element `reduce` codegen (payload rc-accounting in the synthetic match) and materialized `let it = v.iter(); it.fold(..)` in codegen. || MATERIALIZED-ITERATOR bindings LANDED (this thread): `let it = v.iter(); it.<terminal|adaptor>(..)` / `for x in it` now compile. Codegen has no runtime iterator value, so a `let it = <chain>` whose RHS is a fusable `.iter()/.iter_mut()/.into_iter()` chain is NOT codegen'd — it records the (recursively-inlined) chain expr (`iter_let_bindings`, src/codegen.rs) and skips (src/codegen/stmts.rs Let arm). Each use then inlines the chain via `substitute_iter_let_receiver` — at method calls (`compile_method_call` top: `it.fold(..)` -> `v.iter().fold(..)`) and at for-loops (`compile_for` top: `for x in it` -> `for x in v.iter()`), so the existing fused terminals/adaptors/for-paths handle them. Chained lets compose (`let it5 = it4.filter(g)` records `v.iter().filter(g)`). SOUND GATE: intercept only when the RHS is typechecker-typed `Iterator` (new `iterator_typed_exprs` span-set: typechecker expr_types -> ast::Program -> codegen via lowering.rs, sibling of `string_typed_exprs`) AND the peeled base is a genuine iter method — this is what stops a collection-returning `.iter()` (`Column.iter() -> Vec[Option[T]]`, the eager `chars()`/`bytes()` materializations, bare ranges) from being mis-inlined (two such regressions in the syntactic-only draft: `Column.iter()` then `all.len()`, and `s.bytes()` then `b[0]` — both fixed by the type gate). Unsupported uses (stateful `it.next()`, materialized-range terminal, passing `it` to a fn) fail closed (loud `--interp`), never silent-wrong. Verified interp==JIT==AOT: fold/sum/for_each over a materialized iter, adaptor-in-let, chained filter-let, for-over-materialized-iter; `Column.iter()`+len and `bytes()`+index compile unchanged. Gates: fmt, clippy, non-llvm, codegen (2205) green. Tests: codegen::{test_e2e_materialized_iterator_binding, test_e2e_collection_returning_iter_not_mis_materialized}. STILL OPEN on B-19: heap-element `reduce` codegen (payload rc-accounting in the synthetic match) — the last leg; scalar reduce, sum, for_each, and materialized iterators all land.

fix: gpu_wgsl::reachable_helpers: add Index/MethodCall/Cast arms to calls_in and a StmtKind::Let arm to calls_in_block so #[gpu] helper calls in those AST positions are gathered into the reachable-helper set.
title: GPU helper-call gathering (reachable_helpers, GPU-LBM-5) misses #[gpu] helper calls inside Index / let-RHS / MethodCall / Cast positions, so a valid GPU kernel calling a helper there fails codegen with a misleading 'unsupported call in a GPU kernel body' error.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: Surfaced building the GPU-SLIP-2c f32 LBM `stream` kernel on Metal: `let c = coll[g_idx(x,y,w)]` and `coll[g_idx(x-1,y,w)].f1` place the `g_idx` #[gpu] helper call inside an Index expression (and a let RHS). — reachable_helpers walks a #[gpu] kernel/helper body to gather the transitively-reachable helpers to emit as WGSL fns; its calls_in only traversed Call/Binary/Unary/If/Block/StructLiteral/FieldAccess, and calls_in_block only visited StmtKind::Expr statements. So a helper call sitting in an Index (`buf[idx(...)]`), a let-binding RHS (`let c = buf[idx(...)]`), a method receiver/args, or a cast operand was never collected, and lower_call then rejected it with 'unsupported call ... only arithmetic/comparison operators and #[gpu] helper functions are supported' even though the helper existed. Latent since GPU-LBM-5 (helpers) — prior helper-using kernels only called helpers in struct-field-init and if-condition positions, which were covered. The LBM stream kernel is the first to index a buffer by a helper result. Fix adds the missing Index/MethodCall/Cast traversal arms and the StmtKind::Let arm. Regression test: gpu_wgsl::gathers_helper_in_index_and_let_rhs. Not a miscompile (loud codegen error), so no wrong-output risk; a completeness gap that blocked a valid kernel.

title: SILENT: reusing an owned `Option[shared struct]` value across two by-value consuming calls whose callee CLONES the matched subtree double-frees under codegen (JIT+AOT) — heap corruption, no diagnostic; interpreter correct
detail: Passing the SAME owned `Option[shared struct]` binding by value to a recursive consumer TWICE, where the consumer pattern-matches the payload and CONSTRUCTS new nodes referencing the matched subtree's fields (a deep clone), corrupts the heap under both JIT and AOT (`malloc(): unaligned tcache chunk detected` — glibc double-free/write-after-free detector). The interpreter (`karac run --interp`) produces the CORRECT result, so it is a run/build divergence. NO diagnostic is emitted — the RC-fallback pass does not detect that the reused owned handle needs an inc before the first consume, so the first call frees the underlying nodes and the second call double-frees them. MINIMAL REPRO (build crashes, interp prints `nodes: 4`): `shared struct Node { val: i64, mut left: Option[Node], mut right: Option[Node] } fn clone_offset(node: Option[Node], delta: i64) -> Option[Node] { match node { None => None, Some(n) => Some(Node { val: n.val + delta, left: clone_offset(n.left, delta), right: clone_offset(n.right, delta) }) } } fn count_nodes(node: Option[Node]) -> i64 { match node { None => 0i64, Some(n) => 1i64 + count_nodes(n.left) + count_nodes(n.right) } } fn main() { let orig = Some(Node { val: 1, left: Some(Node { val: 2, left: None, right: None }), right: None }); let c1 = clone_offset(orig, 10i64); let c2 = clone_offset(orig, 20i64); println(f"nodes: {count_nodes(c1) + count_nodes(c2)}"); }`. DISCRIMINATORS: (1) a SINGLE clone_offset(orig,..) call with no reuse is CLEAN (build == interp). (2) Reusing `orig` twice but with a READ-ONLY consumer (`count_nodes(orig); count_nodes(orig);` — matches+recurses but constructs nothing) is CLEAN. (3) The same nested-Vec BST-shape builder that SHARES matched handles directly (`left: lefts[a]` instead of `clone_offset(lefts[a],..)`) is CLEAN. So the trigger is the conjunction: reuse-after-consume of an owned Option[shared] handle AND a callee that reconstructs nodes from the matched payload. FIX AREA: the ownership/RC-fallback pass fails to flag the reused owned shared-struct binding at the first by-value call site (no N0503), so codegen emits a move (free at callee scope end) instead of an inc-then-move; the callee's match-arm drop of the owned `node` param then frees storage the caller still references for the second call. Likely interacts with the recursive-clone drop accounting (the callee both consumes `node` and returns fresh nodes). Because it is SILENT and corrupts the heap it can miscompile arbitrary user code — high severity.
source: kata:leetcode-95-unique-bst-ii (generate_trees_dp.kara, bottom-up shape-DP with value offset)
resolution: Fixed for the LOCAL binding manifestation (`let orig = Some(<shared struct literal>)`): codegen's let-binding `shared_option_info` resolution gained a case (e) that registers a fresh `Some(<shared>)` RHS into the caller-retains model (`track_rc_option_var` -> `var_option_shared_heap`), so a per-pass arg-site inc (`share_option_shared_ref_for_arg`) balances the callee's exit dec and a scope-exit dec balances the literal's rc==1. src/codegen/stmts.rs. Regression: tests/memory_sanitizer.rs::asan_fresh_some_shared_reused_across_consuming_calls_no_double_free.
