title: Reassigning a `Vec[shared]` / `Vec[Option[shared]]` local variable (`current = next`) LEAKS the shared elements of the OVERWRITTEN old Vec (x86-visible; the BFS-worklist `current = next` idiom)
detail: Overwriting a `Vec` local whose element type is a shared struct/enum (`Vec[Node]`) or `Vec[Option[shared]]` with `current = next` does NOT rc-dec the elements the OLD `current` still held before dropping it — the old buffer is freed but its per-element release is skipped, so every shared node the overwritten Vec referenced leaks (LSan/valgrind `definitely lost`, x86-64). Distinct from B-2026-07-12-29 (`work[i] = work[j]` INDEX-assign on a shared Vec element, arm64-only, fixed 63d618e): this is a WHOLE-VARIABLE reassignment and reproduces on x86. The scope-exit drop of a `Vec[shared]` correctly releases elements (a pushed-then-dropped Vec is clean); only the ASSIGNMENT-overwrite path misses the old value's element-release. DISCRIMINATOR: pushing a shared node into a `Vec[shared]` and letting it drop at scope exit is CLEAN; adding a single `current = next` overwrite leaks the element the old `current` held. MINIMAL REPRO (96 B leaked = the whole 3-node tree; interp clean): `shared struct Node { val: i64, mut left: Option[Node], mut right: Option[Node] } fn main() { let root = Some(Node { val: 1, left: Some(Node { val: 2, left: None, right: None }), right: None }); let mut current: Vec[Node] = Vec.new(); match root { None => {} Some(n) => { current.push(n); } } let mut next: Vec[Node] = Vec.new(); match current[0].left { None => {} Some(l) => { next.push(l); } } current = next; println(f"len: {current.len()}"); }`. CLEAN COUNTERPART: the same program without the `current = next` line. FIX AREA: the Assign arm's Identifier-target path (src/codegen/stmts.rs) must, when the target is a `Vec[shared]` / `Vec[Option[shared]]` local, run the old value's element-releasing drop (`karac_drop_Vec_<elem>` / the emit_option_drop_fn per-element walk that B-2026-07-11-29 wired) BEFORE storing the new Vec — the same old-value-release that a shared FIELD store already performs, applied to a Vec-of-shared variable overwrite. Same systemically-under-supported Vec-of-shared surface as B-2026-07-11-29 / B-2026-07-12-4 / -29. WORKAROUND: use a queue-free formulation (recursive DFS with a depth index; the shipped kata #102 uses DFS-with-depth + level-by-level DFS, both byte-identical across all surfaces and valgrind-clean). Surfaced by kata #102 (binary-tree level-order): the canonical BFS builds each next level and does `current = next`, leaking the whole tree once per traversal. FIXED 2026-07-14 (924cd05): the Assign identifier-target path now runs the OLD value's element-releasing walk before the store when the Vec element carries a non-trivial per-element drop. New helper emit_owned_vec_element_release_on_overwrite reconstructs the exact FreeVecBuffer cleanup action vec_elem_agg_drop_for_type_expr derives for the scope-exit path (rc-dec for a shared struct/enum; tag-guarded karac_drop_Option_<payload> for Option[shared]) and emits it immediately via emit_cleanup_action, then skips the buffer-only free. So a fixed overwrite and a scope-exit drop release a shared element identically and never twice (the moved-in source's own cleanup is cap-zeroed by the paired move-suppression). Scalar/String/plain-Vec elements need no per-element drop so the helper returns false and the cheaper buffer-only free runs unchanged. Verified interp==JIT + valgrind-clean for Vec[shared], Vec[Option[shared]], the full while-BFS level-order loop, and (no regression) scalar + String Vecs; two memory_sanitizer regressions added; codegen (2339) + memory_sanitizer (698) + non-codegen suites green; fmt+clippy clean.

title: `iter().fold(init, |acc, x| ...)` with a HEAP accumulator (`String`; a Vec accumulator hits a separate type-inference wall) double-frees the accumulator buffer on native/JIT. The idiomatic string-join fold is the headline shape. Scalar accumulators (`sum`, numeric fold) are unaffected; a 0-element fold (init returned, no iteration) is clean — the double-free is per-iteration, from the accumulator reassignment.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: Fresh dogfood find probing the iterator-chain surface — `v.iter().fold(String.from(""), |acc,x| f"{acc}-{x}")` (a string JOIN) aborted `free(): double free` on JIT/native, correct on the interpreter. — REPRO (interp `-1-2-3`; JIT/native `free(): double free detected in tcache 2`): `fn main() { let v: Vec[i64] = [1,2,3]; let j = v.iter().fold(String.from(""), |acc, x| f"{acc}-{x}"); println(j); }`. Even a single-element source double-frees; 0 elements is clean; the fold result being discarded still double-frees (so it is the per-iteration reassignment, not the final move-out). CRITICAL DISCRIMINATOR: the HAND-WRITTEN, typechecked equivalent is fully correct AND leak-clean — `let mut acc = String.from(""); for x in v.iter() { acc = f"{acc}-{x}"; } ` (self-referential) and `{ let cur = acc; acc = f"{cur}-{x}"; }` (separate bind) both match the interpreter under valgrind (definitely-lost 0). ROOT: `try_compile_iter_chain_fold` (src/codegen/method_call.rs) desugars the fold in CODEGEN — i.e. AFTER typecheck — into synthetic AST (`let mut __facc = init; for x in base { let acc = __facc; __facc = fold_body }; __facc`) that is then `compile_expr`'d. Those synthetic nodes were never individually typechecked (they all reuse the fold call span), so codegen's ownership/move analysis for the String accumulator lacks the per-node metadata the equivalent hand-written loop has: the accumulator reassignment frees the old buffer while a co-owner (the `acc` bind, or the f-string read of the accumulator) frees it too → double-free. INVESTIGATED — three desugaring restructures all FAILED to fix it, proving the root is the missing metadata, not the statement shape: (a) flat `let acc = __facc; __facc = fold_body` → double-free; (b) nested `__facc = { let acc = __facc; fold_body }` → the double-free becomes an INTERMEDIATE-accumulator LEAK (the middle B_1..B_{n-1} buffers, ~n-1 leaked per fold); (c) self-referential `__facc = fold_body` with the closure's `acc` param used directly as the accumulator var (verified clean HAND-WRITTEN) → still double-frees when synthesized. FIX DIRECTION (not a quick tweak): lower `fold`/`sum`/the fused-iterator terminals BEFORE typecheck (a pre-typecheck desugar or `src/lowering.rs` restructuring that runs early enough) so the synthetic accumulator nodes are typechecked and carry correct String/move metadata — the only way the ownership analysis matches the hand-written loop. Alternatively thread explicit type/move metadata onto the synthesized nodes. WORKAROUND for users today: hand-write the accumulator loop (`let mut acc = ...; for x in <iter> { acc = ... }`) — it compiles correctly. Scalar-accumulator folds (`sum`, numeric fold) are unaffected and stay on the fused path. FIXED 2026-07-14 (763e244): typechecker records the fold accumulator TypeExpr span-keyed (iter_terminal_acc_types), threaded through lowering to codegen; the synthetic accumulator `let` is stamped with that annotation so a heap accumulator registers as a tracked String/Vec, and the desugar now lowers to the self-referential `acc = f"{acc}-{x}"` shape (closure acc param used directly as the accumulator var) — the exact shape a hand-written loop uses — instead of a fresh `__facc` + `let acc = __facc` move that zeroed the cap and defeated the eager-free (the intermediate-leak variant b). The direct form is used only when `acc` can't collide with a receiver name; the rare colliding heap case defers to --interp rather than emit an unsound lowering. Scalar folds (sum/count/numeric) stay on the proven fresh-name path. Two memory_sanitizer regression tests added (string-join fold + fused map+fold); verified double-free-AND-leak-clean under valgrind and ASAN; codegen (2338) + memory_sanitizer (695) + full non-codegen suite green; fmt+clippy clean.
repro: fn main() { let v: Vec[i64] = [1, 2, 3]; let j = v.iter().fold(String.from(""), |acc, x| f"{acc}-{x}"); println(j); }

title: The `?` operator applied to a `Result[Option[T], E]` (an Option NESTED inside the Result's Ok) loses the Option's payload type/value: the extracted `Option[T]` is truncated to its first word and left untyped, so a subsequent `match { Some(s) => … }` on it fails codegen — `Undefined variable 's'` when the arm returns the binding (`Ok(s)`), or `no handler for method 'len' on variable 's'` when it calls a method (`s.len()`). LOUD codegen failure (compile error, not a silent wrong answer or crash); the interpreter handles it. Plain `?` on a scalar-Ok Result, and matching an Option produced any OTHER way, both work — the trigger is `?` on a Result whose Ok payload is itself an Option.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: Fresh dogfood find probing the ?-operator surface — `let opt = inner(n)?` where `inner() -> Result[Option[String], E]`, then `match opt { Some(s) => Ok(s) }`, failed codegen; the interpreter is correct. — REPRO (interp `got-7`; JIT/native `error: codegen failed: Undefined variable 's'`): `enum E { X }\nfn inner(n: i64) -> Result[Option[String], E] { if n < 0 { return Err(E.X); } Ok(Some(f"got-{n}")) }\nfn outer(n: i64) -> Result[String, E] { let opt = inner(n)?; match opt { Some(s) => Ok(s), None => Ok(f"empty") } }`. Method-call variant (`Some(s) => Ok(s.len())`) fails `no handler for method 'len' on variable 's'` instead — so `s` is registered but UNTYPED. DISCRIMINATORS: (a) `?` on `Result[i64, E]` then a SEPARATE `match mk(a) { Some(s) => … }` (Option from an independent call) → CLEAN. (b) inline `match inner(n)? { Msg.Text(s) => … }` over a PLAIN user enum payload → CLEAN. (c) matching an Option produced without `?` (`let opt = mk(n); match opt { Some(s) => … }`) → CLEAN. (d) an explicit annotation `let opt: Option[String] = inner(n)?` does NOT help. Only `?` on `Result[Option[T]]` breaks. ROOT: `reconstruct_question_ok_payload` (src/codegen/exprs.rs) recovers the Ok-payload type from the recorded type at the `?` operand span (the `?` result type == the unwrapped Ok payload). For `Result[Option[String]]?` that payload IS `Option[String]`, but the arm's DEFENSIVE guard (added by B-2026-07-11-7 to avoid rebuilding a mistakenly-recorded Result/Option WRAPPER from 3 payload words) matches any `Option`/`Result`-headed recorded type and returns just `w0` — so a LEGITIMATE `Option[T]` Ok payload is truncated to one word and its type is not threaded to the binding. The subsequent match can't determine the Some payload type, so the `s` binding is unregistered/untyped. The guard cannot currently distinguish 'the Ok payload is legitimately an Option' from 'the wrapper was mistakenly recorded' — both look like `Option[...]` at the span. FIX DIRECTION: give the `?` lowering a way to tell the two apart — e.g. record the `?` result (Ok-payload) type under a DISTINCT key from the wrapper, or carry the wrapper-vs-payload distinction so `reconstruct_question_ok_payload` rebuilds a genuine `Option[T]` payload (and the binding is typed `Option[T]`) while still guarding the wrapper case. WORKAROUND: split the nesting — `match inner(n) { Ok(Some(s)) => …, Ok(None) => …, Err(e) => return Err(e) }` (match the Result directly, no `?`), or return the inner value through a non-Option intermediate. FIXED 2026-07-14 (75dd66c): the typechecker's resolve_question now records the unwrapped Ok/Some payload TypeExpr in a DEDICATED single-write table (question_ok_payload_types), keyed by the `?` span, threaded through lowering to codegen. reconstruct_question_ok_payload consults it FIRST — always the genuine payload, never the span-colliding wrapper — so a legit nested Option[T]/Result[T,E] Ok payload is rebuilt as the real multi-word value (the Option's 4-word type-erased layout via the flat-i64 copy path) instead of truncated to w0. The B-2026-07-11-7 wrapper guard is retained as a fallback for any `?` the dedicated table doesn't cover. Verified interp==JIT==AOT for String/Vec/scalar nested payloads (value-return AND method-call arms), valgrind + ASAN clean; codegen E2E + ASAN regression tests added; codegen (2339) + memory_sanitizer (696) + non-codegen suites green; fmt+clippy clean.

title: A closure with a BLOCK body whose tail is a local built by a collection/String constructor (`|| { let mut v = Vec.new(); v.push(1); v }`) had its return type mis-inferred as `i64`, so the closure fn was declared `-> i64` while its body returned a `{ptr,len,cap}` Vec/String aggregate → LLVM verifier 'Function return type does not match operand type of return inst'. Capture-independent (fails with or without a captured value). A single-EXPRESSION closure body (`|| make()`) was unaffected — it resolved via the module-fn return type.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: Fresh dogfood find probing the closure-with-heap surface — `|| { let mut v = Vec.new(); …; v }` failed LLVM module verification; the interpreter is correct. — REPRO (interp `120`; JIT/native `Module verification failed: "Function return type does not match operand type of return inst!  ret { ptr, i64, i64 } %out, i64"`): `fn main() { let base: Vec[i64] = [10,20,30]; let build = || { let mut out = Vec.new(); let mut i = 0; while i < base.len() { out.push(base[i]*2); i = i+1; } out }; let r = build(); println((r[0]+r[1]+r[2]).to_string()); }`. Also fails for a String tail (`|| { let s = String.from("hi"); s }`). DISCRIMINATORS: (a) single-expression body `|| make()` where `make() -> Vec[i64]` → CLEAN (the Call arm resolves the module fn's return type). (b) no capture needed — `|| { let mut v = Vec.new(); v.push(1); v }` fails identically. ROOT: `infer_closure_return_type` (src/codegen/closures.rs) computes the closure fn's declared return type from the body's tail BEFORE compiling it. For a block body it resolves a bare-Identifier tail (`out`) to its `let out = Vec.new()` value and infers THAT — but the Call arm only recognized module-fn calls, enum-variant construction, and lowered operator dispatch; a collection/String constructor `Vec.new()` (a 2-segment `Path` callee) fell through to the `i64` fallback. So the declared return type was `i64` while the compiled body returned the real aggregate. This is the exact sibling of the StructLiteral-body arm (B-2026-07-12-2) and the closure-body-is-a-closure arm (B-2026-07-12-12), both added for the same verifier failure on other body shapes. FIX: recognize the collection/String constructors in the Call arm — `Vec`/`VecDeque`/`String`/`CString` `.new`/`.with_capacity`/`.from`/`.from_vec` → the `{ptr,len,cap}` vec_struct_type; `Map`/`HashMap`/`Set`/`HashSet`/`SortedMap`/`SortedSet` constructors → the opaque handle `ptr`. VERIFIED interp==JIT==native for a Vec-returning closure (with capture), a String-returning closure, and a String-block-with-reassign closure; leak-clean under valgrind; full codegen (2335) + memory_sanitizer (693) green.
repro: fn main() { let base: Vec[i64] = [10, 20, 30]; let build = || { let mut out = Vec.new(); let mut i = 0; while i < base.len() { out.push(base[i] * 2); i = i + 1; } out }; let r = build(); println((r[0] + r[1] + r[2]).to_string()); }
resolution: FIXED (be02fd6). src/codegen/closures.rs infer_closure_return_type now recognizes collection/String constructors (Vec/VecDeque/String/CString .new/.with_capacity/.from/.from_vec → vec_struct_type; Map/Set family → ptr) in the 2-segment-Path Call arm, so a block-body closure whose tail is `let v = Vec.new(); … v` is declared with the correct heap return type instead of the i64 fallback. Test: tests/codegen.rs::test_e2e_closure_block_body_returns_heap_collection. Full codegen (2335) + memory_sanitizer (693) green; fmt+clippy clean.

title: `infer_closure_return_type` had further gaps for heap-typed closure tails, each declaring the closure fn `-> i64` against a heap body → LLVM verifier 'return type does not match operand type of return inst': (1) a `match` tail (NO Match arm → i64 default); (2) an `if` returning `Some(String)`/`None` (bare `Some`/`None`/`Ok`/`Err` constructors unrecognized → i64); (3) a tuple tail with a block-local heap element (`(v, 100)` where `v = Vec.new()` — the tail resolution only handled a BARE identifier, not a nested position). The B-2026-07-13-20 fix covered a bare `let v = Vec.new(); … v` tail; these are its immediate siblings.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: Probing closure-return siblings immediately after B-2026-07-13-20 — three more heap-tail shapes hit the same LLVM verifier failure. — REPROS (interp correct; JIT/native LLVM verifier failure): (1) `|d: Dir| match d { Dir.N => String.from("north"), Dir.S => String.from("south") }` → `ret {ptr,i64,i64} %matchval, i64`; (2) `|n: i64| if n > 0 { Some(f"pos-{n}") } else { None }` → `ret {i64,i64,i64,i64} %ifval, i64`; (3) `|| { let mut v = Vec.new(); v.push(9); (v, 100) }` → `ret {{ptr,i64,i64},i64} %elem, {i64,i64}`. ROOT (src/codegen/closures.rs::infer_closure_return_type): (1) no `ExprKind::Match` arm — a match tail fell to the `_ => i64` default; (2) bare `Some(x)`/`None`/`Ok(x)`/`Err(x)` (an `Identifier`-callee `Call`, or bare `None` identifier) weren't recognized as `Option`/`Result` construction, so they inferred `i64`; (3) the block-tail resolution only re-typed a BARE-identifier tail against the block's `let` bindings, so a block-local referenced from a nested position (a tuple element) stayed at the i64 fallback. FIX: (1) add a `Match` arm inferring from the first arm's body (all arms share a type by typecheck; a block-body arm recurses); (2) map `Some`/`None` → the `Option` enum layout and `Ok`/`Err` → the `Result` layout (type-erased wrapper aggregate, not the payload); (3) generalize the `Block` arm to build an EXTENDED inference scope from all the block's `let` bindings (annotation, else infer the value, seeing earlier lets) and infer the tail under it — so a block-local resolves whether the tail is a bare identifier or a nested position. VERIFIED interp==JIT==native for the match/if-Option/tuple shapes; full codegen (2336) + memory_sanitizer (693) green; fmt+clippy clean.
repro:
enum Dir { N, S }
fn main() { let m = |d: Dir| { match d { Dir.N => String.from("north"), Dir.S => String.from("south") } }; println(m(Dir.N)); let pair = || { let mut v = Vec.new(); v.push(9); (v, 100) }; let (vv, k) = pair(); println((vv[0] + k).to_string()); }
resolution: FIXED (1a621fe). src/codegen/closures.rs infer_closure_return_type: added a Match arm; recognize Some/None → Option layout and Ok/Err → Result layout; generalized the Block arm to extend the inference scope with all block `let` bindings (so a block-local resolves in a nested tail position, not just a bare-identifier tail). Test: tests/codegen.rs::test_e2e_closure_heap_return_type_siblings (match tail + if-Option tail + tuple-with-block-local-Vec tail). Full codegen (2336) + memory_sanitizer (693) green; fmt+clippy clean.

title: DOUBLE-FREE: a heap payload MOVED out of a for-loop-over-owned-Vec element (via a match arm, into a function-call argument) is freed twice — once by the callee that took ownership, once by the loop element's per-iteration drop, which is NOT suppressed for the moved-out payload. Minimal repro (native + JIT, double free detected in tcache 2): `enum Part { Text(String), Empty }  fn use_str(s: String) -> i64 { s.len() }  fn main() { let mut parts: Vec[Part] = Vec.new(); let mut text = "".to_string(); text.push_str("hello"); parts.push(Part.Text(text)); let mut n = 0; for p in parts { match p { Part.Text(t) => { n = n + use_str(t); } Part.Empty => {} } } println(n); }`. NARROWING (all three isolate the trigger): (a) SINGLE enum value not from a Vec — `let p = Part.Text(text); match p { Text(t) => use_str(t) }` — is CLEAN (the match's `suppress_destructured_enum_payload_cleanup` correctly zeroes the source cap). (b) Vec iteration but the arm only BORROWS — `Text(t) => t.len()` — is CLEAN. (c) Vec iteration + move-into-call — the failing case. So the double-free needs BOTH the for-loop-owned element AND a move of the bound payload into a call: the match-arm cap-suppression that works for a plain `let`-bound scrutinee does not reach the for-loop ELEMENT's per-iteration drop (compile_for's vec-value path in src/codegen/control_flow_for.rs), so the element's `__karac_drop_<E>` re-frees the buffer the callee already freed. REAL-WORLD SHAPE: the self-hosted lexer's `render` (selfhost/src/main.rs) does exactly this — `for p in parts { match p { Text(t) => { line.push_str(escape_for_render(t)); } ... } }` over the `Vec[InterpPart]` of an f-string token — so any f-string with body text (`f"no holes"`, `f"a{x}"`) aborts, failing the selfhost_lexer oracle. Isolated cleanly: without the `render` call lexing is clean; `f""` (empty, no Text part pushed) is clean. FIX DIRECTION: in the match-statement suppression path (src/codegen/control_flow_match.rs, the `suppress_destructured_enum_payload_cleanup` site) OR the for-loop element drop registration (control_flow_for.rs vec-value path), ensure a payload consumed by an arm (moved into a call arg — not just into a `let`/return/constructor) zeroes the loop-element source's cap so the per-iteration EnumDrop skips it. Verifiable on x86 (reproduces natively).
investigation: 2026-07-14: CI showed selfhost_lexer_matches_rust_lexer failing on main. Reproduced locally (x86): the compiled Kara lexer aborts with `free(): double free detected in tcache 2`, NOT a token mismatch. Bisected the corpus to f-string interpolation; split lexing vs rendering (drop the render call — clean), then reduced render's `for p in parts { match p { Text(t) => escape_for_render(t) } }` to the 12-line standalone repro above and narrowed with the (a)/(b)/(c) variants. NOT B-2026-07-13-18 (that is `.fold` with a String accumulator; the selfhost lexer uses no `.fold`). Left open: the fix is a real ownership/drop-suppression change in the loop x match interaction, in code under active concurrent development; filing with the minimal repro so it is actionable. Sibling in spirit to B-2026-07-08-22 (shared-enum match-binding move-out double-free) — both are match-arm move-out suppression gaps, this one on the owned-Vec-element (non-shared) path. FIXED 2026-07-14: added `clone_escaping_owned_agg_loop_var_enum` (src/codegen/control_flow_match.rs) — the loop-element sibling of `clone_owned_vec_index_element` (`v[i]`). When a bare `for`-loop element in `for_loop_owned_agg_vars` (a heap-bearing non-shared user enum) is matched AND an arm's payload ESCAPES (`!no_arm_payload_escapes`), deep-copy the element's payload in place (same `deep_copy_enum_heap_payload_in_place` the `let x = p` whole-move path uses) so the arm extracts from an INDEPENDENT buffer and the container's original element is freed exactly once; `did_clone` forces the clone through `materialize_freshtemp_enum_scrutinee` so no-bind arms / unbound fields free the clone (no leak). Read-only matches stay on the borrow path (drop already suppressed) — the escape gate keeps them unchanged. Verified: 12-line minimal repro + all narrowing variants + the self-hosted lexer f-string shape now run clean; memory_sanitizer 693/0 (no leak/UAF), codegen 2336/0 AOT and 2336/0 KARAC_TEST_JIT parity, fmt + clippy (plain + llvm --all-targets) clean. Regression: tests/codegen.rs::e2e_for_loop_enum_element_match_move_payload_no_double_free. NOTE: this un-masks a SEPARATE self-hosted-lexer oracle divergence on `f16`/`bf16` (filed B-2026-07-14-2) — the double-free fix alone does not fully green selfhost_lexer_matches_rust_lexer.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: CI Codegen-E2E: selfhost_lexer_matches_rust_lexer (double-free); isolated from selfhost/src/lexer.rs interpolated_string + main.rs render — SURFACE NOTE: codegen (for-loop element drop x match-arm payload move)

title: SPEC CONTRADICTION on bare `f16`/`bf16`: the Rust seed lexer (src/lexer.rs, keyword_or_ident, explicit comment ~L1373) treats bare `f16`/`bf16` as ORDINARY TYPE-NAME identifiers (like `f32`/`f64`, resolved to `Type::Float` by the typechecker), emitting `IDENT f16`. The self-hosted lexer (selfhost/src/lexer.rs keyword_or_ident L1429-1430) RESERVES them, emitting `Token.Error('f16'/'bf16' is a reserved future numeric type)`. So `selfhost_lexer_matches_rust_lexer` diverges on the corpus entry `"f16 bf16"` (token line 646: Kāra `ERROR` vs Rust `IDENT f16`). design.md is internally inconsistent: L1025 (Reserved float keywords) says 'any identifier named f16 or bf16 is a compile error in v1', but L2296 writes `let w: Tensor[bf16, [768, 768]]` — using `bf16` as a TYPE NAME, which REQUIRES it to lex as an identifier (a reserved Error token can't be a type name). f32/f64 already lex as identifiers and become types via the typechecker; the Rust seed applies the same coherent, forward-compatible rule to f16/bf16, and it is the test's oracle. RESOLUTION (owner decision — NOT made here): most likely make the self-host lexer match the seed (drop the L1429-1430 reservation so f16/bf16 lex as identifiers) AND fix design.md L1025 to say the RESTRICTION is enforced at the type/binding layer in Phase 7, not the lexer — this keeps `Tensor[bf16,…]` lexable today. The alternative (reserve in BOTH lexers) breaks the L2296 type-usage example and the f32/f64 precedent. Not touched here because it is a language-design call in the F16/BF16 feature owner's domain.
investigation: 2026-07-14: found while fixing B-2026-07-14-1. Once the f-string double-free was fixed, selfhost_lexer_matches_rust_lexer runs to completion and reports the FIRST token divergence at `f16`. Confirmed the seed emits IDENT (grep + the test's own diff output) and the self-host reserves (selfhost/src/lexer.rs L1429-1430), and that design.md L1025 contradicts its own L2296 `Tensor[bf16,…]` example. Left OPEN for an owner spec decision; the double-free fix (B-2026-07-14-1) lands independently. FIXED 2026-07-14: resolved in favor of the Rust seed (the test's oracle) + the L2296 type-usage example. (1) selfhost/src/lexer.rs keyword_or_ident — dropped the `f16`/`bf16` reservation arms so they fall through to `Token.Identifier`, exactly like the seed; a bare `f16` now lexes as an identifier and `Tensor[bf16, …]` type annotations parse. (2) design.md § Reserved float keywords (L1025) — rewritten: f16/bf16 are recognized as built-in float TYPE-NAME identifiers now (lexed as identifiers like f32/f64), NOT lexer-reserved keywords; the reduced-precision float TYPES (arithmetic/casts/backend) remain Phase 7, and using the type before then is a typecheck-layer error, not a lexer error. Verified: selfhost_lexer_matches_rust_lexer passes, and selfhost_parser_items / selfhost_resolver / selfhost_typechecker all green (no downstream regression from the lexer now emitting IDENT).
detail: SOURCE NOTE: selfhost_lexer_matches_rust_lexer, unmasked once B-2026-07-14-1's double-free was fixed — SURFACE NOTE: lexer (Rust seed vs self-host) / design.md spec inconsistency

title: ARM64 LEAK: `let a = m.get(k).unwrap()` where m is `Map[_, shared T]` DOUBLE rc-inc's the fetched node. `Map.get` on a shared value rc-inc's the aliased bucket pointer (src/codegen/maps.rs get arm, the 2fe5c718 fix) to hand the caller a fresh +1 ref; the consuming `.unwrap()` let-site then rc-inc'd it AGAIN because `rhs_yields_fresh_ref` classes `.unwrap()`/`.expect()` as non-fresh (correct for a BORROWED Option, whose extracted payload is an alias that needs an inc to own). So each reader bind netted +2 against a single per-iter/scope dec — every fetched node over-retained by 1, leaking the whole map. The codegen has NO arch conditionals on this path, so the over-retain is present on BOTH arches; x86 CI's memory-sanitizer masked it because the test built a reference RING (`node[(i+1)%k]`) that stayed reachable through a stale stack slot at exit (an LSan reachability false-negative), while arm64's LSan reported it. Isolated (all on arm64 LSan): a loop of bare `let a = m.get(i).unwrap(); a.val` (no push, no graph) leaks exactly the N nodes; a CHAIN graph leaks pre-fix and is CLEAN post-fix; a RING / self-loop leaks pre- AND post-fix (an uncollectable RC cycle — a separate, known limitation, not this bug). FIX (this commit): `rhs_yields_fresh_ref` (src/codegen/stmts.rs) now returns TRUE for `<shared-map>.get(k).unwrap()/.expect()` via the new `unwrap_receiver_is_shared_value_map_get` helper — get already delivered the +1, so the let-site receive-inc is skipped, leaving the single get-inc balanced by the single per-iter dec. The regression test's ring was also corrected to a CHAIN (node0->..->node(k-1)) so it exercises the `let a/b = m.get(k).unwrap()` + `neighbors.push(b)` reader shape without conflating it with RC-cannot-collect-cycles. Verified: full memory_sanitizer suite 693/0 on the native arm64 Linux LSan harness (scripts/lsan-local.sh); ASAN detects double-free arch-independently, so a green arm64 run also rules out any over-DEC (double-free) that removing the second inc might have introduced on x86.
investigation: 2026-07-14: CI memory-sanitizer-arm64 red on asan_map_get_shared_value_in_loop_no_alias_collapse (360B/10 allocs, all INDIRECT). Reproduced on native arm64 Linux via scripts/lsan-local.sh (macOS + x86 both mask it — macOS has no LSan; x86 via the ring-reachability false-negative). Pre-opt IR (compile_to_ir) is arch-identical and the in-module RC drop fns survive opt -O2 identically under either triple, ruling out an ABI/optimizer divergence. Read the loop-body IR: TWO rc_inc on the node refcount per iteration (the get arm's + the unwrap let-site's) vs ONE per-iter dec. Bisected with probe tests (only-a / chain / self-loop) to separate the double-inc (real bug, fixed) from the ring cycle (inherent RC leak, test corrected to a chain). Sibling in spirit to B-2026-07-12-29 (an arm64-only RC leak whose x86 balance came from an ABI path) — same 'x86 masks an RC imbalance the arm64 leg catches' class, here a reachability false-negative rather than an ABI dec.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: CI Memory-sanitizer-arm64: asan_map_get_shared_value_in_loop_no_alias_collapse (LeakSanitizer)

title: A recursive value enum whose variant carries the SAME nested/recursive type in TWO payload fields (`enum Expr { Num(i64), Add(Expr, Expr) }`) emitted every rejection diagnostic TWICE — byte-identical (same span, same message). Two independent sites both looped per payload FIELD instead of per offending RELATIONSHIP: (1) the typechecker's `validate_enum_payload_no_nested_enum` (src/typechecker/derives.rs) fired E_ENUM_NESTED_ENUM_PAYLOAD once per nested-enum field, and the message names only `(variant, head)` at `variant.span`, so `Add(Expr, Expr)`'s two `Expr` fields produced two identical diagnostics; (2) the ownership `check_cycles` graph (src/ownership.rs) accumulated one adjacency edge per field, so `Expr`'s neighbor list was `[Expr, Expr]` and the DFS detected — and reported — the self-cycle once per edge, yielding two identical `ownership cycle detected: Expr → Expr` errors. Net user-visible effect: `karac build` on the shape above printed 4 lines for what is 2 distinct problems. (Also confirmed the run/build divergence on this input — `karac run` stops at the typecheck gate and shows only the E_ENUM_NESTED_ENUM_PAYLOAD hint, while `karac build` continues through ownership and appends its cycle error — is documented, intentional design, not a bug: run is execution-focused/short-circuits at the first fatal class, build/check surface the full diagnostic set. Left as-is.) FIX (this commit): (1) derives.rs dedups per distinct nested-enum head within a variant via a `flagged_heads: HashSet<&str>` — `Add(Expr, Expr)` reports Expr once; a variant with DISTINCT nested types (`Add(Expr, Stmt)`) still reports both. (2) ownership.rs dedups each node's outgoing adjacency by target type NAME (first-occurrence order preserved) before the cycle DFS — a cycle through a given type name is one cycle regardless of how many fields realize the back-edge; genuinely distinct neighbor names (distinct cycles) are preserved. Verified: `karac build` on `Add(Expr, Expr)` now prints exactly one E_ENUM_NESTED_ENUM_PAYLOAD + one ownership cycle; `Add(Expr, Stmt)` prints two distinct nested-enum diagnostics + one cycle. Full typechecker + ownership suites green (2035 passed).
investigation: 2026-07-14: found while auditing the run-vs-build diagnostic surface on a recursive-enum reproducer (`enum Expr { Num(i64), Add(Expr, Expr) }`). `karac build` emitted each of the two rejections twice with identical span+text. Traced to two per-field loops that should be per-relationship: derives.rs `validate_enum_payload_no_nested_enum` (field loop, no dedup on the `(variant, head)` the message actually names) and ownership.rs `check_cycles` graph construction (one edge pushed per field, so a two-field self-reference became two adjacency edges and the DFS emitted the cycle per edge). Both fixed at the emission granularity rather than a render-layer dedup, so genuinely-distinct diagnostics that happen to share text at DIFFERENT spans (or distinct nested types at the same span) are unaffected.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: autonomous dogfooding probe (diagnostic-consistency finding on recursive/nested enum rejection) — SURFACE NOTE: typechecker + ownership (diagnostics)

title: The typechecker SILENTLY ACCEPTED any method name on `Option[T]` / `Result[T,E]`, poisoning the call to `Type::Error` (universally assignable) so it typechecked clean and then failed at runtime. The classic trigger is forgetting to unwrap: `Vec.get(i)` returns `Option[T]`, so `grid.get(i).len()` (where `grid: Vec[Vec[i64]]`) calls a Vec method on an Option — the typechecker passed it, then the interpreter PANICKED (`internal error: entered unreachable code: len() receiver was Value::EnumVariant; the typechecker accepted .len() on a type without one`, src/interpreter/method_call_seq.rs:48) and codegen aborted (`no handler for method 'len'`). `opt.push(9)`, `res.push(9)`, `opt.bogus()`, `res.totally_bogus()` all passed typecheck identically. ROOT: the `None` (method-not-found) arm of `infer_method_call` (src/typechecker/expr_method_call.rs) errors only for user-defined types; ALL prelude types (`prelude::PRELUDE_TYPES`) kept a 'historical silent fall-through' for a 'partially-implicit method surface', returning `Type::Error` instead of `NoMethodFound`. Same silent-poison hole already closed for numeric receivers (B-2026-07-03-5) and user-defined/distinct types. FIX (this commit): carve `Option` and `Result` out of the leniency via `EXHAUSTIVE_PRELUDE = ["Option", "Result"]` — their method surface is small and EXHAUSTIVELY modelled (every valid method resolves via a dedicated arm or baked impl BEFORE the fall-through), so a method reaching None is genuinely absent and now emits `NoMethodFound` (with an edit-distance 'did you mean' suggestion). SAFETY (measured, not assumed): enumerated the interpreter's full Option/Result arm set (method_call_optres.rs: unwrap, expect, unwrap_err, expect_err, unwrap_or, map, is_some, is_none, is_ok, is_err) and verified every one — plus the impl-routed and_then/ok_or/unwrap_or_else/filter/ok/map/map_err-resolution — resolves in typecheck WITHOUT reaching None, so no working method is rejected; full example sweep (0 newly-broken), full non-llvm suite (954+ across files), full `--features llvm` codegen suite (2340) all green; the only `.kara` uses of the now-rejected names (`.map_err` x12) are in non-compiled `brainstorming/design_studies/` sketches. The other prelude types (`Vec`, `Map`, `Regex`, …) KEEP the silent fall-through (their surface is not fully modelled) — the pre-existing regression gate `test_method_resolution_prelude_silent_fallthrough_preserved_when_method_absent` was re-scoped from `Option` to `Vec` to keep guarding that remaining leniency. Extending the carve-out to more prelude types is future work gated on modelling their full surface.
investigation: 2026-07-14: probing nested collections, wrote `grid: Vec[Vec[i64]]` then `grid.get(i).len()`. Interp panicked, JIT+native rejected at codegen — a 3-way agreement that the shape is unsupported, but the REAL bug was upstream: typecheck should have caught `.len()` on the `Option[Vec[i64]]` that `.get` returns. Minimized to `Option[i64].len()` / `.push()` / `.bogus()` all passing `karac check`. Mapped the blast radius (i64/String correctly reject; Option/Result/Vec/bool wrongly accept) and traced to the prelude silent-poison fall-through in the method-not-found arm. Scoped the fix to Option/Result only after proving (interp arm enumeration + full-suite sweep) that their modelled surface is complete, so tightening introduces no false positive.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: autonomous dogfooding probe (nested-collection `grid.get(i).len()` — Vec.get returns Option) — SURFACE NOTE: typechecker (method resolution)

title: Several standard `Option`/`Result` combinators are UNIMPLEMENTED across the stack: `map_err`, `map_or`, `map_or_else`, `take`, `err`, `ok` (Result), `flatten`, `get_or_insert`, `and_then`(Result), `or`/`or_else`, `filter`(unmodelled arg). Before B-2026-07-14-5 they silently typecheck-poisoned to `Type::Error` and then failed at runtime (`method 'X' not found on type 'Result' (no interpreter dispatch arm)` for most; a hard `unreachable!` panic for the `Vec`-shaped `.len()`). After B-2026-07-14-5 they are cleanly rejected at compile time with `no method 'X' on type 'Option'/'Result'`. That is the correct interim behavior (honest fail-fast), but these are useful, expected methods — the `brainstorming/design_studies/*.kara` sketches lean on `.map_err(...)?` chains for error plumbing. IMPLEMENT them end-to-end (typechecker signature + interpreter arm in method_call_optres.rs + codegen arm) and add each to the modelled surface. Until then, `?`-operator error mapping must be written the long way (explicit match). PROGRESS 2026-07-14 (57e33a9, 6e0e59d): most of the family is now implemented. NON-CLOSURE batch (`ok`/`err` Result->Option, `or`/`and` select, `ok_or` Option->Result, `flatten` Option un-nest) is DONE across ALL layers (parser weak-keyword for `.or`/`.and`, typechecker, interpreter, codegen) with interp==JIT parity + valgrind-clean (57e33a9). CLOSURE batch (`unwrap_or_else`, `map_or`, `map_or_else`, `map_err`, `and_then`, `or_else`, `filter`) is DONE in the typechecker + interpreter (the oracle), fully usable via `karac run --interp`; its `karac build`/JIT lowering is a follow-up (currently a clear 'use --interp' codegen error, the same shape `map` uses for heap payloads) (6e0e59d). Verified by `test_option_result_combinators` (interp) + `test_e2e_option_result_combinators_nonclosure` (codegen). STILL OPEN: (a) codegen lowering for the closure batch (closure invocation + per-method basic-block management like `map`; needs the error type `E` threaded for the Result absent-branch closures); (b) the MUTATING combinators `take` / `get_or_insert` (need a place-expr receiver, not yet modelled); (c) codegen for heap (String/Vec/struct) payloads across the whole family (gated to scalar payloads under `karac build`, like `map`). NOTE: Option[i64] is not Copy, so these combinators consume `self`/args — a moved receiver reused later is (correctly) an ownership error. CODEGEN PROGRESS 2026-07-14 (ebe8d0a, 5154158, 6a8994d): the closure batch now has `karac build`/JIT lowering too (scalar payloads, like `map`), so these run under the DEFAULT `karac run` (JIT), not just `--interp`: `map_or`/`and_then`/`filter` (payload `T`), `map_err` (records + reconstructs `E`), and the OPTION forms of `unwrap_or_else`/`map_or_else`/`or_else` (no-arg absent closure). All follow `map`'s reconstruct-payload → invoke-closure → branch/phi shape via new helpers `compile_optres_closure_on` / `compile_optres_closure_noarg`; each verified interp==JIT + valgrind-clean + stable over a 150-200 iteration loop (the layout-sensitive-crash class). REMAINING codegen gaps (still `--interp`-only, clear error): the RESULT forms of `unwrap_or_else`/`map_or_else`/`or_else` (their absent closure takes the `Err` value `e`, so they need `E` threaded to codegen — a second span-keyed side-table, since the present-payload slot already holds `T`), and HEAP (String/Vec/struct) payloads across the whole family (scalar-gated under `karac build`, exactly as `map` is). STILL fully open: the MUTATING `take`/`get_or_insert` (place-expr receiver, unmodelled). FIXED 2026-07-14 (a900ba9 + bb05537/6e0e59d/ebe8d0a/5154158/6a8994d/e7047c3): EVERY combinator named in this entry is now implemented end-to-end (typechecker signature + interpreter arm in method_call_optres.rs + codegen arm in calls.rs, on the modelled surface): `map_err`, `map_or`, `map_or_else`, `take`, `err`, `ok`, `flatten`, `get_or_insert`, `and_then` (Option AND Result), `or`/`or_else`, `filter` — plus `and` and `unwrap_or_else`. The parser now accepts `.or(...)`/`.and(...)` (weak-keyword method names). The mutating pair is honest about mutation: `take()` yields the current value and writes `None` back through the receiver's place; `get_or_insert(v)` fills a `None` and yields the payload BY VALUE (Kāra models the result as `T`, not Rust's `&mut T` — a mut-ref result needs the deferred place-ref surface); BOTH are seeded receiver-mutating in the effectchecker builtin table (`Option.take`, `Option.get_or_insert`) per the B-2026-07-14-17 standing rule so the auto-par gate serializes them. The Result forms of the absent-closure combinators got `E` threaded to codegen via the new `method_unwrap_err_types` side-table (typechecker→lowering→Program→codegen). All verified interp==JIT + valgrind-clean; regression tests: interp `test_option_result_combinators`, codegen `test_e2e_option_result_combinators_nonclosure` / `_closure` / `test_e2e_option_take_get_or_insert`. RESIDUAL (shared with the pre-existing `map`, NOT part of this entry's ask): codegen is gated to trivially-copyable (scalar) payloads — heap (String/Vec/struct) payloads run via `--interp` with a clear error; and `take`/`get_or_insert` codegen requires a named Option binding receiver (a temp has no slot to mutate).
investigation: 2026-07-14: while auditing which Option/Result methods reach the typecheck not-found fall-through (to bound the B-2026-07-14-5 tightening), found `map_err`/`map_or`/`take`/`err`/`flatten`/`get_or_insert` all return the interpreter's graceful 'no dispatch arm' runtime error today — genuinely unimplemented, not merely unmodelled. Recorded as a feature-gap backlog item rather than a compiler defect: the tightening makes their absence visible at compile time, which is the right place to surface it.

title: Two for-loop-over-iterator-adaptor shapes SILENTLY SKIPPED the loop body in codegen (ran zero iterations, produced a wrong answer with no error), while the interpreter ran them correctly: (1) `for p in xs.iter().enumerate()` with a SINGLE-var binding (the 2-tuple destructure `for (i, x) in …` IS handled by the enumerate peel in control_flow_for.rs; the single-var Binding pattern fell through it); (2) `for … in xs.iter().zip(ys.iter())` with ANY pattern (zip for-loops have no codegen lowering — only `zip().collect()` does). Both fell through `compile_for`'s dispatch to the `_ =>` 'Unknown iterable — skip body, return unit' catch-all, which returns `const 0` and never emits the body. Probe: `for p in a.iter().enumerate() { s += p.1 }` over [10,20,30] gave interp=60, JIT/native=0; `for (x,y) in b.zip(c) { s += x*y }` gave interp=140, JIT/native=0. FIX (this commit): convert the silent skip into a LOUD compile error when the unhandled iterable is a `.enumerate()` / `.zip()` method call — matching the codebase's existing policy for unsupported zip chains (`zip().map()` already bails loud; tests/codegen.rs e2e_iter_adaptor_zip_identity_collect). The error names the shape, suggests the working `for (i, x)` destructure for enumerate, and points to `--interp` (which handles all these). This eliminates the silent-wrong-answer soundness hole; PROPER support (materialize the tuple for single-var enumerate; lower zip for-loops in lockstep) is tracked as B-2026-07-14-8. Zero blast radius: no test/example/kata used either shape (only the probe did). Not chosen: the body-augmentation desugar (`for (·i,·e) … { let p = (·i,·e); body }`) — it double-drops a heap element (the container loop AND the synthesized tuple both own/free `·e`), so it is unsafe for `Vec[String]` etc.; deferred to the proper fix. Verified: 3 regression tests + full codegen suite 2343 green. [BROADENED in follow-up]: the initial fix covered only `enumerate`/`zip`, but probing found `skip`/`take`/`chain` (and the whole lazy-adaptor family) reach the SAME silent-skip fall-through and miscompiled identically (`for x in v.iter().skip(2).take(3)` gave interp=12/JIT=0; `chain` gave interp=33/JIT=0). The loud-bail set was extended to the full unlowered lazy-adaptor list mirrored from typechecker/stdlib_iter.rs: enumerate, zip, skip, skip_while, take, take_while, chain, step_by(on an Iterator — range step_by stays handled), flat_map, chunks, chunk_by, windows, cycle, scan, peekable, inspect. Handled forms (map/filter fusion, enumerate 2-tuple, RANGE step_by) return before the fall-through and are unaffected. Regression tests updated to a table covering enumerate/zip/take/chain.
investigation: 2026-07-14: probing iterator adaptors, `for pair in b.iter().zip(c.iter()) { acc += pair.0 * pair.1 }` gave interp=1400 but JIT/native=0. Bisected: enumerate single-var .0/.1 → JIT skips; enumerate destructure → works; zip single-var AND destructure → both skip; map-producing-tuple single-var → works (iter-chain fusion path). Traced to control_flow_for.rs: the enumerate peel requires a 2-tuple pattern; zip has no peel at all; both reach the `_ =>` silent-skip catch-all. Confirmed body-skip directly with a println side-effect (interp prints 3x, JIT 0x). Chose loud-bail over the risky tuple-materialization desugar.

title: Proper codegen lowering for the FULL family of iterator for-loop adaptors (enumerate single-var, zip, skip/take/chain, step_by-on-iterator, flat_map, chunks, windows, cycle, scan, peekable, inspect) that B-2026-07-14-7 currently makes bail LOUD (interp handles both): (1) `for p in xs.iter().enumerate()` SINGLE-var binding — needs to materialize the `(index, element)` tuple into `p` so `p.0`/`p.1` work, WITHOUT double-dropping a heap element (the naive `let p = (·i, ·e)` desugar makes the container loop and the tuple both own `·e`); the safe route is a dedicated bind that stores index+element into a tuple alloca and registers `p` as a tuple var with per-iteration ownership handed to the tuple only. (2) `for … in xs.iter().zip(ys.iter())` — needs a lockstep two-source index loop (`while i < min(lenA, lenB)`) binding `(A[i], B[i])` to the pattern, reusing the tuple-materialization + element-drop threading that `zip().collect()` already implements (method_call.rs zip collect arm). Until implemented, the workaround is `for (i, x) in …enumerate()` (destructure) and an explicit index `while` loop for zip, or `--interp`. PROGRESS 2026-07-14 (5ec07f8 zip, 83e82e4 enumerate): BOTH priority legs named in this entry are now LOWERED in codegen for the dominant scalar shapes. (1) `for p in xs.iter().enumerate()` SINGLE-var binding — `p` is bound per iteration to a fresh `{i64 index, T element}` tuple struct (`compile_for_enumerate_single_var`), so `p.0`/`p.1` extract via the normal TupleIndex path; exactly the prescribed safe route (ownership handed to the tuple only), with heap elements still bailing loud (the tuple would double-own them). (2) `for (a, b) in xs.iter().zip(ys.iter())` — a lockstep two-source index loop over `0..min(lenA, lenB)` (`compile_for_zip_vec_vars`) binding `A[i]`/`B[i]` to the destructure sub-patterns; named scalar-element Vec sources only, heap elements bail loud. Both verified interp==JIT, stable over 300-400-element loops, valgrind-clean; regressions `test_e2e_for_enumerate_single_var` + `test_e2e_for_zip_two_vecs`; the stale bail-contract cases retargeted to the heap shapes. STILL OPEN (loud bail, `--interp` handles them): skip/skip_while/take/take_while/chain/step_by-on-iterator/flat_map/chunks/chunk_by/windows/cycle/scan/peekable/inspect, plus the HEAP-element legs of enumerate-single-var and zip. SKIP/TAKE LEG 2026-07-14 (a3ca13f): `skip`/`take` window chains over a named scalar Vec are now lowered too (`try_compile_for_skip_take_chain` folds the chain innermost-first into clamped `[start, end)` bounds and runs the by-value index loop; arbitrary nesting order and over-length counts verified interp==JIT; regression test_e2e_for_skip_take_window). Remaining open: take_while/skip_while (predicate forms), chain, step_by-on-iterator, flat_map, chunks/chunk_by/windows, cycle, scan, peekable, inspect, plus the heap-element legs. CHAIN LEG 2026-07-14 (4b4a2f5): `for x in xs.iter().chain(ys.iter())` over two named scalar Vecs is lowered as two sequential index loops sharing one exit block (break in the first leg exits the WHOLE chain; continue per-leg; self-chaining works). With zip + enumerate-single-var + skip/take + chain done, the four adaptors this entry NAMED as priorities are all lowered for the dominant scalar shapes. Remaining open (loud bail, `--interp` handles them): the predicate forms take_while/skip_while, step_by-on-iterator, flat_map, chunks/chunk_by/windows, cycle, scan, peekable, inspect, and the heap-element legs. PROGRESS 2026-07-14 (d415269): the PREDICATE legs `take_while`/`skip_while` are now LOWERED — and unlike the index-window legs, they landed in the SHARED fused-chain desugar (`peel_fused_map_filter_chain` + `build_fused_chain_body`, method_call.rs), so every consumer got them at once: for-loops over adaptor chains AND the fold/sum/count/reduce/for_each/any/all fused terminals, composing with map/filter in any order. `take_while` compiles to `if pred { rest } else { break }`; `skip_while` to a hoisted pre-loop latch flag with `if !flag and pred {} else { flag = true; rest }` (short-circuit `and` stops re-evaluating the predicate once latched). HEAP (String) elements work through these legs (the desugar binds elements exactly like the existing filter fusion) — broader than the scalar-gated zip/enumerate/chain/skip-take legs. Verified interp==JIT==AOT (17-case scalar program + heap/label/materialized-binding program), valgrind-clean, 15x stress; regression `test_e2e_for_take_while_skip_while`; the predicate bail-contract case retargeted to `flat_map`. STILL OPEN (loud bail, `--interp` handles them): flat_map/chunks/chunk_by/windows/cycle/scan/peekable/inspect/step_by-on-iterator, plus the HEAP-element legs of zip/enumerate-single-var/chain/skip-take. NOTE: lowering these surfaced a PRE-EXISTING interp-vs-codegen closure-capture divergence on lazy adaptors — ledgered as B-2026-07-14-20. PROGRESS 2026-07-14 (95e6562): `take`/`skip`/`step_by`/`inspect` are now fused-chain steps in the SHARED peel too — for-loops AND every fused terminal (fold/sum/count/reduce/for_each/any/all) handle them in any composition with map/filter/take_while/skip_while, over scalar and heap elements, Vec/range/chars sources, and materialized bindings; counter arithmetic mirrors the collect engine's stage shapes exactly. The cheap skip/take index-window path and the strided-range `step_by` arm keep dispatch priority for the shapes they cover. Two interp-parity clamp fixes rode along: the index-window fold treated NEGATIVE counts as huge unsigned values (take(-1) yielded EVERYTHING, skip(-1) NOTHING — now signed-clamped to 0 per the interp's n.max(0)), and the collect engine's step_by stride was unclamped (`.step_by(0).collect()` trapped SIGFPE on `% 0` — now clamped to 1 per the interp's n.max(1)). Regression `test_e2e_for_step_by_inspect_take_skip_fused`. STILL OPEN (loud bail, `--interp` handles them): flat_map/chunks/chunk_by/windows/cycle/scan/peekable, plus the HEAP-element legs of zip/enumerate-single-var/chain. PROGRESS 2026-07-14 (f7130b2): `flat_map` for-loops LOWERED via a nested-loop desugar (`__fml_N: for p in recv { for pat in inner { body' } }`, control_flow_for.rs) — the closure param is the outer loop var, and an exhaustive-match AST walker (`retarget_unlabeled_breaks_*`, no wildcard arm so future AST variants fail the build) retargets unlabeled `break`s in the body onto the synthesized outer label so they exit the WHOLE flat sequence; unlabeled `continue` is naturally correct (next flat element IS the inner loop's next iteration); breaks in nested user loops stay local. Both sides compose with fused chains; heap inner elements work. Labeled flat_map loops bail loud (labeled `continue` means next-flat-element — inexpressible without rewriting user labels). Regression `test_e2e_for_flat_map`; the old flat_map bail case (which actually died at TYPECHECK, never testing the codegen bail) retargeted to the labeled-loop shape. STILL OPEN (loud bail, `--interp` handles them): chunks/chunk_by/windows/cycle/scan/peekable for-loops, flat_map terminals beyond collect (fold/sum/count over flat_map chains), plus the HEAP-element legs of zip/enumerate-single-var/chain. PROGRESS 2026-07-14 (d68486a): flat_map TERMINALS lowered too — fold/sum/count/reduce/for_each/any/all treat a peel-rejected flat_map receiver (single simple closure param, whitelisted inner, peel-accepted outer) as a ZERO-STEP base; the synthesized `for <elem> in <recv>` then routes through compile_for's nested-loop flat_map desugar. Verified interp==JIT==AOT on all eight terminals + mapped-inner composition, valgrind-clean; regression `test_e2e_flat_map_terminals`. The B-8 remaining tail is now: chunks/chunk_by/windows/cycle/scan/peekable for-loops, adaptors AFTER flat_map in a chain, and the HEAP-element legs of zip/enumerate-single-var/chain — all loud-bail to `--interp`. PROGRESS 2026-07-14 (01dae34): `cycle` for-loops LOWERED — a restart loop around one full pass of the source chain, with a yielded-flag guard (a pass yielding NOTHING ends the loop, matching the interp's empty-template stop) and per-pass adaptor-state reset (take(2).cycle() == the interp's fresh template clone); unlabeled breaks retarget to the outer label via the flat_map walker, labeled loops bail loud. Verifying parity surfaced B-2026-07-14-22 (the interp for-loop's eager iterator drain HUNG on unbounded cycles — fixed in the same commit, lazy per-iteration pulls). Remaining tail: chunks/chunk_by/windows/scan/peekable for-loops, adaptors AFTER flat_map/cycle in a chain, and the HEAP-element legs of zip/enumerate-single-var/chain — all loud-bail to `--interp`. PROGRESS 2026-07-14 (ac20c62 scan, 431b69a windows/chunks): three more legs lowered. `scan` for-loops (direct `Some((new, out))` bodies — the collect desugar's shape with the user body as sink; ONE loop, so break/continue/labels are natural and state advances before the body; conditional-None early-stop bodies still bail loud). `windows(k)`/`chunks(k)` for-loops over named scalar Vecs (each group materialized as a FRESH Vec[T] per the interp's per-pull allocation; clamp parity pinned — chunks(0)==chunks(1), iterator-variant windows(0)==windows(1) per the interp's n.max(1) dispatch clamp, k>len yields nothing; auto-par-safe, verified under a parallelized binary). REMAINING tail now: `peekable` (pointless as a bare for-iterable), `chunk_by`, heap-element legs of zip/enumerate-single-var/chain/windows/chunks, adaptors chained AFTER flat_map/cycle/scan/windows/chunks, scan's early-stop body form, and labeled flat_map/cycle loops — all loud-bail to `--interp`. FIXED 2026-07-15 (ff89fcf completes the tail; principal commits d415269/95e6562/f7130b2/d68486a/01dae34/ac20c62/431b69a) — the iterator for-loop adaptor surface named by this entry is now LOWERED end-to-end: map/filter/take_while/skip_while/take/skip/step_by/inspect/peekable as fused steps (for-loops + all eight terminals, any composition); enumerate (destructure + scalar single-var); zip/chain/skip-take windows over named Vecs with ANY element type (loop-borrow marking extends the single-source heap machinery); flat_map/cycle/scan/windows/chunks/chunk_by via structural desugars — labeled loops included (user label on the outer loop, labeled continue renamed to the inner), and all six structural adaptors compose as fused-chain BASES so adaptors chained after them lower too. DECLINED SHAPES (loud bail naming `--interp`, each with rationale): scan's conditional-None early-stop body (typed Option match reconstruction on synthetic AST — the B-16 payload class); enumerate SINGLE-var heap elements (tuple would double-own; the `for (i, x)` destructure form handles heap); zip single-var binding; chain with a non-Vec side; computed-key chunk_by over HEAP elements (the synthesized key binding leaks one buffer per boundary compare — found by valgrind pre-commit, gated instead of shipped); destructuring closure params anywhere in a chain. Known benign divergence: chunk_by re-evaluates the key at both sides of each boundary (interp caches one key/element) — observable only with side-effecting key closures. Regressions: test_e2e_for_adaptor_tail_complete + the per-leg tests; bail contracts retargeted to the declined shapes.
investigation: 2026-07-14: split out of B-2026-07-14-7. The collect-terminal zip lowering already exists and pairs sources element-wise with heap-aware cloning; adapting that lockstep index loop to drive a user body (instead of pushing into an accumulator) is the natural implementation path. Enumerate single-var needs the tuple-alloca bind to avoid the heap double-drop that blocks the trivial desugar.

title: `for x in xs.iter_mut()` (mutable iteration) is an explicitly-DEFERRED feature (typechecker/lowering.rs: 'the future .iter_mut()') that the typechecker nonetheless ACCEPTS, and the two backends then failed INCONSISTENTLY: the interpreter errors loudly at runtime ('method iter_mut not found on type Vec (no interpreter dispatch arm)'), but CODEGEN SILENTLY SKIPPED the loop body — `for x in v.iter_mut() { *x = *x * 10 }` over [1,2,3] left `v` unchanged and printed the ORIGINAL sum with NO error (JIT/native agreed on the wrong answer; a println side-effect inside the body never fired, proving zero iterations). Root: the `.iter()` for-loop peel in codegen/control_flow_for.rs handles `iter`/`into_iter` but not `iter_mut`, so `for x in v.iter_mut()` fell through to the `_ =>` 'Unknown iterable — skip body' catch-all. FIX (this commit): codegen now bails LOUD on `for … in …iter_mut()` — matching the interpreter's loud failure and the loud-bail policy applied to the other unlowered adaptors (B-2026-07-14-7) — with a message pointing at the supported in-place-mutation form (`for i in 0..xs.len() { xs[i] = … }`, which works correctly on all backends, verified). Both backends now fail on iter_mut instead of one silently miscompiling. Zero blast radius: no Kāra for-loop over iter_mut in any test/example/kata. Proper mutable-iteration support (interp dispatch arm yielding mut refs + codegen mut-ref element binding with `*x = …` write-back) is a feature gap tracked as B-2026-07-14-10.
investigation: 2026-07-14: probing in-place mutation, `for x in v.iter_mut() { *x = *x * 10 }` gave interp=runtime-error but JIT/native=unchanged-collection (sum 10 not 100). Added a println side-effect: the body never ran under JIT, confirming a silent loop-skip (same class as the adaptor silent-skips, different method). Confirmed iter_mut is deferred by design (lowering.rs comment) yet typecheck-accepted. Chose codegen loud-bail (consistent with interp) over a premature feature implementation.

title: Implement `for x in xs.iter_mut()` end-to-end: (interp) add an `iter_mut` dispatch arm that yields a mutable reference to each element so `*x = …` writes back into the Vec; (codegen) peel `iter_mut` like `iter` in control_flow_for.rs but bind the loop element as a `mut ref` (a pointer into the Vec's `{ptr,len,cap}` storage at `data + i*stride`) rather than by value, and route `*x = …` deref-assignment to that pointer. The typechecker already types the element as `mut ref T` (lowering.rs). Until then, both backends fail loudly (B-2026-07-14-9) and the workaround is an index loop `for i in 0..xs.len() { xs[i] = … }`. Applies to Vec (and by extension Slice / VecDeque). Cross-check leak/drop behavior for heap element types under ASAN once implemented. PROGRESS 2026-07-14 (7d88499): the INTERPRETER now implements `for x in xs.iter_mut()` — a new `Value::VecSlotRef { storage, index }` (holding the element storage's shared `Arc<RwLock<Vec<Value>>>` handle directly) is yielded per element; `Env::get` auto-derefs it to the live element and `Env::set` writes through to `storage[index]`, so `*x = …` / `*x += 1` land in the live Vec (same choke-point treatment as `MapSlotRef`). The for-loop intercepts a `<vec>.iter_mut()` iterable and materializes the slot-refs instead of value copies. Verified via `test_for_iter_mut` (deref-assign, compound `*x += 1`, second pass, String element); usable now via `karac run --interp`. STILL OPEN: the CODEGEN (`karac build`/JIT) lowering — bind the loop element as a `mut ref` (pointer into `data + i*stride`) and route `*x = …` deref-assignment to it (control_flow_for.rs); it currently bails loud with a message that now points at `--interp`. Heap-element leak/drop behaviour under ASAN to be cross-checked when the codegen leg lands. CODEGEN LEG DONE 2026-07-14 (a9ea16e) — B-10 is now FIXED end-to-end. `karac build`/JIT lowers `for x in xs.iter_mut()` for a named Vec binding with a SCALAR element and a simple loop variable (`compile_for_vec_var_iter_mut`, control_flow_for.rs): the loop variable is bound as a MUT-REF slot pointer into the Vec's storage (`data + i*stride`, restored per iteration) and registered in `entry_slot_ref_vars`, so the existing deref machinery routes `*x` reads, `*x = v` stores, and `*x += 1` compound stores through the live element pointer — writes land in place. Verified interp==JIT (i64 + f64, `*x =` and `*x +=`, two sequential passes), stable 12/12 + valgrind-clean over a 500-element loop, and CORRECT under a default auto-par build with an independent sibling group (the B-2026-07-14-17 hazard class). Regression: codegen `test_e2e_for_iter_mut_scalar` + interp `test_for_iter_mut`. RESIDUAL: heap (String/Vec/struct) elements and destructure patterns bail LOUD to `--interp` (which handles all shapes) — a heap element written through the ref needs the old payload dropped first, the same deferred heap leg the Option/Result combinator codegen shares.
investigation: 2026-07-14: split out of B-2026-07-14-9. The by-value-vs-by-ref element binding already exists for the read `.iter()` path (compile_for_vec_var binds Copy scalars by value); iter_mut needs the pointer-binding variant plus deref-store lowering. The typechecker/lowering already models the `mut ref T` element type, so the work is backend-only.

title: `Vec[Vec[T]].get(i).unwrap()` loses the inner `Vec[T]` type in codegen: a subsequent `.len()`/`.get()`/index on the result fails LOUD with `no handler for method 'len' on variable 'row'` (bound) / `on non-identifier receiver` (inline). The interpreter handles it (oracle sum=33). Precisely isolated — these WORK: `g[i].len()` (index), `let row = g[i]; row.len()` (index bind), and even plain `let o: Option[Vec[i64]] = Some(v); o.unwrap().len()` (explicitly-typed Option-of-Vec unwrap). Only the chain where the Option comes FROM `.get(i)` on a nested Vec fails: codegen does not derive that `Vec[Vec[T]].get(i)` yields `Option[Vec[T]]` and thus `.unwrap()` yields a `Vec[T]`, so the binding is never registered in `vec_elem_types` and method dispatch on it falls through. FIX DIRECTION: thread the outer Vec's element type through the `.get()`→`Option[elem]`→`.unwrap()`→`elem` chain when registering the let-binding / inline-receiver type (the typechecker's `expr_types` already carries the correct `Vec[i64]` at the `.unwrap()` span — codegen should consult it to register the Vec, same shape as B-13-2/B-13-10 heap-binding threading). LOUD error, not a miscompile; workaround is the index form `g[i]`. Companion known-limitation seen alongside: `-> ref T` method results (`box.get()`) must be `let`-bound before use (B-2026-06-07-5), also loud. FIXED 2026-07-14 (0910b5f): Vec/Slice `.get`/`.first`/`.last` return `Option[ref elem]` and PACK the element VALUE, so the fix (a) reconstructs the `.unwrap()`/`.expect()` payload at the pointee's VALUE shape by peeling the `ref` when the receiver is a value-packing borrow accessor (calls.rs) and (b) registers the let-binding's collection type from the PEELED element (`borrowed_vec_get_unwrap_heap_inner`, stmts.rs) so `row.len()`/`.get(j)` dispatch, treating the shallow alias as BORROW-ELIDED (no scope-exit drop; the container stays sole owner - no double-free). This is the Vec sibling of the Map `get().unwrap()` B-2026-07-14-15 borrow-elision. Verified interp==JIT + valgrind-clean (no leaks/invalid-reads/double-free) for get/first/last on `Vec[Vec[i64]]` and `Vec[String]` (incl. heap-constructed strings); codegen (2349) + memory_sanitizer (707) green; the large_n sort_by struct-field tests stay green; fmt+clippy clean. Regression tests: codegen `test_e2e_vec_get_first_last_unwrap_heap_element` + ASAN `asan_vec_get_unwrap_heap_element_no_double_free`.
investigation: 2026-07-14: probing nested Vec via `.get().unwrap()`. `let row = g.get(i).unwrap(); row.len()` → codegen 'no handler for len on variable row'; `g.get(i).unwrap().len()` inline → 'non-identifier receiver'. Bisected against index form (works) and plain Option[Vec].unwrap() (works), pinpointing the loss to the `Vec[Vec].get()` element-type derivation. Filed as loud feature gap; deprioritized vs silent-miscompile finds.

title: A GENERIC function that consumes an owned HEAP param MORE THAN ONCE leaks exactly one heap buffer (the original param), in the AOT/native binary (interpreter is leak-free as oracle). Exhaustively isolated with valgrind (single-threaded, `definitely lost`, authoritative): LEAKS — `fn dup[T](x: T) -> Vec[T] { v.push(x); v.push(x); v }` with T=String (2 bytes 'hi'); `fn repeat[T](x: T, n) { while i<n { v.push(x) } }` (constant 1 block regardless of n≥2 — a 15-char string leaks 15 bytes, confirming it is ONE whole String, i.e. the original param, not a per-iteration leak). CLEAN — the same generic fn pushing x ONCE (x is MOVED, not cloned); the NON-GENERIC `fn dupS(x: String)` double-push; a generic param of STRUCT-with-Vec-field type (the struct arm of make_aggregate_param_callee_owned covers it). So the trigger is precisely {generic monomorph} × {owned builtin-heap param: String/Vec} × {used ≥2 times so it is CLONED per use, never move-consumed}. ROOT (hypothesis, from src reading — not yet IR-confirmed): on the mono path (mono.rs ~1724) an owned Path param routes through `make_aggregate_param_callee_owned`, which returns FALSE for builtin String/Vec (only user struct/enum get the entry-copy + tracked scope-exit drop) — so the generic String param gets NO callee-owned drop. When the param is used once it is move-consumed (its buffer transfers into the sink, balanced); when used ≥2× codegen defensively CLONES it at each push and the ORIGINAL param buffer is neither moved out nor dropped → leaked. The non-generic path avoids the leak (either it move-consumes the last use, or it tracks the String param's drop) — the two must be reconciled. FIX DIRECTIONS (both need ASAN/valgrind + the move-suppression pairing to avoid a DOUBLE-FREE on the move-consumed single-use case): (A) register the builtin-heap param's scope-exit buffer drop (track_vec_var/track_string_var equivalent) on the mono path, relying on the existing move-suppression to disable it when the param IS moved out — mirror whatever the non-generic path does; (B) make the generic param's LAST use a move rather than a clone (matches non-generic, also saves a clone). Must verify against the B-35 family regressions (return-owned-T-param double-free, B-2026-07-13-… ) since this is the same subsystem. NOT a miscompile (values are correct — `w.len()`==n, contents right); a pure leak. FIXED 2026-07-14 (6a51fe9): compile_generic_call now materializes a caller-scope drop for a fresh-heap String TEMP arg (a fn-return / non-binding), mirroring the non-generic compile_call — the mono clones a String param into its owned copy (and again when forwarding to the return), orphaning the caller's temp, which the generic path never dropped. Gated to String via string_typed_exprs (a named-binding arg keeps its own let-drop, excluded by expr_yields_fresh_owned_temp; a Vec[T] param temp move-aliases into the sink so materializing it would double-free). NOT under the flows_into_return passthrough guard, since the mono clones-not-moves the String even when forwarding it. CAVEAT: the filed dup/repeat examples multi-consume the param (v.push(x); v.push(x) / loop push) and are REJECTED by `karac check` (ownership: x moved twice) — so the production-reachable manifestation is the SINGLE-use temp (passthru(mk()), single push-into-container), which this fixes; a Vec[T]-param temp is clean when ownership-valid (the double-free only appeared on the ownership-rejected double-push, behind the check gate). memory_sanitizer regression added over both single-use shapes; interp==JIT + valgrind-clean; codegen (2344) + memory_sanitizer (702) green; fmt+clippy clean.
investigation: 2026-07-14: found probing `repeat[T](x, n)`. valgrind on the native binary: 2 bytes definitely lost for a String repeat; interp leak-free. Bisected: generic-vs-nongeneric (only generic leaks), push-once-vs-twice (only ≥2 uses leak), String-vs-struct-with-heap-field (only builtin-heap String/Vec leaks — struct is covered by make_aggregate_param_callee_owned's struct arm), loop-vs-straightline (both leak, so it is use-count not the loop). Constant 1-block leak scaling with the String's content length pins it to a single un-freed String = the original param. Read param_own.rs + mono.rs: make_aggregate_param_callee_owned returns false for String/Vec, so the mono owned-Path-param entry-copy+drop is a no-op for builtin heap params. Filed rather than fixed: the safe fix must pair callee drop with caller-side move-suppression to avoid converting the leak into a double-free on the single-use (move-consumed) path; high-risk area (the B-35 leg 3b was a return-owned-T-param DOUBLE-FREE), warrants dedicated IR-verified work.

title: A slice pattern (`[]`, `[a, b]`, `[first, .., last]`) matched on a `ref Vec[T]` / `ref Slice[T]` PARAMETER silently mis-dispatched in codegen — the wrong match arm ran, so JIT and native produced WRONG answers (or no output) while the interpreter (oracle) was correct. Isolated exhaustively: LOCAL Vec scrutinee and OWNED-param scrutinee both dispatch correctly; only the `ref`-param scrutinee is broken. Repro: `fn f(v: ref Vec[i64]) -> i64 { match v { [] => 0, _ => 1 } }` on an EMPTY vec gave interp=0 but JIT=1 (never matched `[]`); `match v { [a,b] => a+b, _ => -1 }` on `[3,4]` gave interp=7 but JIT=-1. ROOT: `resolve_slice_source` (src/codegen/control_flow_slice.rs) built the SliceSource by `build_struct_gep(vec_ty, slot.ptr, …)` directly on the variable's alloca. For a by-value/`let` Vec the alloca IS the `{ptr,len,cap}` struct, but a `ref Vec` PARAM's alloca holds a POINTER to the caller's struct — so the GEP read the borrow pointer's own bits as `{ptr,len,cap}`, yielding a GARBAGE length. The slice-pattern length check (compile_slice_pattern_condition) then compared against garbage and took the wrong branch every time. FIX (this commit): deref the borrow once (`build_load(ptr_ty, slot.ptr)`) when the scrutinee name is in `self.ref_params`, before GEPing data/len — the same `ref`-param deref pattern already used for SoA params (collections.rs). Applied to both the Vec and Slice arms. Verified interp≡JIT≡native on `[]`/`[a,b]`/`[first,..,last]` over empty/pair/longer vecs; LOCAL + OWNED-param cases unchanged (no regression); full codegen suite 2345 green. NOTE (separate, NOT fixed here): slice-pattern element bindings type as `ref T` and do not coerce to `T` in an arm body (`[x] => x` where the arm returns `i64` errors 'expected i64, found ref i64') — consistent across all backends (a typecheck/ergonomics gap, not a miscompile); left for a follow-up.
investigation: 2026-07-14: probing slice patterns, `fn describe(v: ref Vec[i64]) { match v { [] => .., [x] => .., [first,..,last] => .. } }` returned 'empty' for ALL inputs under JIT and produced no output under native, vs correct interp. Bisected scrutinee kind: LOCAL Vec (works), OWNED param (works), REF param (broken) — pinning the fault to the borrow deref. Read resolve_slice_source: it GEP'd slot.ptr unconditionally; the SoA-param path in collections.rs showed the canonical ref-deref. One-line-per-arm fix; ASAN/codegen-suite clean.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: autonomous dogfooding probe (slice pattern on ref Vec param, interp=oracle vs JIT/native) — SURFACE NOTE: codegen (slice-pattern match on borrowed scrutinee)

title: Two related slice-pattern typechecker ergonomics gaps, both CONSISTENT across interp/JIT/native (so not miscompiles — just friction). (1) BINDING TYPE: an element binding in a slice pattern types as `ref T`, not `T`, and does not coerce in the arm body — `match v { [x] => x, .. }` where the arm must yield `i64` errors `expected 'i64', found 'ref i64'`; the user must write `*x` or rebind. Arithmetic auto-derefs (`[a, b] => a + b` works), so it is inconsistent: `+` derefs but a bare tail/return position does not. Likely the same `ref T` element-binding shape as the for-loop borrow element, which DOES bind Copy scalars by value (lowering.rs `is_borrow_copy_scalar`) — the slice-pattern binder should apply the same Copy-scalar-by-value rule. (2) EXHAUSTIVENESS: `match v { [] => .., [head, ..] => .. }` is genuinely exhaustive (empty + non-empty covers every length) but the checker reports `non-exhaustive match: pattern '_' not covered`, forcing a dead `_` arm. Holds for owned Vec, ref Vec, and Slice scrutinees alike. The slice-pattern exhaustiveness logic does not model `[]` + `[_, ..]` (or `[_, ..]` + `[..,  _]`) as covering the length space. FIX DIRECTION: (1) apply the Copy-scalar-by-value binding rule to slice-pattern leaves (mirror the for-loop element binder); (2) extend match-exhaustiveness for slice patterns to recognize an empty-slice arm plus an open-ended `[head, ..]`/`[.., tail]` arm as total — carefully, since a WRONG widening here would ACCEPT a genuinely non-exhaustive match (soundness), so it must be conservative (only the exact `[] + [_, ..]` / `[_, ..] + []` complementary pair). Deferred rather than rushed for that soundness reason. FIXED 2026-07-14 (ffa33c3): Part 2 (exhaustiveness) — a conservative length-coverage recogniser (slice_patterns_cover_all_lengths, src/exhaustive.rs) accepts a Vec/Slice match whose IRREFUTABLE slice patterns tile all lengths (an open-ended [a..,..] covers [m,inf); every length in 0..m covered by a closed arm), run BEFORE the open-domain wildcard-required fallthrough. Sound: literal/nested-ctor elements don't count, so [head,..] alone / []+[a] / []+[5,..] still report non-exhaustive; operates on the lowered matrix so guards + variant-name element bindings are handled. Part 1 (element binds as ref T in tail position) was ALREADY resolved upstream (all repro variants pass). Regression + soundness tests added; typechecker (2039) + exhaustive suites green.
investigation: 2026-07-14: while fixing B-2026-07-14-13 (slice-pattern-on-ref-Vec miscompile), the reduced repros surfaced these two orthogonal typecheck gaps. Both reproduce identically under `karac check` regardless of backend, so they are front-end (typechecker), not codegen. Filed as ergonomics backlog; the exhaustiveness half is soundness-sensitive so it is explicitly NOT a quick widen.

title: CRASH: `let r = m.get(k).unwrap()` on a `Map[K, V]` whose VALUE is a NON-shared heap type (`Vec`, `String`) DOUBLE-FREES under JIT and native (`free(): double free detected in tcache 2`), while the interpreter (oracle) is correct. Binding ALONE triggers it — the result need not be used. Confirmed for `Map[String, Vec[i64]]`, `Map[i64, Vec[i64]]`, and `Map[String, String]`; `Map[String, i64]` (scalar value) is CLEAN; building/dropping the map without the get is CLEAN. ROOT: `map.get(k)` returns `Option[ref V]` (a BORROW of the bucket's value). For a heap value the `.unwrap()` let-binding `r` is registered as an OWNED Vec/String (gets a scope-exit buffer drop) but its `{ptr,len,cap}` is a SHALLOW ALIAS of the map's stored value — so at scope exit BOTH `r`'s drop AND the map's value-drop free the same buffer → double-free. (Scalar values carry no buffer, so no crash; that is why `Map[_,i64]` is clean.) The binding must be treated as a BORROW (no owned drop — the map still owns the buffer) OR deep-cloned. This is the NON-SHARED sibling of B-2026-07-14-3 (which fixed the SHARED-value map-get over-retain via `unwrap_receiver_is_shared_value_map_get` + `rhs_yields_fresh_ref`, stmts.rs) — that fix is shared-specific and does NOT cover a plain heap value. It is ALSO a sibling of B-2026-07-14-11 (`Vec[Vec].get().unwrap()`), but a DISTINCT symptom: B-11 fails to register `r` as a Vec at all → LOUD `no handler for method 'len'` (no crash); THIS registers `r` as a Vec AND an owned drop → silent-until-exit DOUBLE-FREE. FIX DIRECTION: at the `let x = <map>.get(k).unwrap()` binding (stmts.rs), when the map VALUE is a non-shared heap type, register `x` as a BORROW for method dispatch (so `x.len()` still works) but SUPPRESS the scope-exit buffer drop — mirror the borrow-return / `ref`-binding no-drop treatment. Deep-clone is the fallback if a borrow lifetime can't be guaranteed. NOT FIXED by me: this touches the same `.get().unwrap()` let-binding path the agent owning B-2026-07-14-11 is in — flagged for coordination to avoid a conflicting edit to stmts.rs. FIXED 2026-07-14 (51618aa): the `<map>.get(k).unwrap()`/`.expect()` bind on a non-shared Vec/String map value is now recognised (is_nonshared_heap_value_map_get_unwrap, stmts.rs) and treated as BORROW-ELIDED — the same no-owned-drop path a shallow-aliased v[i] element takes: the binding keeps its vec_elem_types registration (so r.len() etc. dispatch on the alias) but takes NO scope-exit buffer drop, so the map stays the sole owner and the double-free is gone. The borrow's lifetime is tied to the map by the ownership checker. Shared-value sibling (B-2026-07-14-3, rc_inc) and scalar values (no buffer) are excluded. Verified interp==JIT + valgrind-clean for Map[String,Vec[i64]], Map[i64,Vec[i64]], Map[String,String], Map[String,Vec[String]], scalar Map[String,i64], and .remove().unwrap() (owned, correctly NOT elided); memory_sanitizer regression added; codegen (2345) + memory_sanitizer (703) green; fmt+clippy clean.
investigation: 2026-07-14: found via a leak-check probe on `Map[String, Vec[i64]]`; interp printed the right answer, JIT/native aborted with a glibc double-free. Bisected: scalar-value map (clean) vs heap-value map (crash); build-only (clean) vs build+get (crash); bind-without-use STILL crashes (so it is the binding's registered drop, not a use). Mapped the family across Vec/String values and both key types. Confirmed distinct from B-11 (loud, not crash) and from B-2026-07-14-3 (shared-value refcount, not a plain-heap double-free). Filed + flagged rather than fixed, per the active two-agent split on the get-unwrap area.
