Minimal repro: `m.insert(1, DNode{...}); m.remove(1);` (discarded) leaks 24 bytes (one DNode box) under valgrind/`karac build`; the same program that instead binds `let removed: Option[DNode] = m.remove(1)` and matches it is clean. Confirmed the map's own DROP is fine (insert two, drop the map at scope exit — clean), so the leak is not the container teardown but the discarded remove-result. Root: `Map.remove` (maps.rs ~2060) returns `Some(old)` with the value moved out of the bucket (the runtime's `karac_map_remove_old` only frees the KEY buffer via `drop_key`, never the value — 'moved out into the returned Some(old)'), and codegen's expression-statement lowering doesn't emit a scope-exit drop for a discarded Option[shared] temporary. GENERAL SHAPE: any discarded expression statement whose value is `Option[shared]` / `shared` and which OWNS a ref (a move-out, not a borrow) needs a drop; Map.remove is the concrete instance found. FIX (deferred): drop a discarded expression-statement result when its type carries an owned shared/Option[shared] ref (emit the same RcDec/RcDecOption the let-binding scope-exit path uses). WORKAROUND (kata #146): bind the remove result and consume it via `match` (also the natural form when eviction needs the evicted key).
detail: SOURCE NOTE: kata #146 (LRU Cache). Class leak (discarded owned Option[shared] expression-statement result not dropped; Map.remove is the concrete trigger). Low severity: binding+consuming the result is a clean, idiomatic workaround, and the leak is bounded to the discarded-remove form. Map container drop and bound-result drop are both correct — only the bare `m.remove(k);` discard leaks. Not a regression.
resolution: Fixed (47f7940). Two coupled legs: (1) the DISCARDED form — a new `try_track_discarded_shared_option` in the statement-expression discard chain queues the standard tag-guarded `RcDecOption` at the `;` for an owned `Option[shared T]` temp; the payload type resolves from the span-keyed Option[V] record when present, else from the Map receiver's `var_elem_type_exprs` value record (a MethodCall node reuses its receiver-side span, so `m.remove(k)` has no span-table entry — the reason the general fix direction's 'emit the same RcDec the let-binding uses' needed a receiver-derived type source). MethodCall producers are gated to `remove` only: IR inspection showed a displacing `m.insert(k, v2)` releases its old value INLINE in the insert lowering (`map.ins.some` rc_dec) — a second dec would double-free. (2) the UNANNOTATED BOUND form, found during verification: `let r = m.remove(k)` (no type annotation) never registered the binding's Option[shared] scope-exit release either (builtin Map.remove has no `fn_return_option_inner_shared` entry, so let-case (b) missed) — leaked the bound box whenever the match arm only READ the payload; new let-case (b2) derives the shared info from the same receiver record. Valgrind-clean on the ledger repro, displacing-insert + absent-key + unannotated-bind combinations, and the annotated form; interp/JIT/AOT agree. E2E `test_e2e_discarded_map_remove_shared_value` + LSan `asan_discarded_map_remove_shared_value_no_leak` added.

title: AOT double-free: Vec[struct-with-enum-field] element bind -> ref-param call -> match on the enum field -> concat consumes the String payload binding. 19-line repro: `let t = v[0]; render(t)` where render(st: ref SpTok) matches `st.tok` and an arm returns `"id:".to_string() + name`. Interp correct; AOT aborts with free(): double free; `karac run` (JIT) exits 1 SILENTLY with no output (a third divergence surface). Element-bind aliasing family (B-2026-06-14-12 / B-2026-07-18-2): the element bind's deep copy of the enum String payload appears aliased with the container's copy, and the ref-callee's consuming concat frees it against the binder's drop.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: found by the Phase-12 emitter-port oracle work (Slice 33 nested-aggregate capstone smoke, 2026-07-21) — the SpannedToken shape. NOT nested-struct-specific: repro needs only { tok: Tok, n: i64 }. TWO independent triggers, both interp-green/AOT-double-free: (A) vec element bind + ref call + consuming match; (B) NO vec at all — `render(a); let b = a; println(render(b));` (ref-lend, rebind, second ref call — 26-line minA). For trigger A, ingredients all required (each removal goes green): (1) the struct comes from a Vec element bind `let t = v[0]` (a direct mk()/literal binding is clean, and a whole-struct rebind `let b = a` is clean); (2) passed to a `ref` param (matching the field in main directly is clean); (3) the match arm CONSUMES the payload binding via concat (name.len() is clean). Also note the silent-exit-1 JIT behavior with zero stdout/stderr — worse than a crash for diagnosability. Repro file preserved in the emitter-port session notes as min14.kara; full text in `investigation`.
resolution: [renumbered from B-2026-07-21-3 on 2026-07-21: duplicate id from a concurrent-session collision] Fixed (94cf1c4). Root cause (shared with B-2026-07-21-6): the match move-out source suppression resolved the `st.tok` place chain via `field_chain_place_ptr`, whose Identifier arm returned the raw variable slot for the ref-param root `st` — but a ref param's 8-byte slot holds a POINTER to the caller's struct, not the struct, so the `match.dest.suppress.wp` stores (three `store i64 0` at offsets 8/16/24) landed OUT OF BOUNDS in adjacent stack slots. Depending on opt-level/frame layout the corruption surfaced as this AOT double-free, -6's empty-string JIT read, or a silent exit 1. Two-part fix: (1) `field_chain_place_ptr` bails on a `ref`/`mut ref` param root (incl. `ref self`) — no caller may treat a borrowed root as an in-place suppression target (the callee doesn't own that storage); (2) an ESCAPING `match <refparam>.field { V(x) => <consume x> }` over a heap-bearing non-shared user enum now deep-clones the scrutinee (`clone_escaping_borrowed_ref_chain_enum`, the borrowed-chain sibling of `clone_escaping_owned_agg_loop_var_enum`) and rides the freshtemp enum drop-tracking: bindings own independent buffers, a no-bind arm frees the clone, and the caller's value is never touched — matching interpreter semantics. Read-only matches keep the zero-cost borrow-alias path (escape-gated). Note the escape detection counts string `+` as a move because concat desugars to `Call(String.add, [l, r])` and call args are conservative moves. Verified on both repros + minA + identity-return + no-bind + deep-chain + `ref self` + `mut ref` variants across interp/JIT/AOT-O2/AOT-O0 (all print id:foo etc.); E2E `test_e2e_ref_param_enum_field_payload_consume` + LSan/ASAN `asan_ref_param_enum_field_payload_consume_no_leak_no_double_free` added. Struct-typed-field sibling (struct PATTERN through a ref chain) was found pre-existing and filed as B-2026-07-21-7.

title: JIT-only miscompile: a match-bound String payload of an enum FIELD reached through a `ref` struct param prints EMPTY when an arm CONSUMES it via concat — `karac run` prints 'id:' where interp and AOT both print 'id:foo' (three-way divergence). 17-line repro: render(st: ref SpTok) matching st.tok, arm `head = "id:".to_string() + name`. Non-consuming uses (name.len()) are correct; heavier compositions (a Vec[SpTok] coexisting) degrade to a SILENT exit 1 with zero stdout/stderr.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: found alongside B-2026-07-21-5 during the Phase-12 emitter-port Slice-33 capstone (SpannedToken shape). DISTINCT from -3 (an AOT double-free needing a vec-element bind or lend-rebind-lend): this is JIT-only — interp green, AOT green, `karac run` wrong-output. Scoping: consuming concat of the payload binding is the trigger (name.len() arm is correct, min12); no Vec needed (min3/min9/minB all print 'id:'); adding a Vec[SpTok] + element bind escalates to SILENT exit 1 with no diagnostic at all (sptok3/jbis2) — whatever the root, `karac run` should never exit nonzero without a message. Probable relation: the JIT leg of the same payload-ownership confusion as -3 (the AOT leg double-frees, the JIT leg loses the buffer).
resolution: [renumbered from B-2026-07-21-4 on 2026-07-21: duplicate id from a concurrent-session collision] Fixed (94cf1c4) — same root cause and fix as B-2026-07-21-5 (see its resolution): the out-of-bounds `match.dest.suppress.wp` stores through the ref-param pointer slot zeroed the `name` binding's String alloca on this frame layout, so the consuming concat read an empty string under JIT ('id:' instead of 'id:foo'); other layouts double-freed (AOT, -5) or exited 1 silently. Fixed by the `field_chain_place_ptr` borrowed-root bail + the escaping ref-chain scrutinee deep-clone (`clone_escaping_borrowed_ref_chain_enum`). Both repros verified across all four backends; regression tests shared with -5.

title: Struct-PATTERN destructure of a struct-typed FIELD reached through a `ref` param double-frees when a binding escapes: `match h.inner { Pt { s, x } => return "p:".to_string() + s + ... }` with `h: ref Holder` aborts `free(): double free detected` under JIT and AOT (O0+O2); interp prints p:sp:7. The struct-leaf sibling of B-2026-07-21-5/-6: the bound field `s` bit-copy-aliases the CALLER's String and both the binding's scope-exit free and the caller's struct drop free the same buffer.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: found while fixing B-2026-07-21-5/-6 (probing sibling leaf kinds). Pre-existing, NOT a regression from the -5/-6 fix: verified double-freeing on the pre-fix compiler too (there via the same OOB suppress-store corruption; post-fix `suppress_destructured_struct_pattern_cleanup` cleanly bails on the borrowed root, leaving the alias + double free). The -5/-6 clone fix covers only a USER-ENUM leaf (`clone_escaping_borrowed_ref_chain_enum` gates on `enum_layouts`); a STRUCT leaf has no freshtemp drop-tracking channel to ride — a struct-scrutinee clone would need its own StructDrop registration + a per-arm suppression keyed on the clone alloca (new machinery, deliberately not bolted on in that slice). Read-only arms are fine (borrow classification covers them); only an ESCAPING binding (concat/return — note string `+` desugars to `Call(String.add, ..)` and call args count as escapes) hits the double free. Repro: struct Pt { s: String, x: i64 } / struct Holder { inner: Pt, n: i64 } / fn render(h: ref Holder) -> String { match h.inner { Pt { s, x } => { return "p:".to_string() + s + ":" + x.to_string(); } } return "?".to_string(); } / main: let a = Holder{..}; println(render(a)); println(render(a));  => interp p:sp:7, JIT/AOT-O2/AOT-O0 double-free abort.
resolution: Fixed (06ea22a) — the struct-leaf twin of the B-2026-07-21-5/-6 fix. An ESCAPING struct-pattern match over a pure FieldAccess/TupleIndex chain rooted at a `ref`/`mut ref` param now deep-clones the scrutinee (`clone_escaping_borrowed_ref_chain_struct`), registers the clone's own `StructDrop` (`track_struct_var`), and fires each arm's per-field cap-zero suppression against the CLONE slot (new `suppress_destructured_struct_pattern_cleanup_at`, factored from the #16 owned-place suppressor whose expr-resolving wrapper bails on borrowed roots by design). Bindings own independent buffers; unbound fields (incl. a second unbound String field) are freed exactly once by the clone drop; the caller's struct is untouched — interpreter semantics. Gated to: no Index hop (element sources belong to the #18/#38 machinery), every arm a Struct pattern of the leaf type or wildcard (a whole-value binding arm keeps status quo), and `borrow_payload_clone_supported` (never a partial clone). NOTE from verification: even the 'read-only' `s.len() + x` shape was double-freeing (JIT/AOT-O0), because the `iN.add` desugar makes the scalar `x` a call arg the escape walk conservatively counts as a move — the clone leg covers that shape too (correctness first; the spurious-clone cost for scalar-only escapes is a possible later refinement of `no_arm_payload_escapes`). Verified m7 + scalar-escape + identity-move + unbound-second-String + two-hop-chain variants across interp/JIT/AOT-O2/AOT-O0, all valgrind-clean; E2E `test_e2e_ref_param_struct_field_struct_pattern_consume` + LSan/ASAN `asan_ref_param_struct_field_struct_pattern_no_leak_no_double_free` added.

title: if-let over an enum FIELD through a `ref` param with a CONSUMING binding double-frees: `if let Ident(name) = st.tok { return "i:".to_string() + name; }` (st: ref SpTok) aborts free(): double free under JIT/AOT-O2/AOT-O0; interp prints i:il. The if-let ROUTE sibling of B-2026-07-21-5/-6: compile_if_let consults scrutinee_is_borrowed_binding/borrow_call but never the ref-chain clone legs the match path gained (clone_escaping_borrowed_ref_chain_enum/_struct), so the payload binding aliases the caller's buffer and both free it.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: probe pass 4 (2026-07-21) sweeping ref-param field-chain consuming reads after the -5/-6/-7 fixes. Repro p3: enum Tok { Plus, Ident(String) } / struct SpTok { tok: Tok, n: i64 } / fn render(st: ref SpTok) -> String { if let Ident(name) = st.tok { return "i:".to_string() + name; } return "+".to_string(); } / main: render(a) twice. while-let and let-else use the same bind path and need the same wiring check. FIX DIRECTION: wire the match path's ref-chain clone legs into compile_if_let (and siblings), with the escape scope being the then-block.
resolution: Fixed (5fa61ca) — and generalized past the filed if-let repro to ALL three single-pattern binding routes. The ref-chain clone legs are now escape-flag parameterized (`clone_escaping_borrowed_ref_chain_enum/_struct(escapes)`; the match site computes one shared `no_arm_payload_escapes` walk, single-pattern sites use the new `pattern_bindings_escape_in_block`). Wiring: (1) IF-LET — both legs before the freshtemp materialization (enum clone forces it via `did_clone`; struct clone's suppression fires on the clone slot then-arm only); (2) WHILE-LET — enum leg clones per HEADER evaluation (matching iterations ride the per-iteration freshtemp frame; the final non-matching evaluation's copy is freed wholesale on the miss edge via a new `force` flag on `drop_freshtemp_enum_scrutinee_on_miss`, since the fresh-temp gate would wrongly bail on a place scrutinee). The struct leg is deliberately NOT wired for while-let: a struct pattern always matches, making that shape a degenerate infinite loop, not an idiom. (3) LET-ELSE — both legs with an unconditional escape flag (bindings escape into the enclosing scope by construction, mirroring the existing `escape_exprs = None` clone convention there); the else edge diverges with the clone draining in its cleanup walk. Verified p3 (if-let enum), p3s (if-let struct), p7 (while-let enum, incl. Plus-token miss path), p8/p8s (let-else enum/struct) across interp/JIT/AOT-O2/AOT-O0, all valgrind-clean; E2E `test_e2e_ref_param_field_chain_iflet_whilelet_letelse` + LSan/ASAN `asan_ref_param_field_chain_iflet_whilelet_letelse_no_leak_no_double_free` added (the ASAN loop exercises the while-let miss edge per iteration).

title: match on an Option[String] FIELD through a `ref` param with a consuming Some arm double-frees: `match h.opt { Some(s) => return "o:".to_string() + s, None => … }` (h: ref Holder, opt: Option[String]) aborts free(): double free under JIT/AOT-O2/AOT-O0; interp prints o:op. The Option-LEAF sibling of B-2026-07-21-5/-6: the ref-chain clone leg gates to user enums (seeded Option has all-None drop kinds and no freshtemp channel), so the inline String payload binding aliases the caller's buffer and both free it.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: probe pass 4 (2026-07-21), repro p2: struct Holder { opt: Option[String], n: i64 } / fn render(h: ref Holder) -> String { match h.opt { Some(s) => { return "o:".to_string() + s; } None => { return "none".to_string(); } } … } / main: render(a) twice. Result[heap,_] fields presumably share the shape. FIX DIRECTION: an Option/Result-leaf clone leg — clone the instantiated Option value (payload te from the owning struct's field te), track via the FreeInlineOptionPayload channel, cap-zero the clone slot on consuming arms.
resolution: Fixed (c1cbed1). New `clone_escaping_borrowed_ref_chain_option` — the Option-leaf leg of the ref-chain clone family: gates on a pure FieldAccess chain rooted at a `ref`/`mut ref` param whose leaf field te (from the owning struct's field table) is an Option with an INLINE heap payload (`option_inline_payload_elem` — String/Vec/VecDeque; shared payloads bail to the rc machinery, boxed/Map payloads to their own cleanup families), plus the shared escape flag. Deep-clones the Option value via the dispatcher's tag-guarded `emit_option_value_clone_fn` and registers a `FreeInlineOptionPayload` on the clone slot; a CONSUMING `Some` arm/pattern zeroes the clone's TAG (`zero_refchain_option_clone_on_consume` → `zero_option_field_tag_at`) so the binding owns the payload, while `None`/`_`/`Some(_)` leave the cleanup armed. Wired into match, if-let, and let-else (while-let skipped — an invariant ref-field Option scrutinee is a degenerate loop). Verified across interp/JIT/AOT-O2/AOT-O0 on: consuming match/if-let/let-else, `Some(_)` non-consume, Option[Vec[i64]] payload with element read, None-holder paths, and caller reuse — all agree with interp; valgrind-clean (an initially alarming 'possibly lost 4 blocks' turned out to be the auto-par worker pool's pthread TLS — benign, reproduced with KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0 clean). Result[heap,_] fields remain on the status quo: the clone dispatcher has no Result deep-clone yet (noted in clone_drop.rs), so that sibling stays open territory if probing ever hits it. E2E `test_e2e_ref_param_option_field_consume` + LSan/ASAN `asan_ref_param_option_field_consume_no_leak_no_double_free` added.

title: match on a TUPLE-typed FIELD through a `ref` param with a consuming binding double-frees: `match h.pair { (s, x) => return "t:".to_string() + s + … }` (h: ref Holder, pair: (String, i64)) aborts free(): double free under JIT/AOT-O2/AOT-O0; interp prints t:tp:4. The tuple-LEAF sibling of B-2026-07-21-5/-6/-7: no clone leg covers a tuple leaf, so the String element binding aliases the caller's buffer and both free it.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: probe pass 4 (2026-07-21), repro p1: struct Holder { pair: (String, i64), n: i64 } / fn render(h: ref Holder) -> String { match h.pair { (s, x) => { return "t:".to_string() + s + ":" + x.to_string(); } } … } / main: render(a) twice. Medium (tuple struct fields are rarer than named-struct/enum fields). FIX DIRECTION: tuple-leaf clone leg — clone via the tuple clone/drop family (synthesize_tuple_drop_fn_te exists), track a TupleDrop-equivalent on the clone, per-element cap-zero on consuming arms.
resolution: Fixed (8c47c73). New `clone_escaping_borrowed_ref_chain_tuple` — the tuple-leaf leg of the ref-chain clone family: gates on a pure FieldAccess chain rooted at a SIGNATURE `ref`/`mut ref` param (the `signature_ref_params` subset from the -11 fix, so pattern-binding shims stay with their own machinery), the shared escape flag, a Tuple field te (from the owning struct's field table) with at least one heap element, and full clone-family support. Deep-clones via the dispatcher's per-element tuple clone, registers a tuple `StructDrop` (`synthesize_tuple_drop_fn_te`) on the clone slot, and consuming arms zero the consumed elements' caps in the clone (`zero_refchain_tuple_clone_on_consume` → `zero_tuple_elem_cap_at`) — a `_` element stays owned by the clone drop (freed exactly once; LSan-verified). Wired into match, if-let, and let-else (while-let: a tuple pattern always matches — degenerate loop, skipped like the struct leg). Verified consuming match, wildcard-element arm over a two-String tuple, if-let, let-else, and caller reuse across interp/JIT/AOT-O2/AOT-O0 — all agree, valgrind-clean. E2E `test_e2e_ref_param_tuple_field_consume` + LSan/ASAN `asan_ref_param_tuple_field_consume_no_leak_no_double_free` added.

title: whole-field `let` move of a struct-typed FIELD through a `ref` param double-frees when the copy's heap is consumed: `let p = h.inner; return "l:" + p.s + …` (h: ref Holder, inner: Pt{String,i64}) aborts free(): double free under JIT/AOT-O2/AOT-O0; interp prints l:ld:6. The LET-route sibling of B-2026-07-21-7: the field read through the borrow is a bit-copy alias, the binding gets owned struct tracking, and both it and the caller's struct drop free the same String.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: probe pass 4 (2026-07-21), repro p5: struct Pt { s: String, x: i64 } / struct Holder { inner: Pt, n: i64 } / fn render(h: ref Holder) -> String { let p = h.inner; return "l:".to_string() + p.s + ":" + p.x.to_string(); } / main: render(a) twice. An OWNED root's `let p = a.inner` deep-copies (n1-style shapes are clean) — the ref-param root misses that deep-copy but still registers the owned StructDrop. FIX DIRECTION: at the Let compile, a struct-typed FieldAccess RHS whose pure chain roots at a ref param must deep-copy in place (same clone family as the -7 fix) before track_struct_var.
resolution: Fixed (ca37738) — and generalized past the filed struct-field repro to every heap-bearing leaf. New `clone_ref_chain_field_move_rhs`, hooked right after the Let RHS compile in `compile_stmt`: a pure FieldAccess/TupleIndex chain rooted at a `ref`/`mut ref` param deep-copies the compiled value IN PLACE, so the binding owns an independent copy and every downstream registration behaves as if the RHS were a fresh owned temp (interpreter copy semantics; caller's field untouched). Leaves: user STRUCT (dispatcher clone), user ENUM (`deep_copy_enum_heap_payload_in_place` — seeded Option/Result explicitly excluded from this leg, the erased-layout any-heap gate would wrongly bail), String, Vec/VecDeque (full field te from the owning struct's field table so element types survive), and Option with an INLINE heap payload (dispatcher's tag-guarded Option clone; shared payloads stay rc-managed, boxed/Map payloads with their own families; Result stays status quo — no dispatcher deep clone). During verification the sibling String/Vec/Option let-move shapes were found equally broken (not just the filed struct leaf) and are covered by the same helper. Verified all six leaves across interp/JIT/AOT-O2/AOT-O0 with caller reuse — byte-identical to interp, valgrind-clean under KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0 (the auto-par pool's pthread-TLS 'possibly lost' is the known benign pattern). E2E `test_e2e_ref_param_field_let_move_all_leaves` + LSan/ASAN `asan_ref_param_field_let_move_no_leak_no_double_free` added.

title: Vec[String] field .first() consuming read through a `ref` param LEAKS the element copy at O0: `match h.items.first() { Some(s) => return "f:" + s, … }` (h: ref Holder) leaks one element-sized block per call under AOT-O0 (valgrind: 2 bytes x 2 for two calls); output correct on all backends; O2 elides the allocation.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: probe pass 4 (2026-07-21), repro p4: struct Holder { items: Vec[String], n: i64 } / fn first_up(h: ref Holder) -> String { match h.items.first() { Some(s) => { return "f:".to_string() + s; } None => { return "empty".to_string(); } } … } / main: first_up(a) twice. Low: bounded (one small block per call), O0-only in the observed shape, output correct. Likely the borrow-call clone-on-escape leg cloning s but the clone's free not firing on the return path (or a method-chain temp copy left untracked) — needs IR look.
investigation: INVESTIGATION UPDATE (2026-07-21, post-filing): re-diagnosed — NOT a ref-chain bug and NOT the element copy. The leaked block is the `"f:".to_string()` LITERAL TEMP in the consuming arm, and the shape reproduces with a plain OWNED local (`let v: Vec[String] = [..]; match v.first() { Some(s) => println("f:".to_string() + s) .. }` leaks 6 bytes at O0, no ref param anywhere) and with a `ref Vec[String]` param (4 bytes). Generic class: on the BORROW-classified match path (`scrutinee_is_borrow_call` — get/first/last), a `.to_string()` temp built inside a consuming arm and consumed by the concat is not freed on the arm's return/terminated edge at O0 (O2 elides the allocation). Bounded (one literal-sized block per call), output correct everywhere. Title's ref-param framing is superseded by this note; the fix belongs in the borrow-path arm-return temp drain, not the ref-chain clone family (whose -8/-9/-10/-11 fixes are unrelated to this residue).
resolution: Fixed (acd2ba3). Final root cause (completing the investigation note's re-diagnosis): the leaked blocks were the `\"f:\".to_string()` OPERAND temp and the CONCAT RESULT of a string `+` that stayed a surface `ExprKind::Binary` — the lowering's `String.add` desugar skips the rewrite when an operand is a ref-typed Vec-accessor payload (`Some(s)` from `v.first()`), and the whole temp-freeing economy was built around the desugared Call shape: the assoc-call route frees operand temps after the op, and every consumer site's `free_fresh_owned_str_arg` gate (`expr_yields_fresh_owned_temp`) admits only Call/MethodCall. The surface-Binary concat therefore leaked BOTH blocks once per evaluation (print-arg form: operand + result; return form: operand only — the caller consumed the result). Not opt-dependent in truth: O2 merely folded the allocations out of the repro. Two-part fix, both scoped to the vec-struct-shaped Binary-Add: (1) the Binary compile in exprs.rs frees fresh-owned OPERAND temps after the concat (mirroring the assoc-call route; expr gates + cap>0 leave identifiers/places/literals untouched); (2) `free_fresh_owned_str_arg` admits a vec-struct Binary-Add arg, so consumer sites free the concat RESULT exactly like the desugared Call — behavioral parity with the proven route at every site, deliberately NOT widening the shared `expr_yields_fresh_owned_temp` (20+ classification callers). Verified 12 shapes (return/print/bound-intermediate/nested concat, owned + ref-param + struct-field receivers, get/first/pop/Map.get scrutinees, plain-statement controls) — interp-matching output, valgrind-clean at O0 with auto-par off. E2E `test_e2e_surface_binary_string_concat_shapes` + LSan/ASAN `asan_surface_binary_string_concat_temp_no_leak_no_double_free` added.

tracker: src/codegen/vec_method.rs (Vec.push/push_back arg-retain: has Option[shared] binding/field retain via share_option_shared_ref_for_arg, but no retain for a BARE `shared struct` element aliased from an indexed Vec read)
title: `vec_field.push(nodes[j])` — pushing a BARE `shared struct` element read from another `Vec[shared]` (an aliasing indexed read, source still owns it) into a `Vec[shared]` does NOT retain (inc) the element. The container and the source Vec then BOTH reference the node at refcount 1; when the SOURCE Vec drops (e.g. a function-local `Vec[Node]` whose one node is returned), its per-element dec frees the node while the container still points at it — use-after-free / garbage reads under codegen. The interpreter (reference-semantic handles) is correct, so it is a silent run-vs-build divergence.
investigation: 2026-07-21: found re-verifying kata #133 (Clone Graph) — README only ever claimed `karac run` (interp). Under `karac build` both variants diverge (bfs panics `unwrap() on None`, dfs garbage). Reduction: `shared struct Node { val, mut neighbors: Vec[Node] }`; build a `Vec[Node]` pool, `nodes[0].neighbors.push(nodes[1])`, RETURN `Some(nodes[0])` (or push into an outer Vec) so the local pool drops. Minimal repro (rc.kara): after the block `keep[0].neighbors[0].val` reads 200 under interp, garbage/crash under build. If the pool Vec stays ALIVE (bg3: same push, read in-scope) the read is CORRECT — the fault is the missing retain, exposed only when the aliasing source is dropped. NOT caused by the 2026-07-19 weak-ref / indexed-read-offset work: `Node` is non-weak, non-headerless, so `shared_gep_layout` returns base 1 (identical to the old `idx+1`), and bg3 confirms the read offset is correct. Vec.push (vec_method.rs ~2422) retains Option[shared] bindings/fields (`share_option_shared_ref_for_arg`) + heap-closure envs, but a BARE `shared struct` element aliased from an indexed read has no retain arm. FIX (deferred): when the pushed arg statically types as a BARE `shared struct` AND is an aliasing read (indexed element / field / live binding, not a fresh `Node{..}` / call move-out), emit `emit_refcount_inc` so the container holds an independent +1 — the bare-shared sibling of the Option[shared] push retain.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: kata #133 (Clone Graph), re-verification. Class use-after-free (missing RC retain on push of an aliased bare shared-struct element; source-Vec drop frees the still-referenced node). HIGH severity: silent run-vs-build divergence with heap corruption on the canonical adjacency-list build (`node.neighbors.push(other_node)` where nodes live in a pool Vec). Pre-existing (kata interp-only from creation); NOT a regression from the weak-ref work (bg3 reduction proves the indexed read path correct). Repro reductions: rc.kara (fails: source dropped) vs bg3.kara (clean: source alive). FIXED a4a66c5: added `share_shared_struct_ref_for_arg` (bare-shared sibling of the share_option_shared_* push-retain family) — retains an aliasing Index/FieldAccess bare shared-struct push arg via emit_refcount_inc. Kata #133 bfs+dfs now run==build==JIT==Python; retain is balanced (acyclic LSan-clean; cyclic residual is the inherent RC-cycle leak, out of scope). Regression: tests/memory_sanitizer.rs::asan_push_aliased_bare_shared_element_retained_no_uaf; full memory_sanitizer 819 green.

title: match on a Result[String, i64] FIELD through a `ref` param with a consuming Ok arm double-frees under AOT (O0 and O2): `match h.res { Ok(s) => return "ok:".to_string() + s, Err(e) => … }` (h: ref Holder) aborts free(): double free; interp AND JIT print ok:rr (JIT survives by layout luck). The Result-LEAF sibling of B-2026-07-21-9 — exactly the open territory that fix's resolution flagged: the clone dispatcher has no Result value deep-clone, and the ref-chain clone legs gate Result out, so the inline String payload binding aliases the caller's buffer and both free it.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: probe pass 5 (2026-07-21) — the follow-up sweep the B-2026-07-21-9 resolution called for. Sibling probes CLEAN in the same pass: mut-ref write-back + consuming enum match (r2), struct-pattern Vec-field escape through ref (r3). FIX DIRECTION: mirror the -9 Option leg — a `clone_escaping_borrowed_ref_chain_result` gated on `result_inline_payload_elems` (inline String/Vec halves only; shared/boxed halves keep status quo), a Result-scoped in-place deep copy of the tag-matched half (the `deep_copy_option_inline_payload_in_place` word dance at Result offsets, via load_enum_word/store_enum_word + emit_vecstr_defensive_copy), tracking via `track_inline_result_payload_var` on the clone slot, and the consuming-arm disarm via the existing `suppress_inline_result_payload_cleanup_at`. Medium: Result-typed struct fields consumed through borrows are a plausible parser/self-host shape.
resolution: Fixed (3ea6b06). Implemented exactly as filed — the Result-leaf mirror of the -9 Option leg. (1) `deep_copy_result_inline_heap_halves_in_place` (param_own.rs): tag-guarded in-place deep copy of the LIVE half's `{ptr,len,cap}` overlay at Result words 1..3 (Ok and Err overlay the same words; two guards, each emitted only for a DIRECT inline-heap String/Vec half) via emit_vecstr_defensive_copy. (2) `clone_escaping_borrowed_ref_chain_result` (control_flow_match.rs): same strict FieldAccess-chain / signature_ref_params / escape gates as the siblings; per-half shape gate = direct String/Vec (non-shared element) or heap-free scalar — shared / struct-wrapper / nested-seeded halves keep status quo; clone slot registered via track_inline_result_payload_var, consuming Ok/Err arms disarm it with the existing suppress_inline_result_payload_cleanup_at (match / if-let / let-else routes all wired). ONE IMPLEMENTATION TRAP hit and fixed: the tracker must be called BEFORE the deep copy emits IR — its nested-block defensive zero-init keys on current-block != entry, and the copy's tag-guard blocks made that test fire spuriously, landing a zeroinitializer store in the ENTRY block between the value store and the tag read (clone wiped at runtime: 'err:0' + caller-payload leak on every backend). Verified: 10-shape battery (consuming Ok via return-concat x2 calls, Err-live holder, Result[String,String] both-halves-heap both-tags, borrow-only read, Ok(_) wildcard + scalar-Err consume, if-let, let-else + miss edge, Result[Vec[i64],i64] Ok(v) returned, two-hop o.inner.res chain, mut-ref receiver) — interp/JIT/AOT-O2/AOT-O0 parity + valgrind clean (with drain epilogues; see B-2026-07-21-15 for why they are needed). E2E test_e2e_ref_param_result_field_consume + LSan/ASAN asan_ref_param_result_field_consume_no_leak_no_double_free added. During verification the pre-existing struct-field Result payload scope-exit LEAK (independent of any match/borrow — `field_copy_supported`'s deliberate caller-retains exclusion of Result fields) was isolated and filed as B-2026-07-21-15.

title: a struct with a `Result[String, i64]`-class field leaks the live half's heap payload at the owning struct's scope-exit drop — `let a = Holder { res: Ok("rr".to_string()), n: 1 }; println(a.n.to_string());` leaks the 2-byte "rr" buffer (valgrind, AOT O0/O2). No match, no borrow, no call needed: the struct drop simply never frees a Result field's payload. The Option sibling is CLEAN (`Option[String]` field frees via the struct drop's OptionInline arm).
detail: SOURCE NOTE: isolated during B-2026-07-21-14 verification (probe pass 5 follow-up) — every ref-chain battery shape showed one caller-side leaked block sized exactly like the holder's payload, and the no-consume control (c1: construct + print a scalar field only) reproduces it, proving independence from the match/borrow machinery. ROOT CAUSE (by design, now promoted to a tracked gap): `field_copy_supported` (param_own.rs) deliberately returns false for EVERY `Result` field — 'stay caller-retains (this routine can't duplicate them, and the drop correspondingly leaves them excluded)' — so `aggregate_param_copy_supported_struct` marks the owning struct non-copy-supported, and `emit_struct_drop_synthesis`'s OptionInline pass (gated on that same predicate, and keyed to Some("Option") field names only) never classifies the field; it stays FieldDrop::None and the payload leaks wholesale at every scope-exit drop. The leak-vs-double-free tradeoff was the right call before an entry-copy existed; the -14 fix built the missing copy half. FIX DIRECTION (copy == drop, both sides together): (a) admit the narrow direct-String/Vec-halves Result class in `field_copy_supported` (mirroring the -14 clone leg's per-half gate), (b) entry-copy it in `deep_copy_one_aggregate_field` via the new `deep_copy_result_inline_heap_halves_in_place`, (c) extend the OptionInline classifier pass to Some("Result") fields (the drop fn already exists — `vec_elem_agg_drop_for_type_expr` routes Result to `emit_result_drop_fn`, proven on Vec elements), and (d) AUDIT every owned-struct field-move site (`zero_struct_field_move_cap` and the destructure suppressions) for a Result arm — flipping these structs to callee-owned without the move-site zeroing turns today's leak into tomorrow's double-free on `match holder.res { Ok(s) => return s }` over an OWNED local. That audit is why this is its own slice and was NOT folded into -14. WORKAROUND meanwhile: move the field out before scope exit (`let drained = holder.res;` — the binding's FreeInlineResultPayload frees it); the -14 tests use exactly this drain epilogue.
resolution: Fixed (ecf05ca). Completed the copy == drop pair for the DIRECT String/Vec-halves Result class (the -14 predicate `result_field_direct_vecstr_halves_ok` gates every leg, so wider shapes — shared/wrapper/nested halves — stay caller-retains exactly as before): (a) `field_copy_supported` admits the class (false under for-loop strict-shared mode, matching the Option arm); (b) the by-value entry copy duplicates the live half via the -14 `deep_copy_result_inline_heap_halves_in_place` (`deep_copy_one_aggregate_field` Result arm); (c) `emit_struct_drop_synthesis`'s OptionInline classifier pass now also admits Some("Result") fields, registering the existing tag-dispatched `karac_drop_Result_<ok>_<err>` (`vec_elem_agg_drop_for_type_expr` — proven on Vec elements) as the field's drop; (d) every whole/field move site zeroes the source payload area (`zero_result_payload_area`, now pub(super)): `zero_struct_move_caps` (whole-struct move) + `zero_struct_field_move_cap` (arg/field moves) + the #16 struct-pattern destructure arm lose their `fname != "Result"` exclusions, the let-destructure `transferable` gate admits the class with `track_owned_destructure_field_cleanup` registering the leaf's FreeInlineResultPayload, and the direct match/if-let/let-else + plain let/assign moves were already covered by B-2026-07-21-16's legs (built as groundwork). Verified: c1 (the filed no-consume repro) now valgrind-clean; battery of by-value passing (entry copy + caller retains), consuming match on a callee copy, fn-returned holder, struct move + consume, Vec[Holder] element, struct-pattern destructure with consumed AND unconsumed leaves, Err-scalar and Result[String,String] both-halves-heap holders — interp/JIT/AOT-O2/AOT-O0 parity + valgrind clean; the full -14 ref-chain and -16 owned-place batteries re-run green against the now-armed struct drop. Suites: codegen 2537/0, memory_sanitizer 829/0 (Linux LSan), interpreter 1287/0, selfhost_codegen (--features llvm) 1/0, clippy --all-targets clean, fmt clean. E2E test_e2e_struct_result_field_drop_and_moves + LSan/ASAN asan_struct_result_field_drop_no_leak_no_double_free added (single-use holders — the harness ownership gate rejects double-consume reuse; the reuse angle lives in the scratch battery). The -14 tests' drain epilogues remain valid (the -16 let leg makes them true moves).

title: match/if-let/let-else DIRECTLY over an OWNED struct's `Option[String]` field with a payload binding double-frees under AOT — `match a.opt { Some(s) => println(s), None => {} }` (a an owned local `H2 { opt: Option[String], n: i64 }`) frees the payload once via the binding's arm-exit cleanup and AGAIN via the struct drop's OptionInline arm (valgrind Invalid free; output correct — frees run at scope exit). Even a PRINT-ONLY binding arm reproduces. Same class: `let x = a.opt;` or `x = a.opt;` (assign) followed by consuming x. The Result sibling shapes are currently clean only because the struct drop skips Result fields entirely (B-2026-07-21-15's leak).
detail: SOURCE NOTE: isolated during the B-2026-07-21-15 fix-direction audit (the owned-struct move-site sweep the -15 filing called for) — probing what the Option machinery does on the shapes Result would inherit. Verified PRE-EXISTING (a733c33, 2026-07-18, reproduces) — not from the 2026-07-21 ref-chain work, whose clone legs gate on signature ref params and never fire for owned locals. ROOT CAUSE: B-2026-07-03-28 Facet A armed the struct drop's OptionInline free and zeroed the source tag at SOME move sites (#16 struct-pattern destructure, whole-struct move via zero_struct_move_caps, arg/field moves via zero_struct_field_move_cap) — but NOT at (1) a DIRECT variant-pattern match/if-let/let-else scrutinee over the field place (`match a.opt { Some(s) => … }` — the #15 route hands `Option` to the generic enum suppressor, which no-ops on the seeded all-None drop-kind layout), (2) the plain `let x = a.opt;` field move (the Let path registers ownership only for FRESH RHS shapes — Call / rhs_is_fresh_inline_enum — so the move neither zeroes the source nor arms the binding; balanced while unconsumed, double-free once x is consumed), and (3) the `x = a.opt;` assign move (same). Any binding sub-pattern counts — bindings on an owned-place Option-field scrutinee always register an owned free (print-only o6 reproduces). REPRO SET (scratchpad/b15): o1 consume-via-concat, o6 print-only, o5 if-let + let-else, o2/o4 let+consume vs bare-let-balanced, a1 assign+consume, o3 assign-out-of-arm; ro1 Result control clean (drop skips). FIX DIRECTION: (a) a consuming-variant-pattern place-source suppressor at the three pattern sites — pattern gates first (Some/Ok/Err with a binding sub-pattern), leaf `Option`/`Result` via place_chain_type_name, source ptr via field_chain_place_ptr (bails on borrowed roots — the ref-param case is the -9/-14 clone legs' territory), zero the Option TAG / Result payload area; (b) a let/assign move leg beside the #27 enum sibling (suppress_place_field_enum_move_source): zero the source and register the binding's own FreeInline{Option,Result}Payload so a later consume routes through the proven identifier-keyed suppressors. Result arms included from day one: harmless while the struct drop skips Result fields, load-bearing the moment B-2026-07-21-15 arms it. HIGH: memory corruption (abort under hardened allocators) on a completely mundane shape — read an Option[String] field of a local struct with a match.
resolution: Fixed (f9be2c7). Implemented as filed. (1) `place_optres_field_move_info` (control_flow_match.rs): shared resolver for the owned-place field-move legs — FieldAccess place, Option leaf with an inline non-shared String/Vec payload or Result leaf in the direct-String/Vec-halves class (`result_field_direct_vecstr_halves_ok`, extracted from the -14 clone leg so the two stay in lockstep), source pointer via `field_chain_place_ptr` (bails on borrowed roots — the -9/-14 ref-param clone legs' territory — and non-place roots). (2) Pattern leg `suppress_consumed_place_optres_field_source`: in the binding arm, zero the SOURCE (Option tag to None / Result payload area) so the owning struct's drop skips the payload the binding now owns; gated on the scrutinee's bindings actually owning their frees (!pattern_binding_is_borrow, captured while the classification is active — at the if-let/let-else sites the flag is restored before the suppressor cluster, so it is snapshot beforehand). Wired into compile_match / compile_if_let / compile_let_else beside the #15 suppressor. (3) Let leg `track_place_optres_field_move`: `let x = a.opt` now registers x's own FreeInline{Option,Result}Payload AND zeroes the source — the move is real, and a later consuming match routes through the proven identifier-keyed suppressors; also gives the -14 tests' `let dr = h.res` drain route a genuine cleanup registration. (4) Assign leg `suppress_place_optres_field_move_source`: source zero only (the target's let-site cleanup owns the moved-in payload; registering here would double up). Result arms are groundwork for B-2026-07-21-15 — harmless while the struct drop skips Result fields, load-bearing the moment it arms. Verified: full o1-o6/a1 probe set + ro1/c2 controls clean (interp/JIT/AOT-O2/AOT-O0 parity, valgrind), c1 keeps the open -15 leak (no move in it — out of scope), full B-14 battery re-run green through the new let leg. Suites: codegen 2536/0, memory_sanitizer 828/0 (Linux LSan), interpreter 1283/0, clippy --all-targets clean, fmt clean. E2E test_e2e_owned_struct_optres_field_consume_and_move + LSan/ASAN asan_owned_struct_optres_field_consume_no_leak_no_double_free added. Note on semantics: the zero makes a consuming destructure of a struct field a MOVE (later reads of the field see None/empty), matching the established #15/#16 move-suppression semantics for every other field class.

title: A runtime error raised inside a spliced gated-stdlib wrapper body reports the USER file's path with the SPLICE-COMPOSITE line/col — `import std.lazy.{lit}; lit(vec![1i64])` errors at `<user file>:19:5` when the user file has 6 lines (line 19 is the wrapper body's position in the composite spliced source, not a location in the file named).
detail: SOURCE NOTE: found probing LazyExpr.lit's non-scalar rejection during LazyDataFrame slice 6 (constant folding). The error MESSAGE is right and loud ('LazyExpr.lit expects a scalar literal (i64 / f64 / String / bool), got Array'); only the LOCATION is misattributed. Mechanism: gated stdlib modules (runtime/stdlib/lazy.kara et al.) splice their source into a composite before evaluation, and a runtime error whose span falls inside the spliced wrapper keeps the composite offset while the path renders as the user file. Any real-bodied gated wrapper that can raise at runtime hits this class (std.lazy's `lit` is just the first with a runtime-only failure mode — `col` cannot fail, and most gated wrappers delegate to typechecker-guarded builtins). FIX DIRECTION: either remap spans landing in spliced segments to the stdlib module's own pseudo-path (`<std.lazy>:14:5`), or attribute the error to the USER call site span (the arg expression) rather than the wrapper body.
resolution: Fixed (5d5361f). Root cause confirmed as filed, with one refinement: gated imports splice AST items cloned from each module's own SEPARATE parse (GATED_STDLIB_PROGRAMS), so spans inside a wrapper body carry the MODULE source's line/col (lazy.kara line 19 for `lit`'s body), and the CLI renders every runtime-error span against the user file's path — there is no textual composite. Fix takes the filing's second direction (attribute to the USER call site — the faulting argument's home — rather than a stdlib pseudo-path, which would have needed per-span module provenance Span does not carry): the interpreter keeps a stack of active spliced-wrapper call-site spans, pushed around the Value::Function body eval in eval_call when the callee item is stdlib_origin; record_runtime_error attributes a raise to the OUTERMOST frame when the stack is non-empty, so nested wrapper-to-wrapper calls still point at the user-visible entry call, and the error return trace picks up the same span. The stack pops on return: plain user-code errors and errors after a successful wrapper call keep their raise-site spans (both probed). Repro now reports `at <user>:5:13` (the lit(...) call) on error and trace. KNOWN RESIDUALS (same class, other executors — none observable today): spliced IMPL-block methods dispatch through eval_method_call (current gated impl methods cannot raise), and a user closure invoked INSIDE a wrapper would attribute its error to the wrapper call (no closure-taking gated wrapper exists). Suites: interpreter 1287/0 + new test, cli 490/0, codegen 2537/0, memory_sanitizer 830/0, clippy --all-targets clean, fmt clean. Test: test_stdlib_wrapper_runtime_error_attributed_to_call_site.

title: `if let Some(n) = v.pop()` / `while let` / `let…else` over a `Vec[shared T]` (or `VecDeque`) LEAKS the popped node — every element popped through a NON-`match` binding form leaks its refcount. `Vec.pop` is an INLINED builtin whose result is an owned `Option[shared T]` rvalue (the container relinquishes the slot via `len--`, transferring its +1 to the returned Option), but that inlined result never rides the general owned-temp-drop registration a real fn/method return does. The `match` scrutinee chain registered `track_freshtemp_shared_option_scrutinee` for exactly this shape; `if let`/`while let`/`let…else` stopped at the boxed-enum tracker, so the pattern bind's rc-inc + scope-exit rc-dec cancel and the transferred +1 orphans → the node is never freed. Codegen-only (interp/JIT correct output; AOT valgrind + Linux LSan). `match v.pop()` and `if let Some(x) = make()` (real fn/method return, caught by `materialize_freshtemp_enum_scrutinee`) were both already CLEAN.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: found by a valgrind/LSan leak sweep of the 78 shared/RC/weak-using leetcode katas (post-#133-fix regression audit). 2 katas leaked from this bug — #94 binary-tree-inorder-traversal/inorder_iter (explicit `Vec[TreeNode]` stack, `if let Some(node) = stack.pop()`) and #23 merge-k-sorted-lists/heap (`if let Some(x) = heap.pop()`); a 3rd finding, #133 clone-graph, is the SEPARATE by-design undirected-graph RC cycle (all-strong `Vec[Node]` neighbors, design.md 8856, safe/expected like Rust `Rc`). ROOT CAUSE: `compile_match` (control_flow_match.rs) runs a mutually-exclusive fresh-temp scrutinee tracker chain — materialize_freshtemp_enum_scrutinee (#1) → track_freshtemp_boxed_enum_scrutinee (#2) → track_freshtemp_inline_result_scrutinee (#3) → track_freshtemp_shared_option_scrutinee (#4), each gated on the prior returning None. For an `Option[shared T]` scrutinee #1/#2/#3 return None and #4 registers the RcDecOption cleanup that releases the transferred ref. `compile_if_let` / `compile_while_let` / `compile_let_else` (control_flow.rs) only ran #1 and #2, so #4 never fired for a non-`match` pop → leak. A real fn/method return was caught by #1 (its `Option[shared]` return type instance carries the droppable payload kind), which is why only the INLINED-builtin pop shape leaked and misdirected the bisection toward match-vs-if-let. FIX: mirror trackers #3 and #4 (with identical is-none gating) into all three non-match binding sites, and generalize `track_freshtemp_shared_option_scrutinee` to take `&[&Pattern]` (was `&[MatchArm]`) so if-let/while-let/let-else pass their single pattern. Verified: minimal pop (if-let/while-let/let-else) LSan-clean; #94 + #23 CLEAN; fn/method-return (`make()`, `b.make()`) still CLEAN (no double-free — #1 still owns those); #133 unchanged (its 240-byte residual is the true cycle). Regression test: tests/memory_sanitizer.rs::asan_iflet_pop_shared_struct_no_leak.
resolution: mirrored the match scrutinee's fresh-temp inline-Result + shared-Option cleanup trackers into compile_if_let/compile_while_let/compile_let_else; refactored track_freshtemp_shared_option_scrutinee to a patterns slice.

title: A nested `Option[shared]` FIELD reachable ONLY through a popped node leaks when the container is drained via `if let`/`while let`/`let…else` (but NOT `match`). `shared struct N { val: i64, mut nxt: Option[N] }`; `st: Vec[N]` holds node A with `A.nxt = Some(B)` where B is referenced nowhere else; `if let Some(n) = st.pop() { … }` frees A but leaks B (24 bytes). `match st.pop() { Some(n) => … }` is CLEAN (B freed). Build-and-drop without any pop is also CLEAN. So the container drop and the match path both recurse into the popped node's nested shared field; the three non-match binding forms do not. Codegen-only; AOT valgrind/LSan (output correct on all surfaces).
detail: SOURCE NOTE: uncovered during B-2026-07-21-18 post-fix verification (the same 78-kata shared/RC leak sweep). DISTINCT from -18 and NOT a regression from it: measured 24 bytes leaked BOTH pre-fix (587dc94^) and post-fix (587dc94) for the nested if-let case, whereas the FLAT case (`shared struct N { val: i64 }`, no nested field) went 16 bytes → CLEAN with -18. So -18 (flat popped-node leak) and this (nested inner-field leak) are independent. NOT hit by the current corpus: #94 inorder_iter and #23 merge-k both push AND pop every shared node individually, so no node is reachable solely via a popped parent's field — they verified LSan-clean after -18. This bug bites only the narrower shape where an inner shared node lives exclusively behind a popped node's `Option[shared]` field. ROOT-CAUSE HYPOTHESIS (unconfirmed): for an `Option[shared]` whose shared payload type has droppable fields, tracker #1 `materialize_freshtemp_enum_scrutinee` (→ track_enum_var) CLAIMS the freshtemp scrutinee in both match and if-let (so -18's tracker #4 never runs here), but the popped node's recursive field-drop only completes on the match arm; the if-let/while-let/let-else lowering either suppresses the payload's nested-field cleanup after binding, or frees the popped box without recursing into its `Option[shared]` field. FIX DIRECTION: compare compile_if_let/while_let/let_else's post-bind payload-cleanup handling against compile_match's Some-arm for a shared payload with a nested droppable field; ensure the popped node's drop path is the recursive rc-dec (emit_refcount_dec → __karac_rc_drop_N) in all four binding forms. Candidate: route Option[shared] scrutinees uniformly through the shared-option tracker (#4, recursive) instead of letting #1 claim them — but that touches the match path (currently clean), so guard against a match-path regression.
resolution: WITHDRAWN 2026-07-21 — NOT REPRODUCIBLE on main (391f7a0); measurement artifact from a STALE pre-rebase binary, not a real defect. Re-verified on a clean-built HEAD binary across a broad nested-shape battery — if-let / while-let / let-else / match, 1-to-3-level `Option[N]` chains, `VecDeque.pop_front`, and the inner-node-accessed variant — every case reports valgrind 'All heap blocks were freed -- no leaks are possible' under AOT (KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0), including the exact repros in the title. ROOT CAUSE OF THE FALSE ALARM: the 24/48-byte figures were read from the binary that produced the original B-2026-07-21-18 finding, which was compiled BEFORE the concurrent 2026-07-21 codegen fixes landing on main during B-18's rebase (b65ebf1 route-JIT-to-interp, f9be2c7 = B-2026-07-21-16 owned-place Option/Result field move-site zeroing, et al.) were integrated into the COMPILED binary. The rebase merged those commits into the source tree but karac was not relinked between the rebase and the leak measurement, so the numbers reflect my-B18-on-the-old-base, not integrated main. Once main was rebuilt with everything integrated, the nested leak was gone. IR cross-check confirms if-let and match emit an identical drop set (one binding __karac_rc_drop_N, one RcDecOption __karac_rc_drop_N on the freshtemp shared-opt inner ptr, the vec-element rc-dec, and the buffer frees) — there is no if-let-vs-match divergence to fix. No compiler change made; the B-18 fix (587dc94, in main) is what makes the shared-Option pop path count-correct for the nested payload too. Lesson logged: always rebuild karac after a rebase before trusting an AOT leak measurement.

title: Spurious E0500 UseAfterMove on a weak-to-weak field splice `nodes[i].next = nodes[prev].next` where both sides index the SAME `Vec[shared]` and `next` is a `weak` field. `karac check` reports "value 'nodes' moved here, used again here" (moved at the RHS `nodes[prev].next` read), but `karac build`/`run` compile and run it CORRECTLY and valgrind-clean (the reuse takes the advisory shared/RC fallback). The false-positive is specific to the extra `weak`-field access on the RHS: the strong-element form `nodes[i].next = nodes[prev]` (the #143 shape) is NOT flagged. Advisory only — ownership errors other than aliased exclusive borrows do not block the build.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: surfaced authoring leetcode #147 (insertion sort on a Vec-owned + `weak next` list, the #141/#142/#143 cluster). The canonical insertion-sort splice `node.next = prev.next; prev.next = node` lowers to `nodes[i].next = nodes[prev].next` — both sides indexing `nodes: Vec[Node]`, RHS reading the `weak next` field. MINIMAL REPRO (E0500): `shared struct Node { val: i64, id: i64, mut next: weak Node } fn main() { let mut nodes: Vec[Node] = Vec.new(); nodes.push(Node{val:1i64,id:0i64,next:None}); nodes.push(Node{val:2i64,id:1i64,next:None}); nodes[0].next = nodes[1].next; }`. CONTROL (clean, no E0500): replace the last line with `nodes[0].next = nodes[1];` (strong element RHS). So the classifier treats the indexed `weak`-FIELD read on the RHS as a Consume of the container `nodes`, colliding with the LHS index-assign into the same `nodes`; a bare indexed-element read is correctly non-consuming. Sibling of B-2026-07-19-3 (the owned-param `f(nums); f(nums)` UseAfterMove false-positive that got a machine-applicable `.clone()` auto-fix); this is a distinct trigger (compound index-assign self-reference via a weak-field read, no clean `.clone()` insertion site). FIX DIRECTION: in the use classifier, an indexed `<place>[idx].<weakfield>` read on the RHS of an index-assign into the same place root must classify as a non-consuming read (like the bare-element case), not a Consume. Kata #147 keeps the natural weak-to-weak splice and documents the advisory diagnostic (README), matching #137's treatment of the same error class.
resolution: walk_place's Index arm passed leaf_mode through the index unchanged, so a field-of-indexed-element read in consuming position (the assign RHS `nodes[j].next`) classified the container root as Consume. You cannot move out through an index projection (a partial move of an element the container still owns is disallowed), so the root below an index is always Read — force Mode::Reading there, mirroring the bare-index walk_expr arm. src/use_classifier.rs.

title: Materializing a `weak`-field read into a strong `Option[shared]` local and then storing it back into another `weak` field DOUBLE-FREES / use-after-frees. `let after: Option[Node] = nodes[prev].next; nodes[i].next = after;` (`next` is a `weak Node` field) `check`s clean but leaks the upgraded node (40 bytes for a single splice) and, across multiple such splices, corrupts the heap — valgrind reports 'Invalid read of size 8' (use-after-free) and the fuller workload aborts with 'free(): double free detected'. The weak->strong upgrade rc-incs the node, but the subsequent store of that strong `Option` into a `weak` field does not balance against the temp's scope-exit drop, so the node is over-released and later reads/frees hit freed memory. Codegen-only (interp/JIT output correct); AOT valgrind + glibc double-free abort.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: surfaced authoring leetcode #147 as the STRONG-round-trip alternative to the weak-to-weak splice of B-2026-07-21-20. When the E0500 false-positive (-20) pushes an author toward the 'save the successor first' idiom `let after = prev.next; node.next = after; prev.next = node;`, that materializes the `weak` read as a strong `Option[Node]` and stores it back into a `weak` field — which MISCOMPILES. MINIMAL REPRO (leak, 1 splice): `shared struct Node { val: i64, id: i64, mut next: weak Node } fn main() { let mut nodes: Vec[Node] = Vec.new(); nodes.push(Node{val:1i64,id:0i64,next:None}); nodes.push(Node{val:2i64,id:1i64,next:None}); nodes.push(Node{val:3i64,id:2i64,next:None}); nodes[0].next = nodes[1]; let after: Option[Node] = nodes[0].next; nodes[2].next = after; }` -> 'definitely lost: 40 bytes'. ESCALATED REPRO (use-after-free / double-free): two materialize-and-store splices in sequence (`let a = nodes[0].next; nodes[2].next = a; let b = nodes[1].next; nodes[2].next = b;`) -> valgrind 'Invalid read of size 8' x2; the full #147 kata written this way aborts 'free(): double free detected in tcache 2'. ROOT CAUSE (hypothesis): the weak-field read upgrades to a strong `Option[shared]` (rc-inc, correct), but storing that strong `Option` into a `weak`-typed destination field must DOWNGRADE (store a weak ref, drop the strong upgrade's +1) — codegen instead appears to move/retain the strong ref into the weak slot AND still drop the temp, netting an over-release. Contrast: the weak-to-weak direct copy `nodes[i].next = nodes[prev].next` (no strong materialization) is memory-correct and valgrind-clean (that is what kata #147 ships). FIX DIRECTION: at a strong `Option[shared]`/`shared` -> `weak field` store, emit a downgrade (weak store, no retained strong count) so the source temp's scope-exit dec balances the upgrade; audit the assign-into-weak-field lowering for the strong-RHS case.
resolution: A weak-field read is a BORROW (no strong retain), so `let x: Option[shared] = node.link` (weak field) owns no +1, but the binding still queued a scope-exit RcDecOption via track_rc_option_var — an unbalanced dec that over-released the target (leak for one use; UAF/double-free across several). Case (a) (explicit annotation) assumed the RHS delivers an owned/balanced ref (true for a Call move-out or a strong Option[shared]-field read whose compile_field_access balances). Detect a weak-field-read RHS (new expr_is_weak_field_read) and set option_alias_needs_inner_inc so the existing case-(d) inner rc-inc balances the dec. src/codegen/{stmts.rs,expr_ops.rs}.

title:
test_e2e_f16_bf16_enum_payload_pack_unpack CRASHES on macOS arm64 (empty stdout vs expected '4
1
3.5
1.75
6
') while Linux arm64 AND x86 are green — the B-2026-07-20-12 f16-in-compound-enum-payload fix does not hold on Mach-O/Apple arm64; CI leg 'Codegen E2E (macOS arm64)' red across all recent main runs.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: CI triage 2026-07-22 (cloud session A) while landing the LazyFrame codegen twin — failure predates the lazy work (red back through 391f7a0 at least). Empty stdout = the built binary aborts/crashes before printing (wrong-value was the ORIGINAL B-2026-07-20-12 symptom; this is the harder sibling). Linux-arm64 E2E leg is GREEN, so it is Apple-arm64-specific (Mach-O / Darwin ABI or alignment), not generic aarch64 — half-float (f16/bf16) enum payload pack/unpack lowering differs somewhere Apple-specific (calling convention for half types on Darwin arm64 is a known compiler pain point). NOT reproducible in the Linux x86 dev container — needs a macOS arm64 machine or the CI leg itself for iteration. Cross-ref: B-2026-07-20-12 (fixed — x86-verified).
investigation: 2026-07-22 (cloud session): root-cause CLASS identified from the Linux x86 container via llc-18 cross-lowering of forced-aarch64-ABI IR (KARAC_FORCE_TARGET_ARCH=aarch64 + KARAC_JIT_RUNNER capture). LLVM 18's AArch64 backend cannot select ANY standalone fpext/fptrunc node touching bfloat: fpext bf16->f32, fpext bf16->f64 and fptrunc f32->bf16 all die at ISel ('LLVM ERROR: Cannot select: fp_extend'), even load-fed, on BOTH arm64-apple-macosx/apple-m1 AND aarch64-linux-gnu/generic (isolated 6-function llc probe). bf16 ARITHMETIC (fadd/fcmp/fneg bfloat) legalizes fine — the gap is exactly the conversion nodes (fixed upstream in LLVM 19). karac emitted those nodes at the print-widen path (format_f64_to_stack_buf 'f2d'), `as` casts, bound coercions, and mixed-width float-binop promotion. At -O2 the mid-end constant-folds this test program's bf16 machinery away on the container toolchain (why x86 AND Linux-arm64 CI are green and the bug never reproduced locally), but the macOS leg fails at RUNTIME with a successfully-built binary: the harness compiles in-process, so an ISel report_fatal_error would abort the whole test binary — 2546 sibling tests passed, so Darwin's homebrew-LLVM pipeline instead leaves some of the machinery live and lowers it to something that crashes (assertions-off LLVM release builds turn some legalization llvm_unreachable paths into silent garbage instead of a fatal). HARDENING LANDED: eliminate the node class from karac emission entirely — build_float_cast_bf16_safe (codegen/expr_ops.rs) routes every bf16 conversion through integer-level sequences (bf16->f32 = bitcast/zext/shl-16/bitcast, exact; f32->bf16 = round-to-nearest-even bias trick + NaN quieting, matching compiler-rt __truncsfbf2; f64->bf16 via f32), wired at all five emission sites; f16 (half) untouched — softPromoteHalf is mature. Verified: 4-backend x86 battery green on the repro + a cast-direction battery (wid/nar/nar32/mixed-binop/negative); forced-aarch64 raw IR of both programs now fully SELECTS at llc -O0 on both arm64 targets (previously fatal); IR pin test_ir_bf16_widen_to_f64_routes_through_f32 asserts no fpext/fptrunc-bfloat node survives codegen. The E2E test now asserts with child exit status + stderr so the macOS leg reports crash-signal vs clean-exit either way. Close awaits the macOS CI verdict on this push. Found along the way, filed separately: interp does not round `as f16`/`as bf16` to storage precision (B-2026-07-22-4).
resolution: FIXED across 75dfaca + 50e329e; macOS 'Codegen E2E (macOS arm64, LLVM 18)' leg GREEN on the 01c0201 run (first green since the B-2026-07-20-12 test landed). Ground truth came from the enriched E2E assertion (child status + stderr): the macOS 'runtime crash' was the LLJIT parity lane (KARAC_TEST_JIT=1) — the harness shells out to karac_jit_runner, which runs ISel at RUNTIME on the raw un-optimized module; the child died SIGABRT with 'LLVM ERROR: Cannot select: bf16 = fadd' on its own stderr while the parent captured empty stdout. The macOS job is the only aarch64 leg running the LLJIT step (ci.yml: x86 + macOS set KARAC_TEST_JIT=1; Linux-arm64 does not) — exactly the green/red split that made it look Mach-O-specific. Root cause: LLVM 18 AArch64 cannot select standalone fpext/fptrunc-bfloat nodes (verified both apple-m1 and generic v8a), and Darwin's homebrew build additionally fails `fadd bfloat` in common DAG shapes (fixed upstream in LLVM 19). Fix: karac emits NO bfloat conversion OR arithmetic nodes — conversions lower as integer sequences (bf16->f32 = bitcast/zext/shl16, exact; f32->bf16 = RNE bias trick + NaN quieting, matching compiler-rt __truncsfbf2; f64->bf16 via f32; 75dfaca), binops compute in f32 and round back once (bit-identical to LLVM softPromote), negation is an integer sign-bit flip (50e329e). Regression tests: IR pin test_ir_bf16_widen_to_f64_routes_through_f32 (forbids every bfloat conversion/arithmetic node on fn-boundary values), E2E test_e2e_bf16_arithmetic_compare_neg_through_fn_boundary (runs on both LLJIT parity lanes), test_ir_f16_bf16_arithmetic_lowers_to_half_and_bfloat updated to pin the f32-compute shape, and the original payload test reports child status+stderr on divergence. Verified: raw forced-aarch64 IR selects at llc -O0 on both arm64 targets (previously fatal); 4-backend x86 parity on three batteries; full suites + clippy/fmt green. Cross-ref: interp narrowing-cast gap B-2026-07-22-4 (fixed).

title: asan_closure_captures_heap_struct_returned_clean FAILS on the arm64 LSan CI leg (memory-sanitizer-arm64) while the x86 LSan leg is green — an arm64-ONLY leak (or arm64-only asan report) in the closure-captures-heap-struct-returned path; red across all recent main runs.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: CI triage 2026-07-22 (cloud session A); predates the LazyFrame twin work. The proof-of-existence precedent for arch-dependent leaks is B-2026-07-12-29 (shared-Vec index-assign leaked on arm64 only, balanced on x86 — fixed 63d618e); this is the same CI-leg split. The test is recent (closure/ref-chain fix series, B-2026-07-21-*). Repro needs an arm64 Linux box (scripts/lsan-local.sh is native arm64 per CLAUDE.md — a local-Mac session can run it) or the CI leg. Per CLAUDE.md the memory-sanitizer-arm64 job is non-required but is the PERMANENT gate for the arm64 leak class — do not close any closure-capture leak-class fix on x86 evidence alone.
resolution: Fixed (ad55064). RE-DIAGNOSIS: not arm64-specific and not closure-specific — the leak is a FRESH call-result struct temp read via field access in expression position (println(mk().s) / take(mk().s) / mkv().v.len() / even a scalar-field read println(mk().n)): nothing owned the temp aggregate, so every heap field leaked, including UNREAD ones. x86 -O2 DCE'd the dead allocations (green x86 LSan leg), arm64 -O2 did not (red arm64 leg); -O0 reproduces on plain x86 under valgrind — full local iteration loop, no arm64 hardware needed. The closure test failed because its consumers (println(f(..).s), fv(..).v.len(), match fe(..)) are exactly this shape; a plain fn returning the struct leaks identically. FIX: materialize + drop-track the fresh temp at the generic field-access compile (track_freshtemp_field_access_object — gated on expr_yields_fresh_owned_temp, non-borrow accessor, non-shared user struct); extracted field values are borrows for read consumers; MOVE consumers zero the accessed field in the slot via the staged freshtemp_field_access_slot side-channel (field-name + object-span matched): let/assign (consume_freshtemp_field_move; the assign's eager old-value free gains a staged-RHS arm — acc = mk().s also orphaned acc's displaced buffer), explicit return + fn tails, and consuming match/if-let/let-else arms (consume_freshtemp_field_scrutinee, kind-aware via zero_struct_field_move_cap). Verified on a 15-shape battery, 4-backend parity, valgrind clean at O0 and O2; suites codegen 2544/0, msan 834/0 x86, interp 1288/0, clippy/fmt clean; the previously red asan_closure_captures_heap_struct_returned_clean passes locally. E2E test_e2e_freshtemp_field_access_all_consumers + LSan asan_freshtemp_field_access_no_leak_no_double_free added (the arm64 CI leg remains the authoritative gate — awaiting its green on this push).

title: Mixed-name method chains hanging off an associated constructor failed codegen with 'no handler for method on non-identifier receiver' — `Command.new(p).arg(a).stdout(cfg)` (and any user twin like `B.new().with_x().with_y()`) built only when every chain link happened to share ONE method name.
detail: Two compounding gaps, both rooted in the method_callee_types span-collision class (parser sets MethodCall.span == receiver.span, last insert wins, so a chain keeps exactly ONE Type.method key). (1) type_name_of_expr's MethodCall arm resolved the receiver recursively via var_type_names, so a chain ROOT of the form `Type.new(...)` — a MethodCall whose receiver Identifier names a TYPE, not a variable — killed static type recovery for the whole chain. (2) try_compile_freshtemp_user_method recovered the receiver type ONLY from the span-keyed dispatch_key; in a mixed-name chain every link except the surviving one sees a mismatched key (filtered to None by the caller's method-segment guard) and bailed, so the call fell through every dispatcher to the loud 'no handler' error. Same-name chains (`B.new().bump(1).bump(2)`) worked by coincidence — the one surviving key matches every link. Discovered by the first chained `Command` builder the std.process codegen slice compiled.
investigation: A/B probes: identifier-receiver process calls compiled clean; the chained builder failed at the FIRST mixed-name link ('arg' under a surviving 'Command.spawn'/'Command.new' key). User-struct twin `B.new().bump(3).bump(4)` (same-name chain) compiled — confirming the name-coincidence mechanism, not a stdlib-registration difference.
resolution: Fix both halves generally: (1) type_name_of_expr resolves assoc-constructor chain roots through fn_return_type_names['Type.method'] when the receiver Identifier names a known struct/enum AND is not a live variable (shadowing keeps the variable path); (2) try_compile_freshtemp_user_method falls back to type_name_of_expr(object) when dispatch_key is absent/mismatched — the existing 'Type.method must exist as a declared fn' gate still guards against hijacking builtin methods, so the wider recovery cannot re-route Vec/String/Option builtins. Verified: full codegen suite 2546 green (no dispatch regressions), std.process chained-builder E2E interp==JIT==AOT.
fix: same commit as the std.process codegen slice

title: interp: `as f16` / `as bf16` casts don't round to storage precision — narrowing float casts are identity in the tree-walk interpreter, diverging from all LLVM backends
detail: `fn nar(x: f64) -> bf16 { x as bf16 }` + `println(nar(2.7))` prints 2.7 under --interp but 2.703125 (correct round-to-nearest-even bf16) under JIT/AOT-O2/AOT-O0; same class for f16 (interp 2.7 vs 2.69921875 everywhere else). The interpreter models all floats as f64 and treats float->float as-casts as identity (f16/bf16 'not distinguished' per the interpreter/method_call_tensor.rs comment), so any program whose observable behavior depends on narrowed storage precision diverges interp-vs-codegen. Fix shape: round through the target format at Cast evaluation (f32: `as f32` round-trip; f16: half RNE; bf16: high-16-of-f32 RNE — the same math codegen's emit_f32_to_bf16 uses). SOURCE NOTE: found while building the B-2026-07-22-1 cast-direction parity battery.
resolution: FIXED in 6a734aa. Both legs of the class: (1) suffixed narrow-float literals now round at creation in eval_expr (2.7bf16 -> 2.703125, 2.7f16 -> 2.69921875, f32 via the native cast), matching the constants codegen materializes; (2) cast_value gained f16/bf16 arms on the float-source AND int-source paths (int -> narrow float previously stayed Int entirely). Helpers: round_f64_via_f16 = software f32->f16 RNE (Inf/NaN/subnormal/overflow handled, no half-crate dep); round_f64_via_bf16 = f64->f32 then the RNE bias trick + NaN quieting — exactly codegen's runtime lowering (emit_f32_to_bf16), so cast results are bit-identical across interp/JIT/AOT. Residual documented corner: f16 goes via f32 (double rounding) — not constructible from practical decimal literals; bf16 arithmetic in interp still computes at f64 without per-op rounding (typed-value flow, not the cast/literal surface this bug filed). Verified: parity batteries green on all 4 backends; interpreter 1291/0, codegen 2551/0, msan 836/0; regression test test_narrow_float_literals_and_casts_round_to_storage_precision (tests/interpreter.rs).

title: runtime test test_try_wait_kill_reap asserts Unix signal-kill encoding (-2) unconditionally — red on every Windows CI leg (actual 2)
detail: The `Test (windows-latest)` leg failed `process::tests::test_try_wait_kill_reap` with `left: 2, right: -2` on every recent main run (feaa95b, 50e329e, 01c0201). Not a runtime bug: `pack_exit_status` faithfully reports what the OS hands `Child::wait()` after a kill, and the platforms differ legitimately — Unix `kill(SIGKILL)` leaves no exit code (`status.code()` None -> -1 -> encoded (-1<<1)|0 == -2), while Windows `Child::kill()` is `TerminateProcess(h,1)`, so the child exits with CODE 1 -> encoded (1<<1)|0 == 2. The test over-specified the Unix value. SOURCE NOTE: surfaced while verifying the B-2026-07-22-1 macOS leg; orthogonal to that bf16 work.
resolution: Split the final assertion by cfg(windows): unix expects -2, windows expects 2 (matching exactly what CI reported). Both encode 'killed -> not a success exit'; only the surfaced cause differs. Unix path still passes locally; the runtime `pack_exit_status` encoding is unchanged (it was already cross-platform-honest).

title: `s[a..b].to_string()` / `.clone()` — a `.to_string()`/`.clone()` METHOD CALL directly on a String SLICE fails codegen with "indexed-receiver method 'to_string' on 's' — element TypeExpr unknown (outer is not a tracked Vec/Slice/Array variable)", while the interpreter accepts it (a run-vs-build divergence). `s[a..b]` is a ranged index that produces a fresh owned String (compile_string_slice), but `compile_indexed_receiver_method` treated the whole `s[a..b].m()` as a container-element method call and looked `s` up in var_elem_type_exprs — a String isn't a tracked Vec/Slice/Array, so it errored. `s[a..b]` as a VALUE (let-bind, push_str, concat) already worked; only the direct method-call-on-slice form was broken.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: surfaced writing leetcode #151 (reverse words), whose natural word-collection is `words.push(s[start..i].to_string())` — slice a word out of the string and own it. codegen failed; `karac run --interp` produced the correct output, so a run-vs-build divergence. ROOT CAUSE: `compile_indexed_receiver_method` (src/codegen/calls.rs) handles `obj[i].method()` by resolving `obj`'s element type from var_elem_type_exprs and lowering an element pointer — correct for Vec/Slice/Array, but a String with a RANGE index is a substring (compile_string_slice), not an element access. The function had no string-slice arm, so it fell through to the element path and hit the 'element TypeExpr unknown' guard. FIX: since a String slice is ALREADY an owned String, `.to_string()`/`.clone()` on it is the slice value itself — detect a ranged-index receiver whose object is string-typed (the same `string_typed_exprs` gate `compile_range_index` uses to route String slicing) and, for to_string/clone with no args, return `compile_string_slice` directly. No leak (the returned String is the owned value the caller consumes). DEFERRED: other methods on a string slice (`s[a..b].len()`, `.bytes()`, `.starts_with(..)`) still need the receiver bound to a `let` first; a general string-slice-value method dispatch (hoist the slice into a synth String temp with scope-exit free, then dispatch) is a follow-up. Regression test: tests/codegen.rs::e2e_string_slice_to_string_method. Verified: kata #151 run==build==auto-par==interp==oracle, valgrind-clean; full codegen suite 2537 passed.

title: Index-assigning an UNTYPED float literal to an f32 Tensor element silently stores nothing under AOT: `let mut a: Tensor[f32,[2]] = Tensor.zeros(vec![2]); a[0] = 5.0; println(a[0])` prints 0 under `karac build` (interp: 5). The bare `5.0` literal defaults to f64, and the f64->f32 fptrunc on the tensor index-assign store path is dropped — so the element keeps its zeroed value. WORKAROUNDS that store correctly: an explicit `5.0f32` suffix, a matching f64 element, or a computed `(k) as f32`. i64 elements are unaffected.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: found while probing the transcendental-map vectorization slice (cloud session A) — a `t[0]=5.0; ...; t.map(|x| x.exp())` probe read all-zeros; narrowing showed the map/vectorizer is correct and the fault is upstream in the index-assign store. REPRO is map-independent: `t.sum()` (compile_tensor_full_reduce, never touches the map path) reads 0 too. Isolation matrix: `a[0]=5.0` f32 elem -> 0 (BROKEN); `a[1]=3.0f32` f32 elem -> 3 (OK); `b[0]=5.0` f64 elem -> 5 (OK); `u[0]=9` i64 elem -> 9 (OK); `for i {t[i]=(i+5) as f32}` -> OK. So the trigger is precisely: f32 tensor element <- f64 (untyped-float-literal) rvalue via `Index`-assign, where the implicit f64->f32 narrowing store is lost (both constant AND variable index). FIX DIRECTION: the tensor index-assign store lowering must fptrunc the rhs to the element type when the rhs is a wider float (mirror the scalar `let x: f32 = 5.0` coercion, which works, and the `as f32` cast path, which works). Likely in the Tensor `Index`-assign codegen arm (src/codegen — the element-store beside compile_tensor_map's data path). Interp is correct (dynamic coercion). HIGH: a silent wrong-value store on the flagship numerical type with the most natural literal syntax.
resolution: compile_tensor_index_store (src/codegen/tensor.rs) now coerces the rhs to the element LLVM type before build_store: sitofp for an int rhs into a float element, else coerce_scalar_to_type (the shared float<->float / int<->int width helper the scalar `let x: f32 = 5.0` path already uses). Test: tests/codegen.rs::test_e2e_tensor_f32_literal_index_store.

title: Reassigning a `mut String` STRUCT FIELD leaks the OLD buffer when the field's current value was set in a PRIOR function call. `s.buf = read4(s)` (buf: String field, via a `mut ref S` param) frees the displaced buffer correctly only when codegen saw the field assigned earlier in the SAME function body; when the field holds a heap String set by an earlier CALL and this function's first touch of it is a reassignment, no old-value free is emitted, so the old buffer leaks (one 8-byte block per such reassignment). Output is correct; codegen-only (interp clean); AOT valgrind/LSan. Sibling of the Vec[String]-reassign leak class (#126).
detail: SOURCE NOTE: surfaced writing leetcode #158 (Read4 II, call multiple times), whose essential state is a Reader struct with a `buf: String` chunk + a persistent `buf_pos` field; each read refills via `rd.buf = read4(rd)` when the buffer drains, and across calls the field already holds the previous chunk.
