MINIMAL REPRO (leaks 8 bytes x1): `struct S { src: String, mut pos: i64, mut buf: String, mut bp: i64 } fn read4(s: mut ref S) -> String { let n=s.src.len(); let mut chunk:String=""; let mut c=0i64; while c<4i64 and s.pos<n { chunk.push_str(s.src[s.pos..s.pos+1i64]); s.pos=s.pos+1i64; c=c+1i64; } return chunk; } fn consume(s: mut ref S, n: i64) -> String { let mut r:String=""; let mut t=0i64; while t<n { if s.bp>=s.buf.len() { s.buf=read4(s); s.bp=0i64; if s.buf.len()==0i64 { return r; } } r.push_str(s.buf[s.bp..s.bp+1i64]); s.bp=s.bp+1i64; t=t+1i64; } return r; } fn main() { let mut s=S{src:"HelloWorld",pos:0i64,buf:"",bp:0i64}; let a=consume(mut s,4i64); println(a); let b=consume(mut s,4i64); println(b); }` -> prints Hell / oWor (correct), valgrind 'definitely lost: 8 bytes in 1 blocks'. The leaked block is the FIRST chunk ("Hell"), displaced by the second consume() call's `s.buf = read4(s)`. NARROWING: the SAME reassign happening TWICE within ONE function call is freed correctly (a `while` loop that refills twice is clean); a struct with only ONE String field + a LOCAL buffer cursor (so refill happens at most once) is clean; the leak needs (a) the reassigned field to already hold a heap String from a PRIOR call, and (b) this call's first touch of the field to be the reassignment. So the old-value-free on a String field store appears gated on an intra-function 'field is currently heap-owned' fact that resets at function entry, instead of an unconditional cap-guarded free of the loaded old pointer. FIX DIRECTION: `compile_field_store` for a String (and likely Vec/Map) field should ALWAYS load+cap-guard-free the displaced value before storing the new one, regardless of whether this function assigned it — mirror the plain String VAR reassign path (which is unconditional and clean). Cross-check the many reassign paths (heap-env closure field, struct-var, Vec-element) so the unconditional free doesn't double-free a borrow. WORKAROUND for the kata meanwhile: none applied — #158 is DEFERRED pending this fix rather than routed around.
resolution: compile_field_store's mut-ref-param struct-field path stored over the field without freeing the displaced heap value; the old-value free was gated on an intra-function 'field currently heap-owned' fact that resets at function entry, so a reassignment whose first touch of the field is the store (the value set by a PRIOR call) leaked. Fixed by refactoring drop_old_plain_struct_field to take (struct_ty, base_ptr) and calling it from the mut-ref-param path before the store, mirroring the owned-struct path's unconditional cap-guarded free. Regression: tests/memory_sanitizer.rs::asan_mut_ref_struct_string_field_reassign_across_calls_no_leak (the Read4-II state machine, LSan-clean).

title: AOT double-free: a Vec-payload enum variant (Node.Nums(Vec[i64])) COEXISTING with a String-payload variant (Ident(String)), where a String-payload TEMP is passed to a ref-param consuming match AND a Vec-payload value flows through the same describe(ref) fn. 26-line repro (vpmin7): describe(Node.Ident("foo".to_string())) + let a = mk_nums(); describe(a) together abort with 'double free or corruption'; either alone is clean. Interp correct; JIT also aborts. Same mixed-str-enum+aggregate-payload family as B-2026-07-21-5.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: found by the Phase-12 emitter-port Slice-41 work (Vec payloads in enum variants). State-dependent interaction (frame/heap-corruption family): the Vec-payload path alone (vpmin6/vpmin8: direct bind, rebind, ref-param match, i64 OR String return) is AOT-clean, and the Ident-str-temp-to-ref alone (vpmin9) is clean — only their COEXISTENCE in one program crashes. The Kara emitter-port backend compiles the SAME shapes correctly (matches interp, valgrind-clean) — the port out-compiles the seed here (4th such finding). Enum layout in the seed for a mixed String+Vec-payload enum is the suspect. Repro in investigation (vpmin7).
resolution: FIXED in bc0e99d. Root cause: two coupled gaps in the auto-par move-hazard machinery. (1) `collect_move_hazard_locals` classified only String/Vec/Map/Set/Option/Result bindings as move-hazards, never a bare user enum/struct that transitively owns heap — so a `let a = mk_nums()` binding of a `Node` (heap-owning via its `Nums(Vec)`/`Ident(String)` variants) was untracked. (2) The `find_parallel_groups` guards de-parallelized only the CONSUMER of a hazard (B-2026-07-16-19); the PRODUCER stayed grouped. When the producer runs in a `__par_branch` worker its owned heap value is written back to the parent via the par-return slot (a {tag,ptr,len,cap} bit-copy), and a later sequential `let c = a` move + scope-exit drop then free the Vec buffer twice. Isolation: the String-payload `describe(Node.Ident(..))` sibling (seeds the par group) + the Vec-payload producer + the `let c = a` move must ALL be present; any subset is clean (no group forms / handled sequentially), and `KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0` fixes every variant. Fix: new `named_type_owns_heap`/`type_expr_owns_heap` helpers classify a heap-owning non-shared user enum/struct as a (non-wrapper) move-hazard (cycle-guarded variant/field walk), plus a dual `hazard_producer` seed+candidate guard that keeps sequential any statement binding a hazard local consumed-by-move later — purely conservative (declines parallelism, never introduces it). Verified: 4-backend parity on the vpmin7 repro (valgrind-clean); the producer no longer parallelizes while independent pure work still does; par_codegen 197/0, codegen 2559/0, memory_sanitizer 842/0 (new loop×200 ASAN gate asan_auto_par_moved_heap_enum_producer_no_double_free), concurrency units green; clippy+fmt clean. Cross-ref B-2026-07-16-19 (the Option/Result-payload sibling of this class).

title: An unknown associated function on a scalar primitive type — e.g. `i64.max_value()` (a Rust-ism; Kāra spells the constant `i64.MAX`) — passed `karac check` clean and then panicked the tree-walk interpreter (`unreachable!` "variable 'i64' not found; should be caught by resolver`) or failed codegen with a raw "no handler for method" error. A green-check-then-crash.
detail: Found by a run-vs-build parity probe. The typechecker's type-name-receiver associated-call path (`expr_method_call.rs`) has explicit arms for every valid primitive assoc fn (`parse`/`from_str_radix`/`from`/`try_from`; `.MAX`/`.MIN` are field accesses handled elsewhere). When none matched and `find_method` returned None, it FELL THROUGH with no diagnostic (the inline comment claimed a 'method not found diagnostic fires below', but for a primitive receiver nothing downstream fired — check went green). The interpreter then evaluated the `i64` receiver as a value → `eval_expr` hit the undefined-variable `unreachable!` (violating the 'every phase emits structured diagnostics, never just panic' standard); codegen emitted its loud 'no handler' error. Only scalar primitives were affected (struct/enum/String receivers do reach a real downstream diagnostic).
investigation: `karac check --output=json i64.max_value()` → zero diagnostics; `karac run --interp` → interpreter panic at eval_expr.rs:170; `karac build` → 'no handler for method max_value on variable i64'. `i64.MAX`/`.MIN`/`i32.MAX`/`i64.parse` all confirmed still valid (interp==build).
resolution: In the type-name-receiver branch, after the `find_method`-returns-None point, reject an unresolved assoc call when `type_name` is a scalar primitive (i8..usize, f32, f64, bool, char) with a clean `NoMethodFound` diagnostic ("no associated function '<m>' on type '<T>'") — primitives have no user-extensible impl surface, and every valid primitive assoc fn has an explicit arm above, so an unresolved one is genuinely undefined. Struct/enum/String keep the fall-through. Verified: clean diagnostic across check/interp/build, `.MAX`/`.MIN`/`parse` unaffected; full typechecker (2085) + interpreter suites green. Tests: `tests/typechecker.rs::test_unknown_assoc_fn_on_scalar_primitive_is_no_method_found` + `test_primitive_max_min_and_valid_assoc_fns_still_typecheck`.

title: Total-order float wrappers (F32/F64 shipped; F16/Bf16 planned) silently MISCOMPILE in codegen: `a > b`/`a == b` on a wrapper return const-0 (every comparison false; `==` true even for unequal), and `Map`/`Set`/`sort` with a wrapper key COLLAPSE (all keys compare equal -> `get` returns the last-inserted value). Correct ONLY under `karac run --interp` (tree-walk); `karac build` and the default `karac run` (JIT) produce WRONG answers. Pre-existing for the SHIPPED F32/F64; uncaught because there are ZERO codegen tests for the wrappers and the interpreter tests use the `run()` helper that bypasses typecheck (so they only ever exercised `.from` construction + Display, never comparison/map/sort).
detail: SOURCE NOTE: surfaced 2026-07-22 while implementing the phase-11 F16/Bf16 total-order wrappers (phase-11-stdlib-longtail.md line 20, 'same pattern as F32/F64'). Mirroring F32/F64 revealed that the F32/F64 wrapper feature itself does not work in codegen. REPRO (comparison): `fn main() { let a: F32 = F32 { value: 2.5 }; let b: F32 = F32 { value: 1.5 }; println(a > b); println(a == a); println(a == b); }` -> interp prints `true/true/false`, build prints `false/true/true` (every `<`/`>`/`<=`/`>=` is false, every `==` is true regardless of operands). REPRO (map): `let mut m: Map[F32,i64] = Map.new(); m.insert(F32{value:2.0},20); m.insert(F32{value:3.0},30); match m.get(F32{value:2.0}) { Option.Some(v)=>println(v), Option.None=>println(0-1) }` -> interp `20`, build `30` (last-inserted; keys collapse). IDENTICAL for F64 (no float-width coercion involved) and F16, so it is NOT the narrow-float-literal-into-field coercion bug (B-2026-07-22-7 class). A plain `#[derive(Hash,Eq)]` struct with an i64 field works as a map key in codegen (build `20`), so struct keys work generally — the breakage is specific to the wrapper's FLOAT field. ROOT CAUSES (three, all needed for a fix): (1) `a > b` on a wrapper is lowered by the typechecker to `F32.gt(a,b)` (a builtin-Ord method call). In codegen this reaches `compile_assoc_call` (via call_dispatch 2-seg path) and matches no arm, falling through to the const-0 unknown-callee tail -> every comparison compiles to `i64 0` / `false`. (2) The wrapper's codegen VALUE representation is opaque: it flows as an i64 payload, but neither loading the inner float from a spill alloca (reads the wrong bytes -> all-equal) nor synthesizing a `<operand>.value` field-access (errors `cannot resolve field 'value' ... type was not recorded for codegen`, expr_ops.rs ~834) yields the inner float. The baked wrapper struct's fields are not wired into codegen's field-access / hash / eq tables the way a user `#[derive]` struct's are. (3) `emit_cmp_fn_for_type_expr` -> `Body::FloatScalar` (vec_method.rs ~6673) uses IEEE `OLT`/`OGT`, which is a PARTIAL order (NaN incomparable, -0.0==+0.0) -> WRONG for the wrapper's total-order contract (NaN sorts last, -0<+0), and its float arm only lists `f32`/`f64` (no `f16`/`bf16`). FIX DIRECTION (a real multi-part codegen slice, NOT one line): (a) route lowered `<Wrapper>.<cmpop>` in compile_assoc_call to a TOTAL-order compare (`karac_float_cmp` on the inner float, then icmp-vs-0), which first needs (b) a reliable way to extract the wrapper's inner float in codegen (register the baked wrapper struct's fields for field-access, or intercept the wrapper value's known representation); (c) a wrapper-specific total-order comparator (do NOT reuse the IEEE FloatScalar) used by sort/SortedSet; (d) correct Hash+Eq lowering for Map/Set wrapper keys; (e) ADD codegen E2E tests (currently zero). INTERP GAPS found en route (all interpreter-only, folded here because fixing them WITHOUT the codegen fix would introduce a silent run-vs-build divergence): `value_compare` has no wrapper arm -> `Vec[F32].sort()` is a silent no-op; F32 `<`/`>`/`<=`/`>=` are missing from eval_ops (only `==`/`!=` present); the lowered `F32.gt` etc. are not in the interp `is_primitive` dispatch guard so `a > b` errors `path 'F32.gt' has no interpreter evaluation rule` under `karac run --interp`. NAMING NOTE for whoever builds this: the bfloat16 wrapper must be spelled `Bf16`, NOT `BF16` -- all-caps `BF16` classifies as Const-class under the CN identifier rules (a name whose alphabetic chars are all uppercase is a constant; lexer.rs classify_ident), so it is rejected as a type name; `F16` is fine (single leading letter -> CN-7 single-letter Type escape hatch, like F32/F64). design.md currently writes `BF16` in two places.
resolution: FIXED in cd78554. Root cause (codegen): the baked total-order wrapper structs `F32 { value: f32 }`/`F64 { value: f64 }` live only in the synthetic `std.prelude` module, which every codegen super-module assembly path drops (cli.rs) — so their StructDef never reached `register_struct_metadata`/`declare_structs`. Construction stored `i64 0` (the value vanished), `.value` errored 'type not recorded', and every lowered `F32.gt`/`.eq` hit the const-0 unknown-callee tail (assoc_call.rs). Fix: (1) seed F32/F64 as real `{ f32 }`/`{ f64 }` structs in `seed_builtin_struct_types` (the baked-stdlib-struct hook, covering build+run+single-file paths) so construction/`.value`/layout use the normal struct machinery; (2) intercept lowered `F32.gt|lt|ge|le|eq|ne` in `compile_assoc_call` and emit a TOTAL-order compare on the inner float — eq/ne on raw bits (bit-equality: NaN==NaN, -0!=+0), ordering on the monotonic key `bits ^ ((bits >> top) >>u 1)` (f32::total_cmp transform), signed-compared; (3) route F32/F64 in `emit_cmp_fn_for_type_expr` to a `TotalFloatScalar` comparator (not the derived IEEE field comparator) so sort/SortedSet/SortedMap order correctly; Map/Set hash+eq work via the seeded struct for normal values. Interpreter parity (its struct-literal form used the IEEE partial order, diverging on -0/NaN): `F32 { value: x }` now builds a `TotalFloat32/64` (like `F32.from`), `.value` reads the inner float back; added the missing `TotalFloat32` ordering arms in eval_ops, `TotalFloat32/64` arms in value_compare (sort was a silent no-op), and F32/F64 to the lowered-op is_primitive dispatch (eval_call + method_call). Verified 4-backend parity (interp/JIT/AOT-O2/O0) on comparison, `.value`, Map get, Set dedup/contains, sort, and the -0<+0 / -0!=+0 total-order edge. New tests (were ZERO): codegen test_e2e_total_order_float_wrappers, interp test_total_order_wrapper_compare_map_sort_interp_parity. Suites: lib 972/0, interpreter 1293/0, typechecker 2085/0, codegen 2559/0, memory_sanitizer 842/0; clippy(±llvm)+fmt clean. DEFERRED (documented, not user-visible for normal values): Map/Set with a NaN or -0 wrapper KEY uses the seeded struct's derived hash/eq (IEEE), so those pathological keys follow IEEE membership rather than the total-order bit-identity — the ordering/comparison/sort surface (the filed bug) is fully total-order-correct. The F16/Bf16 wrappers named as 'planned' in the title remain unimplemented (separate feature).
tracker: phase-11-stdlib-longtail.md line 20 (F16/Bf16 total-order wrappers) is BLOCKED on this.

title: Overwriting an existing key on a `Map[K, String]` / `Map[K, Vec[…]]` (and the parallel `Map.remove`) leaks the DISPLACED / removed old value's heap buffer when the `Option[V]` result is discarded with `let _ = m.insert(k, v)`. The insert arm loads the old value into a synthesized `Some(old)` payload nobody holds; only the shared/RC-value path dec'd it, so owned `String`/`Vec` values (which need a buffer FREE, not a refcount dec) fell through and leaked one buffer per overwrite. Output correct; codegen-only (interp clean). The owned sibling of B-2026-07-22-8 / the shared-V overwrite dec.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: surfaced by a post-hoc gap-probe sweep after the 156-170 kata batch (the shipped katas all used Map with i64/char values, never Map[K,String], so none exercised this) — writing the natural `Map[K,String]` idiom (memo cache / grouping) with a heap value and an overwrite. MINIMAL REPRO (leaks 8 bytes x1): `fn h(s:String)->String{let mut r:String="";r.push_str(s);r.push_str("-t");return r;} fn main(){let mut m:Map[i64,String]=Map.new(); let _=m.insert(1i64,h("aaa")); let _=m.insert(1i64,h("bbb")); println(m.len());}` -> valgrind 'definitely lost: 8 bytes'. Literals do NOT leak (rodata, cap==0, free skipped) — the leak needs a HEAP value (f-string / push_str-built / owned-param). NARROWING: only the `let _ = m.insert(...)` wildcard-let discard leaks; a BARE `m.insert(...);` expression-statement was already clean (its `Some(old)` Option temp is dropped by the general statement-result cleanup — and naively freeing there too DOUBLE-FREES, which an intermediate version of the fix hit). A BOUND result (`match m.insert(...)` / `let old = ...`) is correct (caller owns the old value). Vec[String] control (`v[0]=...`) was already clean (B-126 class). FIX: `compile_map_method` insert arm — in the discard path (`pending_map_insert_old_dec`), when V is an owned-heap String/Vec (`map_val_owned_heap_str_vec_for`, new predicate: value TypeExpr head is String/Vec and not a shared type), `free_str_vec_buffer_if_heap(old_val)` (self-guards on vec-struct shape + cap>0). The discard flag is now set for owned-heap V only on the wildcard-let form (bare Expr already handled), while the shared-V dec keeps both forms unchanged. Regression: tests/memory_sanitizer.rs::asan_map_string_value_overwrite_discard_no_leak (Map[i64,String] + Map[i64,Vec[i64]] overwrite loop + bound-result no-double-free guard). Map[K, Vec[String]] (deep) NOW HANDLED: the discard path routes owned-heap values through `reclaim_displaced_owned_map_value`, which prefers the per-value drop fn (`map_val_drop_fn_for_type_expr`) so a Vec[String] value deep-drops its inner Strings + outer buffer, falling back to the shallow free only for String / Vec[primitive]. Confirmed clean on Map[i64,Vec[String]] insert-overwrite AND remove. REMOVE SIBLING: `let _ = m.remove(k)` moves the value out into a discarded `Some(old)` with the same leak (Q-probe: 400 bytes over a 50-key drain); fixed identically in the `remove` arm (owned-heap free, wildcard-let gated; shared-V remove left unchanged as unverified). Regression test covers both insert-overwrite and remove.

title: Spurious `rc-fallback` (perf false-positive) for a `match`/`if let` binding that is CONSUMED EXACTLY ONCE, when the match sits inside a loop: `while … { match m.remove(k) { Some(g) => vec.push(g), None => {} } }` reports `RC fallback inserted for 'g' (direct re-use after consume)` even though `g` is a fresh per-iteration binding used a single time. Outside a loop the identical `match … { Some(g) => vec.push(g) }` is clean. Check still PASSES (rc-fallback is a perf diagnostic, exit 0) and output is correct — the cost is an unnecessary Rc on `g`.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: surfaced writing the map-of-lists variant of leetcode #49 (Group Anagrams, `Map[String, Vec[String]]`), whose extraction loop is `while j<order.len() { match table.remove(order[j]) { Some(g)=>groups.push(g), None=>{} } }`. MINIMAL REPRO (rc-fallback on `g`): `fn main(){ let mut m:Map[i64,Vec[i64]]=Map.new(); let mut v:Vec[i64]=Vec.new(); v.push(1i64); let _=m.insert(1i64,v); let mut order:Vec[i64]=Vec.new(); order.push(1i64); let mut out:Vec[Vec[i64]]=Vec.new(); let mut j=0i64; while j<order.len(){ match m.remove(order[j]){Some(g)=>out.push(g),None=>{}} j=j+1i64; } println(out.len()); }`. CONTRAST (all CLEAN): the same match OUTSIDE a loop; `if let Some(g)=make(){out.push(g)}` outside a loop; a bare `Option[Vec]` producer + match + push outside a loop. So the trigger is specifically the LOOP CONTEXT: the CFG/dominator RC predicate (`src/rc_predicate.rs` / the linear forward state machine in `ownership.rs`) treats the loop back-edge as making the single consume-site both C and U (block(C) and block(U) mutually non-dominating across the back-edge), when in fact `g` is re-bound each iteration and never lives across the edge. ROOT CAUSE HYPOTHESIS: the RC predicate does not model that a match-arm/`if let` binding whose entire live range is inside one loop iteration cannot alias the next iteration's binding — its def dominates its single use within the iteration. FIX DIRECTION: in the loop-of-consume rule, exclude a binding whose definition and (sole) consume are in the same loop-body region with no use on any path from the consume back to the loop header. Deferred (perf-only, not a correctness bug; the fix touches core RC dataflow with wide blast radius — filed open rather than rushed). WORKAROUND in the kata: none — kept natural; the kata passes `karac check` (the rc-fallback is a perf note, exit 0) and is valgrind-clean.
resolution: FIXED in 042f848. Root cause: the CFG builder (src/cfg.rs) introduced match-arm and `if let` pattern bindings via `note_local_introduced` alone, never recording a `UseKind::Define` use-site the way `let` and the `for` loop-var do. `loop_of_consume_candidates` (src/rc_predicate.rs) keys its 'freshly re-bound each iteration → not a next-iteration use-after-move' suppression on `Reassign`/`Define` markers in the loop, so with no `Define` for `g` it treated the single consume as re-entering a moved value across the back-edge and fired the rc-fallback. Fix: emit a `Define` for each match-arm pattern binding (at the arm entry, inside the active `@armN` rename frame so it shares the arm body's Consume identity) and each `if let` pattern binding (at the then-branch entry), mirroring `Let`. Purely a diagnostic/perf refinement — check already passed (exit 0, correct output); this just removes the needless Rc. A genuine loop-carried move (value defined OUTSIDE the loop, moved inside each iteration) is unchanged and still correctly fires (its `Define` is not in the loop). Verified: the repro + an `if let` variant emit zero rc-fallback notes while the genuine-move contrast still fires; 4-backend output parity (valgrind-clean); lib 972/0 (two new regression tests: cfg::match_arm_and_if_let_bindings_record_define_use_sites, rc_predicate::loop_of_consume_suppressed_for_match_arm_binding_in_loop), codegen 2559/0, memory_sanitizer 842/0; clippy+fmt clean.

title: Auto-par false-negative REGRESSION from B-2026-07-22-9: the new producer-side move-hazard guard de-parallelizes a heap-owning producer whose binding is consumed by an Option/Result COMBINATOR METHOD (`a.unwrap_or("x")`), even though a published par-return slot consumed that way is round-trip-safe (B-2026-07-17-4). Two `let a = first_word(..) -> Option[String]` producers with literal args stopped grouping, tripping `test_move_hazard_publish_only_option_calls_still_group` and reddening the Test job on ubuntu/macos/windows.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: caught by CI (Test job, all three platforms) on tip d3a3206; regression window is bc0e99d (B-2026-07-22-9) which added the producer-side guard. REPRO (the guarding unit test): `fn first_word(s:String)->Option[String]{ let words=s.split(" "); if words.len()>0 {Some(words[0])} else {None} } fn main(){ let a=first_word("aa bb"); let b=first_word("cc dd"); println(a.unwrap_or("x").len()); println(b.unwrap_or("y").len()); }` — the two producers must share a par group; post-bc0e99d they got []. MECHANISM: `find_parallel_groups`'s `hazard_producer[i]` fired when any later stmt's `consuming_hazard_reads` contained a name `i` introduced. `stmt_consuming_hazard_reads` marks an Option/Result (`hazards==Some(true)`) method receiver as consumed (the combinator family moves self), so `a.unwrap_or(..)` counted `a` — and the producer of `a` was declined. But that consume is exactly the case B-2026-07-17-4 made safe on a published slot (branch-side publish suppression + parent re-registration = one owner). CONTRAST (correctly still guarded): a bare user-enum producer (`let a=mk_nums()` -> `Node.Nums(Vec)`, a `Some(false)` hazard) consumed by a plain alias-move `let c=a` double-frees with the writeback and must stay sequential — that is bc0e99d's actual target.
resolution: FIXED in 7a73b9d. Added a `count_wrapper_method_receiver: bool` flag to `stmt_consuming_hazard_reads` gating ONLY the `Option`/`Result` combinator-method-receiver insertion. `analyze_function` now builds two per-stmt sets: `consuming_hazard_reads` (flag=true, drives the consumer guard, unchanged) and a narrower `moving_hazard_reads` (flag=false, excludes the safe wrapper-method consume). The producer guard in `find_parallel_groups` reads `moving_hazard_reads`. Genuine alias/owned MOVES (`let c=a` Let-RHS, owned-arg, struct/array/tuple element, for-iterable) are marked via flag-independent paths, so bc0e99d's protection is untouched. Verified: concurrency 130/0 (was 129/1); ASAN asan_auto_par_moved_heap_enum_producer_no_double_free ok (guard intact) AND asan_auto_par_published_option_string_slots_no_double_free_no_leak ok (re-parallelized path double-free/leak-clean under LSan-on-Linux); clippy -D warnings + fmt clean.

title: An early `return` out of a `for (k, v) in map` / `for x in set` loop leaks the `karac_map_iter_new` iterator handle. The sole `karac_map_iter_free` was emitted only in the loop's exit block; normal exhaustion and `break` branch through that block, but an early `return` routes to the function-exit cleanup drain, which had no record of the iterator. Output correct; codegen-only (interp is GC-clean). One 16-byte iterator block leaked per early return.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: surfaced by kata #211 (Add and Search Words — trie wildcard '.' DFS), whose recursive matcher does `for (_, child) in nodes[idx].children { if dfs(...) { return true; } }` — an early return out of a Map-field iteration, taken once per wildcard branch. valgrind on the built kata reported 10 'definitely lost' 16-byte blocks (one per search that hit an early return). MINIMAL REPRO (1 lost block): `fn first_ge(m: Map[i64,i64], t: i64) -> i64 { for (k, v) in m { if v >= t { return v; } } return -1i64; } fn main(){ let mut m: Map[i64,i64]=Map.new(); let _=m.insert(1i64,10i64); let _=m.insert(2i64,20i64); println(first_ge(m, 15i64)); }` -> valgrind 'definitely lost: 16 bytes in 1 block' at karac_map_iter_new. A loop that runs to completion was already clean, and `break` was already clean (break_bb == the loop's exit block, which frees). ROOT CAUSE: compile_for_map_var / compile_for_set_var (src/codegen/control_flow_for.rs) emit the single karac_map_iter_free only at exit_bb; normal exhaustion and break branch through exit_bb, but an early `return` routes to the function-exit cleanup drain (emit_scope_cleanup, start-frame 0), which had no record of the iterator handle. FIX: new CleanupAction::FreeMapIter{iter_alloca} (src/codegen/state.rs) storing the iterator handle in an alloca and registered in the frame ENCLOSING the loop — below LoopFrame::cleanup_depth, so break/continue (which drain only frames >= cleanup_depth) never touch it; only a full return/function-exit drain reaches it. exit_bb now loads the handle, frees it, and NULLS the slot, so the enclosing frame's normal fall-through drain no-ops (karac_map_iter_free(null) is a runtime no-op) — exactly-once free on every path (normal exhaustion / break / early return). Applied identically to the Set path (Set lowers to Map[T,()], same iterator). SortedMap iteration (the smf keys-buffer path) was verified to NOT leak on early return, so left unchanged. Regression: tests/memory_sanitizer.rs::asan_map_set_iter_early_return_no_leak (300x loop of a Map early-return helper + a Set early-return helper; LSan-gated).

title: F32/F64 total-order wrapper: `.value` field access on a match-arm binding extracted from a USER-ENUM payload falls through to the const-0 tail -> malformed IR / module-verification failure under `karac build` (interp correct). Followup to B-2026-07-22-11.
detail: REPRO: `enum Num { I(i64), F(F32) } fn show(n: Num) -> f64 { match n { I(x) => x as f64, F(f) => f.value } } fn main() { println(show(Num.F(F32 { value: 3.5 }))); }` -> interp prints 3.5; `karac build`/JIT fail with "Module verification failed: Function return type does not match operand type of return inst! ret i64 0 / double" (the F32 arm binding's `.value` access hit the const-0 unknown-field fallback, an i64 0, against the f64 return). NARROWED: it is SPECIFIC to the baked wrapper struct bound from an enum payload AND accessed in the arm. CONTRASTS THAT WORK (all build+run+match interp): (1) a plain user struct in the same shape `struct P { x: f64 } enum Num { I(i64), F(P) } ... F(p) => p.x` -> OK; (2) extract the WHOLE F32 in the arm and access `.value` OUTSIDE the match `fn getf(n) -> F32 { match n { ... F(f) => f } } ... let r = getf(..); r.value` -> OK. So the enum-payload match-arm binding of an F32/F64 doesn't get its wrapper type recorded for codegen field-access (`field_index_for`/`type_name_of_expr` on the payload binding), unlike a user struct. Cross-ref B-2026-07-22-11 (the wrapper codegen seed) which this extends; the wrapper works as a standalone binding, struct field, tuple element, fn return, Vec element, and Map value — only the enum-payload match-arm field access is gapped.
resolution: NOT the binding (the F32 payload `f` is a correct `{ float }` struct with `var_type_names["f"]="F32"`, and `f.value` extracts the f32 fine) but the MATCH MERGE: the `F(f) => f.value` arm yields `float` while the `I(x) => x as f64` arm yields `double`, so the phi's all-same-type check (compile_match) failed and the whole match fell to the `i64 0` placeholder -> `ret i64 0` against a `double` return. Added `unify_float_match_arm_widths` (control_flow.rs) — the float sibling of the existing `unify_int_match_arm_widths` — called in compile_match before the phi: it widens every narrower float arm up to the widest present (fpext is exact; the fn-tail `coerce_to_current_ret_type` re-narrows losslessly for a narrower declared return), routed through `build_float_cast_bf16_safe` so f16/bf16 arms never emit an unselectable `fpext bfloat`. Covers F32/F64/F16/Bf16 wrappers, by-value + by-ref scrutinee, arm ordering, and `.value` in arithmetic — all agree across interp/JIT/AOT-O2/AOT-O0.

title: A `Map`/`Set` value bound out of a USER-ENUM variant payload loses its container type for codegen method dispatch: `match v { Table(m) => m.len() }` fails 'no handler for method len on variable m' under `karac build` (interp correct). `Vec` payloads work.
detail: REPRO: `enum V { Table(Map[String, i64]) } fn describe(v: ref V) -> i64 { match v { Table(m) => m.len() as i64 } } fn main() { let mut m: Map[String, i64] = Map.new(); let _ = m.insert("a", 1); println(describe(V.Table(m))); }` -> interp prints 1; `karac build`/JIT fail with "codegen: no handler for method 'len' on variable 'm' (method dispatch fell through)". The Map binding `m` extracted from the enum variant payload is not registered in codegen's `map_key_types`/Map-var tables, so method dispatch can't recognize it as a Map. CONTRASTS THAT WORK: (1) a direct `let mut m: Map[..] = Map.new(); m.len()` -> OK; (2) a `Vec[String]` payload bound the same way `enum Node { Words(Vec[String]) } ... Words(w) => w.len()` -> OK (so Vec payload bindings DO get typed; the gap is Map/Set-specific). Likely the same match-arm-binding type-registration path that handles Vec/String/struct payloads misses Map/Set. Pre-existing (independent of the F32 work); found probing mixed-heap enum payloads (B-2026-07-22-9 family).
resolution: The via-ptr (`ref V`) fast path (`bind_pattern_values_via_ptr`) bound the single-pointer Map word as a bare ref-to-i64: `llvm_type_for_name("Map")` returns the i64 fallback, which MATCHES the payload word, so the `declared_mismatches_word` guard (which correctly defers Vec — its `{ptr,i64,i64}` type mismatches the word) never tripped, and the dispatch side-tables (`map_key_types`/`set_elem_types`) were never registered. Fix defers Map/Set-family payloads to the value-source path (`pattern_binds_map_set_payload` guard, mirroring the existing struct-payload deferral), which registers them via `register_var_from_type_expr` and — under a borrow scrutinee — correctly skips the scope-exit free. EXTENDED to the whole family: `SortedMap`/`SortedSet` share the K/V/elem extraction but the typechecker's `record_pattern_inner_type` arm and the by-value registration arm only listed `Map`/`Set`, so those legs failed the same way BY VALUE TOO (pre-existing wider gap). All four shapes agree across interp/JIT/AOT-O2/AOT-O0. NOTE: an enum holding a Map/Set still leaks the handle at scope-exit drop (the enum drop walker has no Map/Set arm) — pre-existing and independent, filed as B-2026-07-23-4.

title: Matching a fresh-temp `Result[_, _]` (a direct function-call return) whose extracted payload is a STRUCT with a heap field (String/Vec), and reading that field (`match f() { Ok(w) => println(w.s) }`), double-frees the field's buffer under `karac build` — a memory-safety bug in an extremely common pattern. interp is clean.
detail: Precise trigger (all three required): (1) the scrutinee is a FRESH TEMP — a direct `f()` call, not a bound `let r = f(); match r` (bound-local is CLEAN); (2) the payload is a STRUCT that contains a heap field, not a bare String/Vec (a `Result[String, _]` payload is CLEAN); (3) the arm READS the heap field into a value-consuming/temp context — `println(w.s)` triggers it; `println(w.s.len())` / a borrow-only read does NOT. `Option` is CLEAN (only `Result`). Detection is heap-state sensitive: glibc's tcache detector fires reliably for a String of length >= 2 and stays silent for length 0/1, but the double-free (UB) is present regardless. Mechanism (hypothesis): the fresh-temp `FreeInlineResultPayload` cleanup's struct-drop half (control_flow_match.rs::track_freshtemp_inline_result_scrutinee) frees the payload struct's heap field at scope exit; passing `w.s` as a `println` argument also drops that buffer (an aliased {ptr,len,cap}, not a deep clone). A plain (non-match-bound) struct `println(w.s)` is CLEAN, so the extra free is specific to the inline-result-payload binding.
investigation: Minimal: `struct W { s: String } fn f() -> Result[W, i64] { Ok(W { s: "boom".to_string() }) } fn main() { match f() { Ok(w) => println(w.s), Err(e) => println(e) } }` -> double free under build (String len>=2), clean under --interp. Bisected against bound-local, Result[String,_], Option, borrow-only read, plain-local-struct: all clean.
resolution: Root cause: an inline `Result` struct payload's heap field has two potential owners — the fresh-temp `FreeInlineResultPayload` cleanup (overlay / struct-drop half) and, for a bound payload, the wrapper binding — reconciled by a per-arm suppressor that zeroes the source payload area on a CONSUMING arm. The wrapper gate in control_flow_match.rs (`if !(borrow_only && wrapper)`) deliberately SKIPPED suppression for a borrow-only struct-wrapper read so the source frees it (`Err(e) => e.rejected.len()`, else leak). But `consume_class` scores a free-FUNCTION call ARGUMENT as entry-copied / non-consuming, so `println(w.s)` — a heap FIELD passed BY VALUE to a free fn, which MOVES the String into the callee and frees it — read as borrow-only, leaving the source drop armed to free the same buffer again. Fix: new `wrapper_arm_moves_heap_field_to_free_fn` (control_flow_match.rs) backed by `consume_class::binding_fields_passed_to_free_fn_arg` detects a `binding.heapfield` passed as a free-fn call arg and forces suppression, overriding the borrow-only wrapper skip. Whole-area suppression is sound: an inline Result/Option struct payload holds at most one String/Vec (two = 6 words, over the 5-word inline area). The genuine borrow-only read (`w.s.len()`) is unaffected and keeps the source armed (no over-suppression leak). Covers Ok and Err sides, `println` and user free-fns.

title: A generic fn whose return type PERMUTES the struct's type params — `fn swap[A,B](p: Pair[A,B]) -> Pair[B,A] { Pair { first: p.second, second: p.first } }` — miscompiles: the mono builds the returned struct literal with the INPUT layout `Pair[A,B]` instead of `Pair[B,A]`, failing LLVM module verification when A and B have different sizes.
detail: ROOT CAUSE: the struct's OWN param names (Pair[A,B]) collide with the generic fn's param names (swap[A,B]); codegen's `mono_struct_type_from_active_subst` substitutes Pair's DECLARED field TEs (`first: A`, `second: B`) through swap's active subst by NAME, conflating the two A/B namespaces, so it yields Pair[A,B] regardless of the permutation. The literal's true type `Pair[B,A]` is not span-recorded for a literal INSIDE a generic-fn body, so `struct_inst_mono_type_for_expr` returns None and the buggy active-subst fallback wins. Typed locals (`let a: B = p.second`) do NOT help. Only fails when the permutation changes the layout: `swap[i64,i64]` and a non-generic hand-written reorder both compile+run clean. interp unaffected. Correct fix: RECORD the literal's generic instantiation type expr (`Pair[B,A]`, abstract params) at lowering time so codegen substitutes it via the active subst — a cross-phase (lowering + codegen) change. Deferred to a dedicated slice.
investigation: Minimal: `struct Pair[A,B] { first: A, second: B } fn swap[A,B](p: Pair[A,B]) -> Pair[B,A] { Pair { first: p.second, second: p.first } } fn main() { let q = swap(Pair { first: 42, second: "x".to_string() }); println(q.first); }` -> 'Module verification failed: Invalid InsertValueInst operands'. swap[i64,i64] and non-generic reorder both clean. CODEGEN-SIDE CONFIRMED (2026-07-23, while clearing the -11/-12/-14 cluster): the fix is LOWERING-ONLY. The struct-literal path (exprs.rs:1065) already tries `struct_inst_mono_type_for_expr` (span record) BEFORE the buggy `mono_struct_type_from_active_subst` fallback. If lowering recorded the literal's ABSTRACT instantiation `Pair[B,A]` (swap's params) in `enum_inst_type_exprs[literal.span]`, codegen already resolves it correctly: `mono_struct_type("Pair",[B,A])` builds subst {A_pair->B, B_pair->A}, substitutes Pair's fields `first:A_pair`/`second:B_pair` -> `first:B`/`second:A`, then `llvm_type_for_type_expr` -> `llvm_type_for_name` resolves the abstract B/A through the active `type_subst` map (types_lowering.rs:2014) -> {String,i64}. So NO codegen change is needed and the naming collision is sidestepped (we never substitute Pair's declared fields through swap's subst directly). The ONLY missing piece is the lowering pass recording the abstract instantiation for a struct literal INSIDE a generic-fn body (today it records concrete-context literals only). RISK to scope in the slice: audit other `enum_inst_type_exprs` consumers (Option/Result/enum payload sizing, enum construction) so an added struct-literal record with abstract args can't be misread — though those key on enum/option literal spans, not struct-literal spans, so the blast radius looks small. Deriving the type from field VALUES instead is UNSOUND (a literal `5` into a concrete `i32` field would size the slot i64), so the abstract-instantiation record is the right mechanism.
resolution: ROOT CAUSE (corrected — the earlier lowering-only hypothesis was WRONG): the user's generic fn `swap` collides by NAME with the baked stdlib `mem::swap` `#[compiler_builtin]`. `check_items` skipped body type-checking via `env.compiler_builtins.contains(&f.name)` — a name-keyed set populated across user + baked stdlib programs — so the user `swap` body was NEVER type-checked and its `expr_types` were never recorded. That starved codegen's per-literal instantiation record (`enum_inst_type_exprs[span]` empty), so `struct_inst_mono_type_for_expr` returned None and codegen fell to `mono_struct_type_from_active_subst`, which builds the returned literal with the INPUT layout `Pair[A,B]` instead of the permuted `Pair[B,A]` -> LLVM module verification failure when A/B differ in size. The naming-collision-in-codegen-substitution story in the original detail was a red herring; the codegen substitution is never even reached because the abstract instantiation was never recorded. Empirically bisected: renaming `swap`->`flip` (no builtin collision) compiles+runs clean; instrumenting showed `check_function` fires for `main` but not the user `swap`, and the ONLY skip in `check_items` is the name-keyed compiler-builtin gate. FIX (one line, typecheck): gate the body-skip on THIS function's own `#[compiler_builtin]` attribute (`a.is_bare("compiler_builtin")`, the same predicate `env_build` uses to register it) instead of the cross-program name set. The real builtin is still skipped; a user function that merely shares a builtin's name is now type-checked. This also closes a broader soundness hole: any type error in a builtin-name-shadowing user function previously went unreported. Verified interp==JIT==AOT + full suites (typechecker 2088, codegen 2570, interpreter 1304, memory_sanitizer 850 LSan, par_codegen 197, cli 532, selfhost oracle).

title: SILENT MISCOMPILE in the selfhost codegen PORT (selfhost/src/codegen.kara emitter, NOT the seed): OR-PATTERNS `A | B | C =>` matched only the FIRST alternative's variant tag, so `A | B` behaved like `A` — e.g. is_kw(Plus) wrongly returned true for a `Fn | Let | If | Else` arm. The OrPat pattern was collected but only its first alt's tag drove the branch; the rest were dropped.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: this is a work-in-progress in the SELFHOST codegen.kara emitter (Phase 12 port), found by real-shape probing against the differential oracle, fixed in the same slice it was found (Slice 50). Filed retroactively for ledger completeness — the emitter emitted WRONG code with no error until the OrPat leg was written. Fix: emit_match's OrPat arm now collects every alternative's variant tag and ORs their icmp-eq tests into the branch condition. Unit-variant alts only (payload-binding or-alts out of surface). The seed's own codegen is correct here; this was purely the port's incomplete emitter.
resolution: Fixed in Slice 50 (990ba16): or-chain of per-alt tag equality tests.

title: SILENT MISCOMPILE in the selfhost codegen PORT (codegen.kara emitter): MATCH GUARDS `Pat if <cond> =>` were IGNORED entirely — the emitter always took the first tag-matching arm regardless of the guard, so `Num(n) if n > 100` fired for Num(3). Affected BOTH match paths (enum-variant match and int-literal match); the int-match guarded-wildcard case (a `grade(n)` shape) was a second instance in the same class.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: WIP selfhost codegen.kara emitter (Phase 12 port), found by real-shape probing, fixed in Slice 49. Filed retroactively for completeness. Fix: the guard is now evaluated AFTER the payload binds (it reads the bound vars) and, on failure, branches to the next arm (which may re-match the same tag with a different guard/none). Wired into all three arm kinds — enum-variant guards, guarded catch-alls (failure flows to the mdead fall-through, next arm continues), and int-literal-match guards.
resolution: Fixed in Slice 49 (73b3e69): guard eval + fall-through, both match paths.

title: SILENT MISCOMPILE in the selfhost codegen PORT (codegen.kara emitter): `loop {}`, `break`, and `continue` were UNHANDLED — a `loop { … break }` emitted a no-op returning 0, and a `while` with `continue` ignored the continue (ran the full body). The For arm handled only `.bytes()`; loop/break/continue had no emission.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: WIP selfhost codegen.kara emitter (Phase 12 port), found by real-shape probing (parser.kara uses `loop { … break }` heavily), fixed in Slice 48. Filed retroactively. Fix: a loop-label stack (loop_break/loop_cont, innermost last) resolves break->end and continue->the loop's continue target; for-loops route continue through an increment block so it skips the body remainder but NOT the step. Covers while/loop + break/continue inside for-loops.
investigation:
fn main() { let mut i = 0; let mut s = 0; loop { if i >= 5 { break; } s = s + i; i = i + 1; } println(s.to_string()) }
// port emitter before fix: printed 0; correct: 10
resolution: Fixed in Slice 48 (fa25a34): loop-label stack + increment-block continue targets.

title: SILENT MISCOMPILE in the selfhost codegen PORT (codegen.kara emitter): `for x in <vec>` element iteration was UNHANDLED — the loop emitted nothing/0 (the For arm handled only `.bytes()`), so every real vec traversal via a for-loop miscompiled. All prior corpus loops had sidestepped it with while-index loops.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: WIP selfhost codegen.kara emitter (Phase 12 port), found by real-shape probing, fixed in Slice 47. Filed retroactively. Fix: emit_for_vec loops [0,len) loading each element as a BORROW into the var slot (element kind by vec kind: Vec[i64]/Vec[String]/Vec[struct]/Vec[enum]); a heap-temp vec is freed after the loop. Range for-loops (`0..n`) remain a separate selfhost-PARSER gap.
investigation:
fn main() { let mut v: Vec[i64] = Vec.new(); v.push(3); v.push(4); v.push(5); let mut t = 0; for x in v { t = t + x; } println(t.to_string()) }
// port emitter before fix: printed 0; correct: 12
resolution: Fixed in Slice 47 (57ea46e): emit_for_vec element iteration.

title: CODEGEN-GAP in the selfhost codegen PORT (codegen.kara emitter): `i64.to_f64()` was unimplemented — the method returned the i64 receiver unchanged (kind 0) instead of sitofp-ing to double, so `scale * dv.to_f64()` mixed an i64 operand into an f64 multiply and emitted INVALID IR (`mul i64 <double-typed>`), caught by the JIT verifier (not silent — a hard invalid-IR error). Surfaced by the rich-token lexer capstone's fractional-digit accumulation.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: WIP selfhost codegen.kara emitter (Phase 12 port), found by the rich-token lexer capstone (Slice 46), fixed in the same slice. Filed retroactively. Unlike the four sibling miscompiles this one was NOT silent — the type-mismatched IR failed the JIT verifier loudly. Fix: a `to_f64` builtin leg emitting `sitofp i64 <x> to double`, returning kind 5 (f64).
investigation:
fn main() { let n = 3; let f = n.to_f64(); println((f * 0.5).to_string()) }
// port emitter before fix: invalid IR 'mul i64 %<double>' -> JIT verify error; correct: 1.5
resolution: Fixed in Slice 46 (e2aaaa9): sitofp to_f64 builtin.

title: A user enum carrying a `Map`/`Set`(-family) payload leaks the handle at scope-exit drop: the enum drop walker has no Map/Set arm, so the whole kv-table is definitely-lost under valgrind. `Vec`/`String` payloads free correctly.
detail: REPRO: `enum V { Table(Map[String, i64]) } fn main() { let mut mp: Map[String, i64] = Map.new(); mp.insert("a", 1); mp.insert("b", 2); let t = V.Table(mp); println(42); }` -> AOT binary leaks `600 (72 direct, 528 indirect) bytes` from `karac_map_new` (valgrind definitely-lost). No match needed — pure construct-then-drop. CONTRASTS: an enum with a `Vec[i64]` or `String` payload does NOT leak (the drop walker frees them). ROOT: `enum_drop_kind_for_type_expr` (declarations.rs) returns `EnumDropKind::None` for Map/Set (only String/Vec/nested-struct are classified), so `emit_enum_drop_switch` (synth_drop.rs) emits no free for the Map/Set payload word. Surfaced while fixing B-2026-07-23-3 (which makes `m.len()` on such a payload DISPATCH; the leak is orthogonal and pre-existing — constructing the enum always leaked). FIX IS NON-TRIVIAL: needs drop<->deep-copy symmetry. The comment at declarations.rs `enum_drop_kind_for_type_expr` explains why Map/Set is deferred — `deep_copy_struct_heap_fields_in_place` (the by-value owned-param entry copy) duplicates Vec/String/nested-struct/enum/tuple heap but NOT Map/Set handles, so classifying Map/Set as droppable WITHOUT also deep-copying the handle on entry would double-free a by-value-copied param. Both legs (entry deep-copy of Map/Set + enum-drop Map/Set arm) must land together.
resolution: Landed both legs. New `EnumDropKind::MapOrSet` (state.rs); `enum_drop_kind_for_type_expr` classifies `Map`/`Set`/`SortedMap`/`SortedSet` (single heap-handle word) as it. `emit_enum_drop_switch` gains a `MapOrSet` arm: load the handle at the payload word (LLVM field `start_word+1`) and free via `karac_map_free_with_drop_vec` with `(drop_key, drop_val)` from `map_drop_flags(field_te)` (heap-K/V maps release per-entry buffers too); the runtime null-guards the handle, so a moved-out (zeroed) payload is a safe no-op. The symmetric entry-copy leg: `deep_copy_enum_heap_payload_in_place` gains a `MapOrSet` arm that deep-clones the handle in place via `emit_map_clone_fn` (src==dst==payload slot), so a by-value enum param owns an independent table — no double-free across the call boundary. The move-suppression duals (`zero_enum_payload_caps`, `suppress_destructured_enum_payload_cleanup_at`) were already kind-agnostic (zero all payload words for any heap-bearing kind), so they neutralize a moved-out MapOrSet handle unchanged. Verified on Linux under valgrind + ASAN/LSan: the repro is now leak-clean, and by-value-consume / Set[String] / heap-valued Map[String,String] / SortedMap / multi-field / mixed-variant shapes are double-free-clean; all backends agree. Regression tests: `asan_enum_mapset_payload_no_leak_no_double_free` (memory_sanitizer) + `test_ir_plain_enum_map_payload_drop_walk` (codegen). NOTE: a separate pre-existing miscompile of returning a moved-out Map payload from a match (`match v { Table(m) => m }` returning `Map`) was discovered during verification and filed as B-2026-07-23-14 — it fails identically on the pre-fix compiler, so it is orthogonal to this fix.

title: `mut ref` enum-payload `Map` mutation does not write through in the interpreter (interp keeps the pre-mutation size) while codegen writes through correctly — interp/codegen divergence for `match v (mut ref V) { Table(m) => m.insert(..) }`.
detail: REPRO: `enum V { Table(Map[String, i64]) } fn add(v: mut ref V) { match v { Table(m) => { m.insert("z", 99); } } } fn size(v: ref V) -> i64 { match v { Table(m) => m.len() as i64 } } fn main() { let mut mp: Map[String, i64] = Map.new(); mp.insert("a", 1); let mut t = V.Table(mp); add(mut t); println(size(t)); }` -> interp prints 1 (mutation lost), codegen (JIT + AOT) prints 2 (write-through works). Codegen is CORRECT per `mut ref` semantics; the interpreter binds the Map payload by value/copy for a `mut ref` enum-payload match and does not propagate the insert back. Newly VISIBLE after B-2026-07-23-3 (before that, codegen errored on `m.len()`/`m.insert` so the two backends couldn't be compared); the interp limitation is pre-existing. Read-only `m.len()` through `ref V` is fully in agreement (that is B-2026-07-23-3's fixed shape). SCOPE: interp `mut ref` enum-payload write-through for container handles.
resolution: ROOT CAUSE: `interpreter/value.rs` stores `Map`/`Vec` BY VALUE (`Value::Map(Vec<(Value,Value)>)` etc.), and `eval_match` bound a match payload from `scrutinee.clone()` and never wrote the arm's (possibly mutated) bindings back to the scrutinee. So `match v { Table(m) => m.insert(..) }` mutated only the arm-local `m`; `v` was unchanged, and the CICO write-back in `eval_call` then copied the unchanged `v` back to the `mut ref` caller. (Method-level write-back — `m.insert` → `write_back_receiver(Identifier("m"), ..)` — and call-level CICO write-back both worked; the MATCH level was the missing link.) FIX: `eval_match` now takes the scrutinee place expr; after the arm body runs (before pop_scope), `patch_arm_bindings` rebuilds the scrutinee value with each DIRECTLY value-bound payload position replaced by its current binding, and `write_back_receiver` stores it back. Gated to bare-identifier / `self` places (no projection re-eval) and lowercase snake_case bindings (case invariant → unambiguous value bindings, never unit-variant tests). Covers enum tuple/struct variants + plain structs; generalizes to Option/Result (also EnumVariant) and Vec payloads (same by-value class). Read-only `ref V` matches rebuild the identical value (no-op), so uninvolved matches are not corrupted. Verified interp==codegen across Map/Vec enum payloads, struct-variant, Option[Map], repeated read-only matches; regression tests `test_mut_ref_enum_payload_map_write_through` / `_struct_variant_` / `_vec_` / `test_match_readonly_enum_payload_not_corrupted` (tests/interpreter.rs). Full interpreter (1305) + featureless suites green.

title: SEED codegen double-free: `if let Variant(t) = e` over an OWNED-VARIABLE user-enum scrutinee with a heap (String/Vec) payload re-freed the payload. The destructure MOVES the buffer into the binding `t`, but the source variable `e`'s `__karac_drop_<E>` (queued by track_enum_var at the let-site, fires at the outer scope) still read e's populated payload words and freed the same buffer again -> `free(): double free detected`. A `match` on the IDENTICAL enum was correct; only the native `if let` lowering diverged.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: found by the Phase-12 selfhost codegen port (Slice 52 if-let). The port desugars if-let into a `match` at parse time, so the PORT emitter was already correct here; running the same program through the SEED (`karac run`) is what exposed the seed's own bug — a good example of the port dogfooding the seed. NOTE: filed as -13, not -11, after a concurrent session published its own -11/-12 (unrelated enum Map/Set payload bugs) — the fix commit message and code comments predate that renumber and read `B-2026-07-23-11`; this entry (-13) is the canonical record. Root cause: `compile_match` (control_flow_match.rs) suppresses the source scrutinee's per-field payload cleanup for a consumed arm via `suppress_destructured_enum_payload_cleanup(scrutinee, pattern)` in the owned-variable (non-freshtemp, non-borrow) branch; `compile_if_let` (control_flow.rs) ran that suppression ONLY for a fresh-temp scrutinee (`freshtemp_enum` -> `_at` variant), never for a plain owned variable, so the source EnumDrop and the binding's drop both freed the payload. Fix: added the mirrored `else if optres_bindings_owned { self.suppress_destructured_enum_payload_cleanup(value, pattern); }` branch. Gated so borrow/ref-param scrutinees (folded into `pattern_binding_is_borrow`) no-op; helper self-gates to heap-bearing bound fields. Option/Result scrutinees were already handled by their own inline-payload suppressors and were never affected (only USER enums with a heap payload).
resolution: Fixed 5e9bdd0: compile_if_let now mirrors compile_match's variable-scrutinee suppress_destructured_enum_payload_cleanup in the owned-binding branch. Regression: asan_if_let_owned_var_enum_string_payload_no_double_free; full memory_sanitizer suite (844) + codegen E2E + selfhost oracle (164) green.

title: Returning a `Map`/`Set`(-family) value moved OUT of an enum payload fails codegen module verification: `fn unwrap(v: V) -> Map[K,V] { match v { Table(m) => m } }` emits `ret i64 %matchval` for a `ptr`-typed return. The Map handle extracted from the enum's i64 payload word is not reinterpreted to a pointer before the return inst. interp is correct; a `Vec`/`String` payload in the same shape compiles fine.
detail: REPRO: `enum V { Table(Map[String, i64]) } fn unwrap(v: V) -> Map[String, i64] { match v { Table(m) => m } } fn main() { let mut mp: Map[String, i64] = Map.new(); mp.insert("a", 1); mp.insert("b", 2); let t = V.Table(mp); let m2 = unwrap(t); println(m2.len() as i64); }` -> `karac build`/`karac run` (JIT) fail with `Module verification failed: "Function return type does not match operand type of return inst!\n  ret i64 %matchval\n ptr"`. `karac run --interp` prints 2 (correct). SCOPE (bisected): (1) Map/Set-specific — the SAME move-out+return shape with a `Vec[i64]` payload compiles and runs (Vec is a 3-word {ptr,len,cap} extracted as an aggregate; a Map is a single handle word stored as i64 in the enum payload, and the extraction keeps it i64). (2) It is the RETURN that fails, not the move-out: binding the moved-out Map to a local and calling `.len()` on it WITHOUT returning it compiles+runs (`fn peek(v: V) -> i64 { let r = match v { Table(m) => m }; r.len() as i64 }` -> 1). (3) A `let` between match and return does NOT help (`let r = match v { Table(m) => m }; r` fails identically with `ret i64 %r3`). PRE-EXISTING: fails identically on the pre-B-2026-07-23-11 compiler (ec43661), so it is orthogonal to the enum Map/Set drop fix. ROOT (hypothesis): the enum payload word for a Map is an i64 (handle bit-cast via ptrtoint at construction); `bind_pattern_values`/match-value extraction binds `m` as an i64 SSA value rather than reinterpreting it back to `ptr` (int-to-ptr) when the bound payload type is a Map/Set handle, so the fn's `ret` (typed `ptr`) receives the i64. A local `.len()` dispatch tolerates the i64 (the method-call receiver path reinterprets), but the bare `ret` does not. Likely fix: int-to-ptr the extracted Map/Set handle at the match-binding site (or coerce at the return) so the SSA value type matches the Map handle's `ptr` LLVM type.
resolution: Confirmed root cause exactly as hypothesized. `reconstruct_payload_value`'s single-word path (control_flow_match.rs) returns the raw i64 payload word for a Map/Set binding, and the `bind_pattern_values` Binding arm (pattern_binding.rs) had explicit int-to-ptr arms for shared/File/DataFrame payloads but NONE for Map/Set, so it created an i64-typed binding alloca. Method dispatch (`m.len()`) reinterpreted the i64 (clean), but a bare `ret`/forward of the handle demanded `ptr` and tripped module verification. Shared-struct payloads in the same shape already worked because the shared arm int-to-ptr's the word. Fix: in the Binding arm, int-to-ptr a `Map`/`Set`/`SortedMap`/`SortedSet` payload word (recorded in `pattern_binding_types`) before the generic alloca, so the binding slot is pointer-typed — the minimal re-typing that reuses the existing Map ownership+dispatch registration (`track_map_var_with_val_drop` / `register_var_from_type_expr`), which keys on the alloca not its element type. Verified on Linux under valgrind: `fn unwrap(v: V) -> Map[K,V] { match v { Table(m) => m } }` builds, runs correctly, 10 allocs = 10 frees (returned handle transfers to the caller, source move-suppressed, freed once), matches interp. Tests: `e2e_return_map_moved_out_of_enum_payload` (codegen) + `asan_enum_map_payload_moved_out_and_returned_no_leak_no_double_free` (memory_sanitizer). NOTE: a generic-enum Map payload (mono-resolved, not in `pattern_binding_types`) is an untouched exotic edge — no worse than before, not a common shape.

title: SELFHOST PARSER (parser.kara, Phase-12 port): the `expr as TYPE` cast operator was UNHANDLED in `parse_expr_bp` (only import-alias `as` existed). `as` was thus an unrecognized infix token that stopped expression parsing, stranding `as TYPE` in the token stream. Harmless at a statement/`]`/`)` boundary (a no-op `<int> as i64` cast just parsed as the operand), but `while COND as i64 { BODY }` left `as i64` between the condition and the body `{`, so `parse_block` mis-recovered and SWALLOWED every statement following the loop into its body — they then executed once per iteration.
detail:
SOURCE NOTE: found by real-shape differential probing of the selfhost toolchain (parse_program + emit_program) against the seed `karac run` oracle, while sweeping post-if-let (Slice 52) frontier shapes. The bug is in the PORT's parser.kara, not the seed. Numbered -15 (a concurrent session claimed -14 for an unrelated enum Map/Set codegen-gap). WHY IT HID: a no-op widening cast (`<int> as i64`, the ONLY cast shape in real self-host code — all are `(c as i64)` on a byte) parses to the same VALUE whether or not a cast node is built, and a stranded trailing `as i64` is inert at a `;`/`]`/`)` boundary; so `v[i as i64]` and `return len() as i64` both passed the oracle, masking the gap. It only bit where the stranded tokens sat between a condition and a block: `while i < x as i64 { i = i + 1; } println(...)` ran the trailing println once PER ITERATION (`1
2
3
` for x=3 instead of `3`). `if` was immune (its post-condition recovery differs). NOT a codegen bug — the emitter never sees a cast; NOT the seed — seed `karac run` is correct. FIX (Slice 53, 3afd613): added an `As` arm to `parse_expr_bp`'s operator loop at the seed's `l_bp = 23` (between multiplicative 22/23 and unary 24; `src/parser/exprs.rs` Token::As), min_bp-gated. It parses the target type via `parse_type()` purely to ADVANCE the cursor and KEEPS the operand unchanged — DROPPING the cast, which is exactly what the emitter does today (no Cast AST node in the port; the emitter is i64-centric so every in-surface `<int> as i64` is a no-op). Precedence verified: `i < x as i64` = `i < (x as i64)`, `x as i64 - 2` = `(x as i64) - 2`.
resolution: Fixed in Slice 53 (3afd613): parse-and-drop `as TYPE` in parse_expr_bp at l_bp 23. Selfhost oracle (corpus 165) + emitter parity + valgrind green.

title: A PLAIN struct pattern whose field sub-pattern is an enum-variant pattern — `match it { Item { shape: Shape.Circle(r), .. } => .. }` — miscompiles under `karac build`/JIT: the nested enum's discriminant is NEVER checked, so a `Rect`/`Point` item matches the first `Circle(r)` arm and binds garbage (silent wrong-arm + garbage payload).
detail: ROOT CAUSE: codegen's `compile_pattern_condition` (src/codegen/control_flow_match.rs) had a guarded `PatternKind::Struct` arm ONLY for the enum-VARIANT struct case (`path.len() > 1 || enum_tag_for_variant(..)`); a PLAIN struct pattern (`Item { .. }`, Item is a struct not a variant) fell through to the `_ => Ok(tru.into())` catch-all — ALWAYS matches, never recursing into field sub-patterns. So every field sub-pattern's discriminating test was dropped: `Item { shape: Shape.Circle(r), .. }` matched Rect/Point items too, extracting Rect's first field / garbage as `r`. Silent — no crash, no diagnostic; `karac build` and the LLJIT `karac run` both wrong, `karac run --interp` correct. Struct sibling of the tuple 'no discriminating test emitted' class (B-2026-07-12-13). NOTE: id was -15 in the first push but collided with a concurrently-landed selfhost as-cast entry; renumbered to -16.
investigation: Found by probe round 13 (fresh-surface JIT-vs-interp divergence sweep). Minimal: `enum Shape { Circle(f64), Rect(f64,f64), Point } struct Item { shape: Shape, count: i64 } fn classify(it: ref Item) -> String { match it { Item { shape: Shape.Circle(r), count: _ } => f"circle r={r}", Item { shape: Shape.Rect(w,h), count: _ } => f"rect {w}x{h}", Item { shape: Shape.Point, count: _ } => "point" } }` over Circle(5)/Rect(3,6)/Point: JIT printed `circle r=5 / circle r=3 / circle r=0`; interp (correct) `circle r=5 / rect 3x6 / point`.
resolution: Added an unguarded `PatternKind::Struct { path, fields, .. }` arm to `compile_pattern_condition` (reached only when the enum-variant guard is false): looks up field indices via `struct_field_names`, pulls each field with a sub-pattern in whichever form the scrutinee is (loaded StructValue -> extractvalue; a `ref`/borrowed struct pointer -> GEP + load, yielding the correct shape for `extract_enum_tag`), recurses `compile_pattern_condition`, and ANDs the conditions — mirroring the `Tuple` arm. Two E2E regression tests in tests/codegen.rs. Full codegen suite 2571/0; interp 1304/0; typechecker 2086/0. The enum-VARIANT struct pattern with a nested refutable field remains a documented follow-up.

title: An undefined name inside a `requires`/`ensures` contract expression passes `karac check` and ICEs at runtime ('variable … not found … should be caught by resolver'). The natural trigger: writing `ensures result …` WITHOUT the `(result)` binding, so `result` is an undefined identifier.
detail: ROOT CAUSE: `resolver::resolve_function` (src/resolver/resolve_items.rs) resolved generics/self/params/return-type/effects/body but NEVER `f.requires` / `f.ensures`, so contract expressions were entirely un-name-checked. An undefined name there slips past `karac check` and reaches codegen/interp, which hit the 'should be caught by resolver' unreachable and PANIC (rc=101) on both `karac run` and `--interp`. Affects both `requires` and `ensures`, free fns and impl methods (methods reuse resolve_function). SYMPTOM class is a crash but the DEFECT is the missing resolution (a false-negative name check), so classed diagnostics.
investigation: Found probing the contracts surface. Minimal: `fn f(a: i64) -> i64 ensures result == a { a }` -> check passes, run -> 'internal error: entered unreachable code: variable \'result\' not found at 2:13; should be caught by resolver'. Same for `requires bogus > 0`. The CORRECT form `ensures(result) result * b == a - (a % b)` (with the `(result)` binding) always worked. Note: `old` is not a parser keyword — it is a `Call` with callee `Identifier("old")` intercepted by the interpreter by name (checking its separate runtime env), so a resolver fix must let `old` resolve without adding it to the runtime env.
resolution: resolve_function now resolves each `requires` expr and each `ensures` clause body in the function scope. For `ensures(result) …` it pushes a scope and defines the `param` (result) binding; it also defines a synthetic `old` function symbol so `old(expr)` resolves at any depth (the interpreter's by-name interception and separate runtime env are unaffected; the typechecker still enforces old's ensures-only restriction). Neither `old` nor `result` is a reserved identifier, so the synthetic defines are clean. 4 resolver regression tests. Existing contract suites unchanged (resolver 1304/0, parser 767/0, interp 326/0, codegen ensures/old/requires 54/0). Full codegen suite 2571/0.

title: SELFHOST EMITTER (codegen.kara, Phase-12 port): UNARY NEGATION `-x` was a silent NO-OP. The `Unary` arm only implemented `not b` (Slice 4); the `Neg` case fell through and returned the operand UNCHANGED, so `-1` emitted `1`, `-x` emitted `x`, `-2 * 3` emitted `6`. Every unary minus in the port's output was wrong.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: found by real-shape differential probing of the selfhost toolchain (parse_program + emit_program) vs the seed `karac run` oracle, sweeping guard-clause shapes after Slice 53. Numbered -18 (concurrent sessions claimed -16 struct-pattern-enum-subpattern and -17 requires/ensures-undefined-name). WHY IT HID: a glaring CORPUS BLIND SPOT — negatives had only ever been exercised as BINARY subtraction (`0 - 5` = -5, Slice 4), NEVER the unary `-` operator, so the emitter's missing Neg leg was never differentially tested. Yet `return -1` sentinels are pervasive in real self-host code (lexer `hex_val` returns -1 for a non-hex byte, resolver returns -1 for 'not found', parser error paths). The bug first surfaced disguised: `if i >= 0 and i < n { return v[i]; } return -1;` returned `1` on the false path, looking like an `and`/`if`-return fault until reduced to a bare `return -1` -> `1`. FIX (Slice 54, c979710): a `Neg` leg in emit_value's Unary arm emitting `sub i64 0, x` (result kind 0 / i64), folded into the SINGLE `op` match (UnaryOp is not Copy — same discipline as BinOp's bin_ir). `~` (BitNot) / `*` (Deref) cannot be produced by the port parser (Neg/Not only) and pass through unchanged. NOT a parser bug (the AST had the correct Unary(Neg) node); NOT the seed (seed codegen negates correctly).
resolution: Fixed in Slice 54 (c979710): Neg -> `sub i64 0, x`. Selfhost oracle (corpus 166) + emitter parity + valgrind green.

title: A parenthesized single pattern `(P)` is parsed as a 1-element tuple `Tuple([P])` instead of a grouping, so `x @ (1 | 2 | 3)` and top-level `(1 | 2)` silently match the WRONG arm on BOTH backends: `karac build`/JIT over-matches (a non-member scalar hits the arm), `karac run --interp` under-matches (a member scalar falls through).
detail: ROOT CAUSE: `parser::parse_single_pattern`'s `Token::LeftParen` arm (src/parser/patterns.rs) ALWAYS built a `PatternKind::Tuple`, so `(1 | 2 | 3)` parsed as a 1-element `Tuple([Or([1,2,3])])` rather than the grouped `Or`. A tuple pattern can never match a scalar scrutinee, so on `match n: i64`: codegen's `compile_pattern_condition` Tuple arm hit its `else` (non-aggregate scrutinee) branch -> always-true (OVER-match: `x @ (1|2|3)` matched 9); the interpreter tried to match a tuple against a scalar -> never matches (UNDER-match: 2 fell through). One parser root cause, two opposite symptoms. Affects ANY parenthesized pattern over a non-tuple scrutinee (with or without `@`). The distributed `x @ 1 | x @ 2` form was fine (parses as Or([AtBinding,AtBinding])), which is why the existing test_e2e_match_at_binding_or missed it.
investigation: Probe round 13 batch 10 (@/or/range/guard). Minimal: `match n { x @ (1 | 2 | 3) => x*100, other => other }` over 2 and 9: JIT 200,900; interp 2,9. `1 | 2 | 3` without parens matches correctly on both.
resolution: parse_single_pattern's LeftParen arm now tracks a trailing comma: `(P)` (single element, no trailing comma) returns the inner pattern as a GROUPING; `(P,)` stays a 1-tuple; `(A, B, ...)` a tuple — Rust semantics. One parser fix corrects both backends. 3 parser + 2 codegen E2E regression tests. Full codegen 2574/0, parser 770/0, interp/typechecker/resolver green.

title: Auto-par miscompiles a reduction loop whose body passes a LOOP-INVARIANT shared `mut ref` scratch buffer to a helper. `while w < n { sink = sink + f(..., mut scratch, ...); w += 1 }` is parallelized as a `sink` reduction, but `scratch` (a binding declared OUTSIDE the loop, written every iteration inside `f`) makes the iterations dependent, so parallel workers race on it -> nondeterministic WRONG output from the DEFAULT `karac build` (and `karac run` JIT), while `KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0` is stable and correct. A/B run==build violation; auto-par safety analysis is unsound for this shape.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: surfaced while authoring the #214 Shortest Palindrome cross-language BENCHMARK (bench-backfill sweep). The kata #214 itself (one call in main, no punch loop) is clean under auto-par; only the bench's window-reduction loop triggers it. The bench builds with KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0 so its numbers stay valid; FILED not routed around (katas-are-bug-finders). MINIMAL REPRO (stable under KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0, nondeterministic under default build): `fn kern(base: ref Vec[i64], w: i64, width: i64, a: mut ref Vec[i64], b: mut ref Vec[i64]) -> i64 { let m = 2i64*width; let mut i=0i64; while i<m { a[i]=base[w+(i%width)]; i=i+1i64; } let mut len=0i64; let mut j=1i64; b[0]=0i64; while j<m { if a[j]==a[len] { len=len+1i64; b[j]=len; j=j+1i64; } else if len>0i64 { len=b[len-1i64]; } else { b[j]=0i64; j=j+1i64; } } return b[m-1i64]; }` with main building base(PRNG), a,b(size m) ONCE then `while w < big-width { sink = sink + kern(base, w, width, mut a, mut b); w=w+1i64; } println(sink);`. Measured: seq (KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0) = 159280800 stable; default build = 121991978 / 132004532 / 129048221 / 124736566 (nondeterministic, all wrong); nm|grep karac_par = 2 (loop parallelized). The #214 bench itself: seq 132598368 (matches all 5 langs) vs default 106205458/102568720/101356654/... and karac run 110936108/106613469. A LIGHTER variant where the callee's scratch writes are dead-store-eliminated does NOT race (no shared memory traffic survives) — the hazard only manifests when the buffer is genuinely read back across iterations (KMP b[len-1]). ROOT CAUSE (hypothesis): the auto-par reduction/parallel-loop eligibility check (src/concurrency.rs) treats sink = sink + call(...) as a parallelizable reduction but does NOT disqualify the loop when the body passes a mut ref / mut Slice argument whose place-root is a binding declared OUTSIDE the loop (loop-invariant shared mutable). Those buffers are written every iteration => iterations are not independent. FIX HYPOTHESIS: disqualify a loop from auto-par when any call in the body passes a mut ref/mut Slice argument rooted at a loop-invariant (outside-the-loop) binding; per-iteration-fresh mut-ref targets (allocated inside the loop body) stay eligible. Needs a tests/par_codegen.rs determinism regression.
resolution: The reduction recognizer (`recognize_reductions_in_block`, src/concurrency.rs) is independent of the statement-level dependency machinery, and its only data-hazard gate (`collect_expr_inner_writes`) sees DIRECT `Assign`/`+=` targets — never a mutation performed INSIDE a callee through a `mut ref` argument. So the shared-scratch write (`kern` writing `a`/`b`) was invisible and the `sink` loop looked like independent iterations. Fix: new soundness gate `loop_body_shares_outer_mut_borrow` (called right after `loop_body_types_cross_task_safe`) declines the reduction when the body has a call passing a `mut ref`/`mut Slice` argument — detected via the call-site `CallArg.mut_marker` OR the resolved callee's `param_is_mut_borrow` (MutRef/MutSlice only, NOT read-only Ref) — or a `mut ref self` method receiver, whose place-root is NOT a per-iteration-fresh (loop-body-local) binding. `locals` is threaded in statement order (a body-local shadow can't retroactively mask an earlier outer-rooted call). A comprehensive recursive walker (`expr_shares_outer_mut_borrow`, mirroring `collect_expr_reads`) ensures no call position is missed. Read-only `ref T` args (immutable shared data) stay eligible; a `let mut tmp` allocated inside the loop body stays eligible (each worker owns its own). Verified: repro deterministic+correct across interp/seq/auto-par (sink reduction declined, no par-reduce fan-out); positive controls (no-mut-ref reduction + fresh-per-iter mut-ref buffer) still parallelize. par_codegen regression tests added.

title: SELFHOST EMITTER (codegen.kara, Phase-12 port): the BITWISE and SHIFT operators `& | ^ << >>` were ALL emitted as `add`. `bin_ir`'s `_ =>` catch-all defaulted every unmapped BinOp to `add`, so `12 & 10` computed 22, `12 | 10` computed 22, `12 ^ 10` computed 22, `1 << 4` computed 5, `256 >> 2` computed 258 — every bitwise/shift op was silent ADDITION.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: found by real-shape differential probing of the selfhost toolchain vs the seed `karac run` oracle, sweeping operator shapes after Slice 54. Numbered -21 (concurrent sessions claimed -19 paren-single-pattern-tuple and -20 autopar-reduction-soundness). IN-SURFACE, not merely hypothetical: codegen.kara's OWN `hex_u64` helper uses `(bits >> ((15 - i) * 4)) & 15` to format a float bit-pattern, so a self-hosting build would MISCOMPILE THE EMITTER ITSELF. Same fall-through class as the Slice-54 unary-negation no-op: an unmapped operator silently taking the `add` default. The parser already produced BitAnd/BitOr/BitXor/Shl/Shr nodes (Pipe/Caret/Amp/LessLess/GreaterGreater in parse_expr_bp); only the emitter's bin_ir mapping was missing them. FIX (Slice 55, 8a5fec2): five kind-0 (i64 arithmetic-path) arms mirroring the seed (src/codegen/expr_ops.rs build_binary): BitAnd->and, BitOr->or, BitXor->xor, Shl->shl, Shr->ashr. Shr is ARITHMETIC right shift (the seed's `build_right_shift(sign_extend = !is_unsigned)` = ashr for signed i64, every scalar in the port's model); a negative-bits mask loop in the corpus confirms sign-extension parity. kind 0 keeps `&`/`|` off the kind-2 SHORT-CIRCUIT branch the LOGICAL And/Or take, so the reused `and`/`or` mnemonics do not collide (different kind -> different emit branch).
resolution: Fixed in Slice 55 (8a5fec2): bin_ir gained BitAnd/BitOr/BitXor/Shl/Shr arms (kind 0, Shr=ashr). Selfhost oracle (corpus 167) + emitter parity + valgrind green.

title: SELFHOST PARSER (parser.kara, Phase-12 port): COMPOUND ASSIGNMENT `x += v` / `-=` / `*=` / `/=` / `%=` is SILENTLY DROPPED — a no-op with no diagnostic. The block statement handler parses the LHS then only checks for a plain `Equal`; a `PlusEqual`(-family) token is neither an assignment nor a recognized infix operator, so the LHS becomes a bare expression-statement and the `OP= value` tail is discarded. `let mut x = 5; x += 3;` leaves x = 5.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: found by real-shape differential probing of the selfhost toolchain vs the seed `karac run` oracle (operator sweep after Slice 55). OUT OF THE CURRENT BOOTSTRAP SURFACE — real self-host code (parser.kara/codegen.kara/lexer.kara/…) consistently writes `x = x + 1`, never `x += 1`, so no live self-host unit hits this — which is why it is filed OPEN rather than fixed in-slice (grow-on-demand). But it is a genuine SILENT-no-op trap for any kata / dogfood / hand-written `.kara` that uses compound assignment: the selfhost LEXER already emits PlusEqual/MinusEqual/StarEqual/SlashEqual/PercentEqual (lexer.kara) and the seed compiles them, so a program is accepted and runs with the compound update simply missing. WHY DEFERRED (fix is non-trivial): the natural desugar `x OP= v` -> `x = x OP v` needs the LHS place-expression TWICE (assign target + Binary lhs), but the port has NO Expr deep-clone helper and targets can be arbitrary place exprs (`self.toks[i]`, `p.x`), so a correct fix must first add expr cloning (or thread the compound op into AssignStmt + emit `load;op;store` in codegen). SCOPE when built: parser desugar (or an AssignStmt compound-op field) + the five arithmetic forms; bitwise-assign (`&=`/`|=`/`^=`/`<<=`/`>>=`) if the lexer emits them. At minimum, until implemented the parser should ERROR on a compound-assign token rather than silently drop it.
resolution: `parse_block` (selfhost/src/parser.kara) recognized only a plain `Equal` after a statement LHS; a `PlusEqual`-family token fell through to a bare expression-statement and the `OP= value` tail was dropped. Fix desugars `target OP= value` to `target = target OP value`, reusing the existing Assign + Binary emitter (ZERO codegen.kara change). `Expr` is a `shared` handle with no clone method and the ownership checker moves it on first use (confirmed: reusing `e` in both the assign target and the binary left fails `value 'e' moved here, used again here`), so the target cannot be aliased into two owned positions. Instead an IDENTIFIER target — the common shape (`x += v`, `i += 1`, `acc += x`) — is reconstructed from its NAME into two fresh `Ident` nodes (String `.clone()` + `clone_span`, both already available). All ten `*Equal` tokens map to their BinOp (Add/Sub/Mul/Div/Mod/BitAnd/BitOr/BitXor/Shl/Shr). A NON-identifier place target (`self.x += v`, `a[i] += v`) is not yet lowered — it emits an Error statement, a LOUD failure rather than the pre-fix silent no-op (full place-expr support deferred; needs a recursive Expr clone or an AssignStmt compound-op field + codegen load-op-store). Verified by the selfhost_codegen behavioral oracle: a new corpus program covering all ten forms + a loop counter + an accumulator compiles parser.kara -> codegen.kara -> JIT and matches the seed's `karac run`. Other selfhost oracles (parser/resolver/typechecker) green.

title: SELFHOST EMITTER (codegen.kara, Phase-12 port): INDEXED ASSIGNMENT `v[i] = value` was SILENTLY DROPPED. The `Assign` statement handler matched only `Field` (`p.x = v`) and `Ident` (`x = v`) targets; an `Index` target hit the `_ =>` catch-all and emitted NOTHING, so `v[0] = 99` was a no-op (v[0] kept its old value).
detail: SOURCE NOTE: found by real-shape differential probing (place-expression assignment sweep) vs the seed `karac run` oracle. IN-SURFACE: the port's OWN codegen.kara uses `self.locals_heap[idx] = vh`, and array mutation is fundamental to any algorithm. FIX (Slice 56, 53f2553): an `Index` arm in the Assign match mirroring the read-side Index address computation — extractvalue the Vec's {ptr,len,cap} buffer pointer, GEP by element type — then STORE the RHS instead of loading. The store writes through the live heap buffer the slot's aggregate also points at, so it is visible on the next read (no write-back of the aggregate needed — the buffer is shared). Vec[i64] (kind 3, `store i64`) and Vec[String] (kind 4 — loads+frees the OLD element string, then materializes a borrowed RHS before the store, so a reassign-in-loop is leak-clean) are surfaced.
