Vec[bool] is DEFERRED (open B-2026-07-23-24 — it needs a distinct i1-lane element kind, the same gap that breaks Vec[bool] push/read) and Vec-of-struct/enum assign targets have no port site.
resolution: Fixed in Slice 56 (53f2553): Index arm in the Assign match (Vec[i64] + Vec[String]). Selfhost oracle (corpus 168) + valgrind green.

title: SELFHOST EMITTER (codegen.kara, Phase-12 port): `Vec[bool]` has NO distinct element kind — it is conflated with `Vec[i64]` (kind 3), so the i1/i64 lane is mishandled at BOTH ends: `push(false)` emits `store i64 false` (an i1 constant into an i64 store → module verification failure), and a read `v[i]` returns i64 while `if v[i]` needs i1 (`br i1 <i64>` type error). Vec[bool] cannot be constructed or read.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: found while adding indexed assignment (B-2026-07-23-23, Slice 56) — a `v[0] = true` probe exposed it. IN-SURFACE: the port's own codegen.kara declares `locals_heap: Vec[bool]` and both pushes to it and reads `if self.locals_heap[idx]`, so a self-hosting build needs this. ROOT: the emitter assigns Vec[bool] the SAME kind as Vec[i64] (3), with no record that the element lane is i1. A correct fix is a dedicated slice adding a distinct Vec[bool] element kind (or an is_bool flag on the vec kind) that threads three coordinated legs: (1) push zext's the i1 arg to the i64 store lane; (2) element read truncs the i64 lane back to i1 (kind 1) so bool contexts (`if`, `and`/`or`) type-check; (3) indexed assign (already structured in Slice 56's Index arm) zext's the i1 RHS. Deferred from Slice 56 to keep that slice's Vec[i64]/Vec[String] paths clean and fully tested rather than shipping a half-wired Vec[bool].
resolution: Fixed for the LOCAL Vec[bool] surface (selfhost/src/codegen.kara). Kept Vec[bool] on Vec[i64]'s kind-3 i64-lane storage (identical {ptr,len,cap} layout, buffer-only drop, len, materialize — all inherited from the already-valgrind-clean kind-3 path, so ZERO new storage/drop/ownership sites and no leak risk) and convert only at the value boundaries via two helpers: `to_i64_lane` zext's an i1 bool (kind 1) into the i64 store lane on `push` and indexed assignment (`v[i] = b`); `to_i1` truncs an i64-lane bool back to i1 in every boolean-context consumer (`if`/`while` conditions, `and`/`or` short-circuit operands, `not`). Both are no-ops off the Vec[bool] path (kind-0 i64 pass-through / kind-1 i1 pass-through), so every pre-existing corpus program emits byte-identical IR — verified: the selfhost_codegen oracle stays green with two new Vec[bool] corpus programs (the exact ledger repro `push(false); v[0]=true; if v[0]` plus a mixed push/indexed-assign/len/if/while/and/or/not exercise), each running identically to the seed's native `karac run`; and a valgrind pass on the selfhost-emitted AOT binary is clean (0 errors, buffer freed at scope exit). REMAINING (follow-up, not this slice): a VALUE-position Vec[bool] read stays kind 0 (i64 lane), so `v[i].to_string()` would print 1/0 not true/false, and bool param/field/return over a Vec[bool] element is unhandled — those need the read to return kind 1, which requires a per-vec bool marker; deferred because the covered boolean-context surface is exactly the ledger repro and the self-host `if self.locals_heap[idx]` need. The Vec[bool] STRUCT FIELD receiver ops (`self.locals_heap.push(...)`) are also still gapped, but that is the separate pre-existing field-receiver-push gap (the push handler only matches Ident receivers), not the element-kind bug fixed here.

title: Auto-par over-parallelizes a fine-grained inner loop, making the DEFAULT `karac build` catastrophically slow (~1000x) while output stays CORRECT. A punch/reduction loop that per pass rebuilds a small array and insertion-sorts it under an integer concatenation comparator runs ~0.00s sequentially but ~15s under auto-par (measured at 5 of 400 passes) due to per-task scheduling overhead dwarfing the trivial per-iteration work. Not a race (deterministic, byte-correct) and distinct from the now-fixed B-2026-07-23-20 soundness race: this is an auto-par COST-MODEL gap (parallelizing a loop whose body is too light to amortize task spawn).
detail: SOURCE NOTE: surfaced authoring the #179 Largest Number cross-language BENCHMARK (bench-backfill sweep). REPRO (concrete, committed): kara-katas/leetcode/101-200/179-largest-number/bench/largest_number.kara. It rebuilds a 500-elem array from a fixed base each pass (one element perturbed), insertion-sorts descending by the Largest-Number concat comparator (concat_val via num_digits/pow10 — PURE integer arithmetic, no allocation), and sinks a Horner checksum: `while p < passes { <rebuild arr>; sort_desc(mut arr); sink = sink + checksum(arr); p+=1 }`. MEASURED on FIXED karac (release build off current main, which INCLUDES the B-2026-07-23-20 fix): at passes=5, KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0 build ~0.00s vs default (auto-par) build 14.95s — identical correct output 2318655841; `nm | grep karac_par` = 1. Full passes=400: seq ~0.21s vs default >90s (>400x). So the -20 fix did NOT address this. Auto-par output is byte-correct and deterministic (verified matches seq), so it is NOT a soundness/race bug — it is pure scheduling overhead: auto-par appears to parallelize a FINE-GRAINED inner loop (the comparator's num_digits/pow10 or the checksum Horner loop — a handful of integer ops per iteration) where per-task spawn cost dwarfs the work by ~1000x. NOTE a naive minimal repro (reduction loop + insertion sort with an f-string-allocating comparator, fresh Vec per pass) did NOT reproduce (auto-par was fine there), so the trigger is specific to this fine-grained integer-comparator shape; the committed bench is the reliable repro. FIX HYPOTHESIS: auto-par's profitability/cost model needs a per-iteration-work floor — a loop whose body is a few scalar ops (or a call to a helper with only tiny scalar loops) must NOT be parallelized; the spawn+join overhead is unrecoverable. The bench itself is unaffected (bench.sh builds KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0); filed not routed around.
resolution: Added a narrow param-bounded per-iteration-work floor to the auto-par reduction cost gate (src/codegen/reduce.rs). A VARIABLE-trip-count reduction is now declined when its per-iter body scores below VARIABLE_K_PER_ITER_FLOOR_UNITS (= RUNTIME_NESTED_LOOP_MULTIPLIER, i.e. less than one runtime nested loop's worth of work) AND its trip-count bound (end/lo) references a current-function parameter — the reusable hot-path helper signature (fn pow10(n){while i<n{r=r*10}}). Such a helper invoked millions of times inside an O(n^2) comparator previously bypassed the compile-time K*per_iter gate (bound is not a literal) and lowered to par_reduce, paying unrecoverable per-call dispatch (~1000x slowdown, output correct). A local/literal-bounded one-shot loop, or a coarse body doing real per-iter work (a nested runtime loop), stays eligible. Threads a per-function current_fn_param_names set through codegen (codegen.rs field + init, functions.rs populate in codegen_function) consumed by new reduction_bound_references_param / expr_references_current_param helpers. Verified: the committed #179 bench (pow10/num_digits concat comparator) is declined (nm: no karac_par_reduce mul-combine helper) and the default build now matches the KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0 timing/output; full par_codegen suite (200) green including the two new B-23-25 tests; clippy (+/-llvm) + fmt clean.

title: Compiler-driven inline-hint pass runs on the LOWERED AST but its node-count thresholds are calibrated for RAW-source sizes, so a small loop-hot helper loses its `inlinehint` after lowering inflates its node count. `fn expand(chars: ref Vec[char], lo, hi)` (expand-around-center) is 42 nodes in source but 51 post-lower (operator/`.len()`/`and`/index desugar to trait-method Call nodes), just over the tight loop-hot cap (MEDIUM=48). It stays out of line, so the caller's range/monotonicity facts never reach its hot index loop and the surviving half-bounds-checks cannot be elided — the palindrome benchmark ran ~2.5x slower than the equal-safety Rust mirror.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: surfaced re-benchmarking the string-DP cluster (#5/#115/#161) on a quiet machine; #5 measured 2.46x slower than `rustc -O -C overflow-checks=on` sequentially. ROOT CAUSE (empirically proven, not theorized): disassembly of the sequential `karac build` showed `expand` OUTLINED (a standalone symbol, called twice per outer iteration) with two live half-bounds-check panic branches in the inner loop (chars[lo] upper, chars[hi] lower); the source-level BCE (index_bounds_already_proven) had correctly elided the guard-proven halves (lo>=0 lower, hi<n upper) but the other two halves need the caller's `c < n` fact, which only reaches `expand` after INLINING. Rust inlines expand and kills both. Force-inlining Kara's expand via a hand-edited alwaysinline attr through opt/llc/clang-18 dropped runtime 1.93s->0.91s (2.13x) and closed the gap to ~1.0-1.16x vs Rust, confirming inlining is the lever. The inline_hints pass (src/inline_hints.rs) is consulted at codegen time on the lowered program (codegen.rs compute(program) after lower()), but SMALL=16/MEDIUM=48 and the module's own unit tests only `parse()` (pre-lower). Instrumented sizes: expand 51 nodes, sites=2, any_in_loop=true post-lower — misses the loop-hot MEDIUM=48 cap by 3, so no hint, so LLVM's own cost model leaves the `[2 x i64]`-returning helper out of line. longest_palindrome (86 nodes, 1 site) kept its hint via the single-site cap (256), which is why only the 2-site loop-hot helper regressed.
resolution: Gave the loop-hot inline tier its own explicit cap LOOP_HOT_CAP=128 (half SINGLE_SITE_CAP), replacing the reuse of MEDIUM=48. A function called from inside a loop is a strong inline signal — it pays call overhead every iteration AND inlining exposes the caller range/monotonicity facts that let LLVM elide the surviving half-bounds-checks — with no principled reason to sit 5x below the single-call-site cap. `inlinehint` is advisory so LLVM still applies its own cost model; this only widens latitude for the loop-hot class, not a forced inline. Post-fix: expand gets Inline post-lower, inlines (0 standalone symbols), bounds checks elided, #5 sequential build reaches parity with Rust (795ms vs 790ms, 1.01x; was 2.46x). Correctness verified across all four surfaces (interp/jit/build/auto-par-off all agree). Added a post-lower-shaped regression test (medium_loop_hot_helper_gets_inline). Full suite green: lib 990, codegen E2E 2575, memory_sanitizer/LSan 851, clippy(+llvm --all-targets)+fmt clean.

title: `for k in map.keys()` (and `.values()`/`.entries()`) eagerly materializes the whole key/value set into a fresh heap `Vec` on every evaluation, so a `keys()` iteration inside a hot loop pays a malloc + full-set copy + free per outer iteration. Rust's `keys()` is a zero-allocation, inlined lazy bucket walk. On LeetCode #170 (Two Sum III), `find` does `for k in ds.counts.keys()` and runs 1.2M times over a ~170-entry map — 1.2M materializations — making the Kāra bench ~1.74x the equal-safety Rust mirror.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: found triaging the corpus perf outliers after the B-2026-07-24-1 inline fix. ROOT CAUSE (disassembly-confirmed): `compile_map_keys_values_entries` (src/codegen/maps.rs:572, comment at :699) ALWAYS returns an OWNED `Vec[K]`/`Vec[V]`/entries materialized eagerly; there is no lazy for-loop path (method_call.rs:5705-5707 and :9514 both note keys/values/entries are materialized). So `for k in <map>.keys()` lowers to: call the eager materializer (malloc a Vec + `karac_map_iter_new`/`iter_next` per entry storing each into the buffer + `iter_free`), then iterate the buffer, then drop it. In #170's `find` (objdump of the inlined loop in `main`: malloc@plt at 8ca7, iter_new at 8cb4, a store-into-buffer loop at 8ce0 calling iter_next per key, iter_free at 8d16) this whole build-then-iterate-then-free happens once per `find` call — 1.2M times. The map get() inside find IS on the mono inline fast-path (no call) and insert() is mono (`karac_map_i64_i64_insert_old`), so the collection ops are fine; the gap is purely the per-call keys() Vec materialization. MEASURED (fixed karac, idle container): kara seq 5419ms vs rust 3105ms = 1.74x (recorded 11:32 snapshot); the two-probe `add` (get-then-insert vs Rust's single-probe `entry`) is NOT the cause — add runs only 170x. FIX SKETCH: give `for <pat> in <mapplace>.keys()|.values()|.entries()` a lazy lowering that drives `karac_map_iter_new/next/free` directly (no intermediate Vec), fail-closed to the eager path unless (a) the element type is a primitive Copy type (no per-key drop / no borrow-escape of a String key) AND (b) the loop body does not mutate or reassign the map place (borrow safety during iteration). A fully Rust-competitive version would further INLINE the KaracMap bucket scan (tombstone-skipping) into the loop like the mono get/insert probes, eliminating the per-key `iter_next` call too. Deferred: real for-loop-lowering change with correctness gates + full x86/arm64 leak verification; not a contained fast-path.
investigation: || PARTIAL FIX + ROOT-CAUSE CORRECTION 2026-07-25 (commit ea6b875). STAYS OPEN. (1) THE EAGER MATERIALIZATION IS GONE. `for k in m.keys()` / `.values()` / `.entries()` over a map place now lowers lazily. The fix needed NO new machinery, contrary to this entry's original FIX SKETCH: `for (k, v) in m` ALREADY drives `karac_map_iter_new/next/free` with no intermediate Vec, and already carries the `FreeMapIter` scope-exit cleanup that makes an early `return` out of the body leak-free (B-2026-07-23-1) — so the deferral reason recorded here ('iterator lifetime cleanup on break/return is leak-prone') was already solved upstream. All that was missing was ROUTING, done as a pattern rewrite in `compile_for` (src/codegen/control_flow_for.rs): `for k in m.keys()` => `for (k, _) in m`, `for v in m.values()` => `for (_, v) in m`, `entries()` => pattern unchanged, then recurse on the receiver. That reuses every existing dispatch path — Identifier / FieldAccess alias minting / SortedMap ascending order / loop frames / labels / per-iteration cleanup. GATE (fail-closed, both halves): the map's key AND value types must be SCALAR. A heap half loses the side-table registration the eager path installed under the loop variable's name — `tests/cli.rs::test_run_derive_message_repeated_string_and_map_roundtrip` caught this immediately, a `Map[String, _]` key loop failing with "no handler for method 'bytes'" — and would also hand the body a BORROW where the eager `keys()` Vec gave it an OWNED deep clone. Heap-half maps keep the eager path unchanged. (2) THE ROOT-CAUSE ATTRIBUTION IN THIS ENTRY IS WRONG, and the correction matters more than the change. The IR confirms the win landed — `@find` in the #170 bench now contains iter_new/iter_next/iter_free and NO `@malloc` — but the WALL CLOCK DID NOT MOVE: ~5.13s (3 runs: 5.13/5.12/5.17) against the equal-safety Rust mirror's ~2.49s (2.49/2.55/3.09) on the same idle container, i.e. still ~2x and if anything wider than the 1.74x recorded here. So the per-call Vec materialization was NOT the dominant cost of the #170 gap, even though the disassembly-confirmed malloc/copy/free was real and is now removed. Do not quote this change as closing the gap. REMAINING SUSPECT (the second half of the original fix sketch, now the whole of it): the per-key `karac_map_iter_next` CALL — ~170 keys x 1.2M finds is ~200M non-inlined calls — versus Rust's inlined, tombstone-skipping bucket walk. The next step is to INLINE the KaracMap bucket scan into the loop the way the mono `get`/`insert` probes already are, eliminating the call entirely. That is where the 2x lives; measure it before believing it. GATES ON THIS CHANGE: codegen E2E 2576/2576, memory_sanitizer 852/852 (x86 Linux, LSan live), cli 532/532, fmt + clippy --all-targets clean. Verified byte-identical interp/build output for keys/values/entries, a struct-field receiver, SortedMap ascending order, String keys (eager path), and `break` out of a lazy keys loop. || DISCRIMINATOR RUN 2026-07-25 — THE WALK IS THE COST, NOT THE PROBE. Measured, not assumed. After the partial fix above failed to move #170, the two live hypotheses were (A) the per-key `karac_map_iter_next` call and (B) probe strategy — karac's scalar bucket probe vs Rust hashbrown's 16-way SIMD group probing — since #170's `find` does ~170 `get`s per call ON TOP of the walk. PROBE that separates them (committed at kara-katas/oracle/map-keys-walk-probe/): #170's exact loop shape, ~170-entry `Map[i64,i64]`, 1.2M outer iterations, but NO `get` in the body, so the only per-key work is the iterator step. The body xors each key with the outer index so the inner walk depends on `i` and neither compiler can hoist it; both versions pay that identical xor and both print 1620243187968. RESULT (container x86, idle, 5 runs each): Kara 1.70/1.71/1.70/1.72/1.73 s vs Rust `-O -C overflow-checks=on` 0.26/0.23/0.23/0.24/0.23 s = ~7.4x, i.e. ~8.3 ns per key vs ~1.13 ns. HYPOTHESIS A CONFIRMED, B NOT IMPLICATED: with the probing removed entirely the gap WIDENS from ~2x to ~7.4x, so the walk alone more than accounts for #170's deficit and the probe needs no work for this bug. MECHANISM (objdump-confirmed): `karac_map_iter_next` is a real `call` per key — it lives in the RUNTIME ARCHIVE, so LLVM cannot inline through it. Each step pays (i) the opaque call, (ii) TWO `ptr::copy_nonoverlapping` writes through out-parameters whose lengths are the RUNTIME-VARIABLE `key_size`/`val_size` loaded from the map header rather than compile-time constants, and (iii) an iterator index living in a heap `Box`, so it is a memory load+store per step instead of a register. ~7 ns of extra work per key — far more than call overhead alone (~1-2 ns) would explain, which is why the earlier back-of-envelope under-predicted it. Contrast: the mono `karac_map_i64_i64_get` IS inlined at -O2 (a `linkonce_odr` function emitted INTO the module, so LLVM sees through it) — it does not even appear in the optimized `main`. That is exactly the shape the walk needs. NEXT STEP (now evidence-backed, was speculative): emit a MONO INLINE BUCKET WALK in codegen — a `linkonce_odr` scan over `capacity` testing `status[i] == BUCKET_OCCUPIED` and loading key/val at statically-known offsets — instead of calling the runtime iterator. All three costs vanish together: typed loads replace the variable-length memcpy, the index stays in a register, and the call disappears. Follow `get_or_emit_map_mono_methods` in src/codegen/maps.rs; the layout is `KaracMap` in runtime/src/map.rs. Gate it the same way the pattern rewrite is gated (scalar key AND value) and keep the runtime iterator for every other shape. PROJECTED PAYOFF, stated as a projection and to be re-measured, not trusted: #170 spends the same 204M walk steps, so removing ~1.4s of walk from its 5.13s would land near ~3.7s against Rust's ~2.49s — roughly 2x down to ~1.5x. Closing the REST of that gap is a separate question about the ~170 gets per call, and hypothesis B is where it would be re-opened, on its own evidence. || FIXED 2026-07-25 (bef6bbc). The discriminator's verdict held: open-coding the bucket scan closed the gap. `for (k, v) in m` — and therefore `for k in m.keys()` after ea6b875 routes it there — now emits the walk INLINE when both halves are scalar: for `slot in 0..capacity`, test `status[slot] == OCCUPIED`, load the halves directly from `kv[slot*stride]` / `kv[slot*stride + key_size]`. Same shape `emit_map_shared_half_rc_dec_walk` and the runtime's `karac_map_free_with_drop_vec` already used, against the offsets pinned by `karac_map_field_offsets_match_codegen`. All three costs identified above vanish together — the opaque call, the variable-length out-parameter memcpys, and the boxed iterator index. BONUS: no iterator is allocated at all, so `break` / early `return` are leak-free without any `FreeMapIter` cleanup on this path. MEASURED (container x86, idle, same-session numbers on both sides — never mixing snapshots): walk-only probe kara 1.70s -> 0.32s vs Rust 0.27s, i.e. 7.4x -> 1.19x; LeetCode #170 5.13s -> 3.56s vs Rust 2.97s, i.e. 2.06x -> 1.20x. That BEAT the 1.5x projection recorded above. Both outputs byte-identical to their references. GATES: codegen E2E 2576/2576, memory_sanitizer 852/852 (x86 Linux, LSan live), cli 532/532, fmt + clippy --all-targets clean. SCOPE / WHAT IS STILL ON THE RUNTIME ITERATOR (deliberate, fail-closed): a HEAP half (String/Vec key or value) needs the per-element clone/drop the runtime path performs, and `SortedMap` keeps its ascending-order path. Extending the inline walk to heap halves is a separate slice and would have to carry the clone/drop semantics with it. Loads are emitted at alignment 1 because a mixed-width map (`Map[i32, i64]`) puts the value half at a `key_size` offset with no natural alignment guarantee. RESIDUAL ~1.2x: not chased. Whether it is the remaining ~170 gets per call (hypothesis B, hashbrown SIMD group probing vs karac's scalar probe) or loop-shape differences is UNMEASURED — do not assume, re-run kara-katas/oracle/map-keys-walk-probe/ style isolation before opening anything on it.
resolution: Inline map bucket walk for scalar-halved for-loops (bef6bbc), on top of the lazy keys()/values()/entries() routing (ea6b875).

title: `u8 as char` was rejected at typecheck with E_INT_AS_CHAR even though it is the ONE infallible integer→char cast — every byte (0..=255) is a valid Unicode scalar (the Latin-1 block: no surrogates, far below 0x10FFFF), exactly the cast Rust permits directly. The blanket `is_integer(from) && to == char` rejection applied the wider-integer rationale (surrogates / >0x10FFFF) to u8, where it is vacuous. Separately, the interpreter's `cast_value` had no `char` target arm, so once the cast was permitted `n as char` in the tree-walk interpreter left a `Value::Int` instead of a `Value::Char` — a latent run-vs-build divergence (`String.push(b as char)` appended nothing and `f"{c}"` printed the codepoint under `--interp`, while codegen produced the character).
detail: SOURCE NOTE: surfaced authoring the #290 Word Pattern kata (a deliberately Map[String]/Vec[String]-heavy pick to stress under-exercised surfaces). `split_words` used the natural `cur.push(b as char)` over a `Slice[u8]`; typecheck rejected it with E_INT_AS_CHAR. TWO defects: (1) TYPECHECK false-positive — src/typechecker.rs check_cast_pair blanket-rejected every integer→char cast; u8→char is infallible and should be allowed (Rust's only permitted numeric→char cast). Fix: carve-out `matches!(from, Type::UInt(UIntSize::U8)) && to == Char => return` BEFORE the blanket rejection; wider ints (u16/u32/i64/…) still rejected. Codegen already lowered it correctly (a plain zext: char is i32, u8 unsigned), so no codegen change was needed. (2) INTERPRETER run-vs-build divergence, exposed once (1) permitted the cast — src/interpreter/eval_expr.rs cast_value's int_from closure had no `char` arm, so it fell to `_ => Value::Int(i)`; verified with a minimal probe (`100u8 as char`: interp printed `100` / `String.push` no-op → empty word; build printed `d`/`dog`). Fix: add `"char" => Value::Char(char::from_u32(i as u32).unwrap_or('\u{FFFD}'))` (total on 0..=255). Post-fix the #290 kata is byte-identical across interp/JIT/auto-par/seq and matches the oracle. Tests: tests/typechecker.rs::cast_u8_as_char_accepted; tests/codegen.rs::e2e_u8_as_char_builds_the_character. Suite green: lib 989, typechecker cast_ 25, codegen E2E 2576, clippy(+llvm)+fmt clean.

title: USE-AFTER-FREE under codegen: a RECURSIVE function taking an OWNED `String` parameter whose argument is an ELEMENT of a `Vec[String]` obtained from a `Map[String, Vec[String]]`, where the parameter is USED AFTER the recursive descent, reads freed String buffers. `karac build` prints garbage bytes for the affected elements; `karac run` (LLJIT) aborts inside `karac_string_clone` with a `ptr::copy_nonoverlapping` unaligned/non-null precondition violation. The tree-walk interpreter is CORRECT, so this is also a run-vs-build divergence. Silent data corruption (no crash) under AOT build makes it high severity.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: surfaced authoring LeetCode #332 Reconstruct Itinerary (a deliberately Map[String, Vec[String]]-shaped pick to stress nested heap-owning collections — the surface-driven kata strategy). COMMITTED REPRO: kara-katas/oracle/recursive-owned-string-param-uaf/repro.kara (~35 lines, self-contained, no deps). Expected (interp + true answer): route.len=6, [0]=SFO [1]=ATL [2]=SFO [3]=JFK [4]=ATL [5]=JFK. Observed under `karac build` (and KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0, identical): indices 1..4 are freed-buffer garbage, e.g. [1]=Rq\xef\xbf\xbd, [3]='  ['; indices 0 and 5 happen to survive. Under `karac run` (LLJIT) the process aborts non-unwinding in karac_string_clone (runtime/src/clone.rs:80) via core::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping's UB precondition check. ABLATION (each ingredient removed individually still PASSES, so all four are required): (1) RECURSION — a non-recursive callee that pushes the param immediately is fine; (2) OWNED `String` param — the argument is `dests[used]`, an element read out of a Vec; (3) the source Vec must be MAP-DERIVED (`adj.get(airport)`) — a Vec returned from a plain factory fn does NOT reproduce, nor does a map-derived Vec without recursion; (4) DEFERRED USE — the param is pushed AFTER the recursive loop (`route.push(airport)` below the `while`), so it must outlive the frame-local `dests`. Probes nest6/nest7/nest8 in the session scratchpad each isolate one ingredient and all pass. FIX HYPOTHESIS: the owned `String` parameter is being passed as a BORROW into the map-derived `Vec`'s element storage rather than a cloned/moved owned String; each recursive frame's `dests` local (a fresh Vec materialized by `Map.get`) is dropped at the end of its loop iteration / frame, freeing the element buffers that deeper-or-later uses of the surviving `airport` parameter still point at. Suspect the ref_arg_index_borrow_ptr / borrowed-arg elision path (src/codegen/collections.rs) classifying `dests[used]` as an in-place element borrow — correct for a `ref T` parameter, WRONG for an owned `String` parameter that outlives the container. Any fix must be verified under memory_sanitizer on BOTH x86 and arm64 (this is exactly the codegen-ownership class the LSan gates exist for). CONSEQUENCE: LeetCode #332 is held out of the kata corpus until this is fixed — shipping it would violate the corpus's A/B run==build invariant.
investigation: REFINED 2026-07-25 (session 2). ROOT CAUSE NARROWED to the element READ, not argument passing. ABLATION: binding the element to a local first — `let next = dests[used]; visit(adj, cursor, next, route);` — still corrupts identically, so the call-site arg path (ref_arg_index_borrow_ptr and friends) is NOT the culprit; all of its call sites were also read and confirmed correctly gated behind `is_ref`. THEORY (consistent with every probe): reading a heap-bearing element out of a container (`dests[used]` on a `Vec[String]`) yields a SHALLOW copy of the element's {ptr,len,cap} that SHARES the heap buffer with the container, which still owns and will free it. Whenever that shallow copy outlives the container the buffer dangles. This also explains why the non-recursive ablations (nest6/nest7/nest8) PASS: they have the same latent sharing, but no allocation happens between the container's free and the read, so the freed bytes are still intact — the recursion in the real shape interleaves many allocations after each frame's `dests` is freed, so the memory is reused and the corruption becomes visible. The passing ablations are therefore NOT evidence of correctness, only of non-manifestation. IMPLICATION FOR THE FIX: this is an ownership-model change at the element-read site (clone a heap-bearing element when the read escapes the container's lifetime), not a contained call-site patch — it interacts with the existing borrow-elision / clone-on-move machinery and must not introduce double-frees or leaks. Deliberately NOT attempted under low remaining context: a speculative clone insertion here fails either as a double-free or as a leak. Verify any fix under memory_sanitizer on x86 AND arm64. || ABLATION MATRIX (session 2, continued) — two further decisive negatives that narrow the trigger to a COMBINATION rather than any single mechanism: (A) MAP-FREE RECURSION PASSES. A recursive fn with the identical shape but a plain factory-returned local `Vec[String]` instead of a map — `fn rec(depth, s: String, out: mut ref Vec[String]) { if depth>0 { let d = make(); rec(depth-1, d[0], out); } out.push(s); }` at depth 4 — is CORRECT under build. So the general 'element read yields a shallow copy' theory in the note above is NOT sufficient on its own: the same recursion + element-read + deferred-push shape over a non-map container is fine. The Map is REQUIRED. (B) PLAIN MAP-DERIVED DROP PASSES. Pulling the value into a local that dies at end of function, twice, then re-reading the map — `fn touch(adj: mut ref Map[String, Vec[String]]) { let d: Vec[String] = match adj.get("k") {...}; }` called twice, then read `adj` again — leaves the map intact under build. So it is ALSO not a simple 'dropping a Map.get result frees the map's buffer' double-free. NET: the trigger requires map-derived values AND recursion together; neither the element-read path nor Map.get's value ownership is wrong in isolation. Next step for whoever picks this up: dump the pre-opt IR for the committed repro and diff the drop/cleanup emission for `dests` between the recursive frame and the (correct) non-recursive shape — the suspicion is a per-frame cleanup registration that is emitted once but runs against a value the recursive callee has already consumed or re-materialized. Probe files u2/u3/u4 in the session scratchpad correspond to ablations (local-binding / map-free / plain-drop) respectively. || ROOT CAUSE FOUND (pre-opt IR diff, session 2). Dumped pre-opt IR for the failing repro and for the passing map-free ablation and diffed the free/clone emission inside the recursive function. The failing `@visit` contains a block the passing `@rec` does NOT: `freearg.free: call void @free(ptr %freearg.ptr)`, whose predecessor is `map.ins.some` — i.e. it runs on the KEY-ALREADY-EXISTS path of `Map.insert`. The freed value is extracted as fields 0 (ptr) and 2 (cap) of a {ptr,len,cap} struct, and `cursor`'s VALUE type is plain `i64` (not heap), so the struct being freed is the passed KEY, not the old value. MECHANISM: on `map.insert(k, v)` where `k` is already present, the map retains its existing key copy and codegen frees the redundant just-passed key buffer via `free_str_vec_buffer_if_heap` (src/codegen/runtime.rs:1887, reached from the old-value/redundant-key drop path around :1868). That is correct when the key argument is a fresh TEMPORARY the caller does not retain — and WRONG when it is a variable or parameter the caller still uses. In the repro `cursor.insert(airport, used + 1i64)` runs once per loop iteration with the SAME `airport`, so from the second iteration on the key exists and `airport`'s buffer is freed — while `airport` is the function's owned String parameter that is pushed into `route` AFTER the loop. Hence route holds freed memory. This explains EVERY ablation: no map => no insert => no free; no recursion => the same key is not re-inserted while still live; plain Map.get create/drop => no insert at all; binding the element to a local does not help because the free is on the insert path, not the argument path. FIX DIRECTION: gate the redundant-key free on the key argument being a consumable temporary (an rvalue the caller does not retain) rather than a live place expression — the consume/temporary classification in src/codegen/consume_class.rs looks like the right oracle. Alternative: always store a cloned key and never free the caller's. Verify under memory_sanitizer x86 AND arm64: the wrong gate direction turns this UAF into a leak. || RETRACTION 2026-07-25 (session 3) — THE PREVIOUS 'ROOT CAUSE' IS WRONG AND IS HEREBY WITHDRAWN. Session 2 concluded from an LLVM IR diff that `Map.insert` frees a LIVE key on the key-already-exists path (`map.ins.some` → `freearg.free` in src/codegen/maps.rs:1771 / runtime.rs:1887), i.e. that `cursor.insert(airport, used+1)` frees the owned `String` parameter `airport`. That is NOT what the compiler emits. METHODOLOGY DEFECT that produced the wrong answer: the throwaway `examples/dump_ir.rs` harness used to obtain that IR called parse → resolve → typecheck → ownershipcheck → codegen but SKIPPED `lowering::lower_program`. Lowering is what forwards the typechecker's SPAN-KEYED side tables into the AST (`pattern_binding_types`, `pattern_binding_inner_types`, the Str-span table, … — src/lowering.rs:259ff), so without it codegen sees an EMPTY `pattern_binding_types` and degrades every match-arm payload binding to the 1-word i64 default. The unlowered dump therefore showed `%dests = alloca i64` GEP'd as a 24-byte `{ptr,i64,i64}` (a spectacular-looking stack OOB) and a `matchval`-less `match.merge` — BOTH artifacts of the broken harness, present in a probe that RUNS CORRECTLY. Re-dumping WITH `lower_program` gives the correct `%dests = alloca { ptr, i64, i64 }` and a real `%matchval` phi. LESSON (generalizes to any future IR investigation): an IR-dump harness MUST run `lower_program` or its output is not the IR the compiler actually emits — prefer reproducing through the real driver over a hand-rolled phase chain. WHAT THE CORRECTED IR ACTUALLY SHOWS: the value freed at `map.ins.some` is `%dcopy.result`, the DEFENSIVE COPY that `maybe_defensive_copy_param_arg` makes of the owned-`String` param key (src/codegen/maps.rs ‘insert’ arm), and the free is guarded on `cap > 0`; `%dcopy.result` is a phi that passes `%airport` through UNCHANGED only when `cap == 0`, in which case the guard suppresses the free. So the redundant-key free is BALANCED and is not the bug. The duplicate-key leak fix B-2026-06-20-9 that emits it is intact. STATUS: root cause is once again UNKNOWN. Still-valid evidence: the four-ingredient ablation matrix above (recursion + owned String param + map-derived Vec element + deferred use), the committed repro, and the run-vs-build divergence. Discard only the session-2 `Map.insert`/live-key conclusion and the session-2 'element read yields a shallow copy' theory (already disproved as insufficient by ablation A). NEXT STEP for whoever picks this up: dump IR through a harness that includes lowering (examples/dump_ir.rs now does) and diff the failing `@visit` against the passing map-free `@rec` again — the earlier diff was run on unrepresentative IR and must be redone from scratch. || ASAN-DRIVEN NARROWING 2026-07-25 (session 3, after the retraction above) — first HARD evidence, replacing IR-reading with a sanitizer verdict. Method: a temporary #[test] in tests/memory_sanitizer.rs driving `run_under_asan_with_full_pipeline` on the committed repro (Linux, so LSan/ASan both live). VERDICT: heap-use-after-free; 4-byte region; ALLOCATED BY `karac_string_clone`; FREED from `visit`; READ by `memcpy` of size 3 in `main` (an f-string printing `route[i]`, i.e. a 3-char airport code). Reproduced identically at KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=0, so it is not an optimizer artifact. With `fast_unwind_on_malloc=0:malloc_context_size=30` the free stack is `free ← visit ← visit ← visit ← visit ← main` — the leak is reached at recursion depth 4. (1) THE `Map.insert` REDUNDANT-KEY FREE IS DEFINITIVELY EXONERATED — causally, not just by reading. Disabling `free_str_vec_buffer_if_heap(kv)` at src/codegen/maps.rs:1771 removes the ONLY direct `call void @free` from `@visit` (verified by dumping IR under the patch: count drops to 0), and the ASan report is BYTE-IDENTICAL. So the free attributed to `visit` is a TAIL CALL from the runtime's `karac_free_buf` (a tail jmp pushes no frame, so ASan credits the caller) — i.e. one of `visit`'s Vec/String element-drop sites, which is the `dests` scope-exit drop. Beware this attribution trap when reading ASan output for Kara binaries: a `visit`-attributed `free` may be any `karac_free_buf` the function emits. (2) PRIME SUSPECT, independently reproducible in 7 lines: the recursive call `visit(adj, cursor, dests[used], route)` lowers to a bare `%v.elem = load { ptr, i64, i64 }` of the element followed by `call void @visit({ ptr, i64, i64 } %v.elem, …)` — NO CLONE. The element header is passed as a shallow alias into the caller's `dests` buffer, which `visit` drops (elements included) right after the call returns. MINIMAL REPRO of the missing clone (no map, no recursion): `fn take(s: String, out: mut ref Vec[String]) { out.push(s); }` called as `take(v[0], mut out)` emits `%v.elem = load …; call void @take(%v.elem, …)` with no clone. That case does not crash only because the callee's `out.push(s)` defensively copies the owned param on the way in — the alias is latent, not benign. (3) WHY: `maybe_defensive_copy_param_arg` (src/codegen/runtime.rs:3344) opens with exactly the intended guard — `expr_is_heap_vec_index(arg_expr)` → `clone_owned_vec_index_element` — and its doc comment claims coverage of the 'owned call arg' sink. But every call site of that helper is an ENUM-CONSTRUCTOR payload (src/codegen/call_dispatch.rs:2677, 2771, 2973, 3018); a plain free-function call argument never routes through it. So the B-2026-07-04-2 / B-2026-07-05-1 element-clone fix covers tuple literals, push, struct fields, map values and enum payloads, but NOT the by-value argument of an ordinary call. NEXT STEP: extend the owned-arg consume path to run `maybe_defensive_copy_param_arg` (or at least the `expr_is_heap_vec_index` → `clone_owned_vec_index_element` leg) for by-value heap params at ordinary call sites, then re-run the ASan probe. GATE: the wrong gate direction converts this UAF into a leak, so memory_sanitizer must be green on x86 AND arm64 (`scripts/lsan-local.sh` for the latter) before this is called fixed. The temporary ASan probe was NOT committed; re-create it from the repro at kara-katas/oracle/recursive-owned-string-param-uaf/repro.kara — and promote it to a permanent regression test with the fix. || CAVEAT ON SUSPECT (2), same session — do NOT start by 'fixing' the missing call-site clone without re-reading the ABI. src/codegen/call_dispatch.rs (~line 1573) documents the by-value convention explicitly: an owned `String`/`Vec` parameter is CALLER-RETAINS — the callee never frees it (such params land in `owned_vecstr_params` and get a defensive deep-copy at each RETAINING consume site, never a callee-side `track_vec_var`). Under that convention passing `dests[used]` as a bare element alias is BY DESIGN, not obviously a defect, and the `take(v[0], mut out)` minimal case is memory-correct end-to-end precisely because the callee's `out.push(s)` deep-copies on the way in. So suspect (2) may be consistent with the ABI rather than the bug. UNRESOLVED TENSION that the next attempt should start from, since it is what actually pins the defect: in the repro `route.push(airport)` DOES emit the defensive copy (the `while.exit` → `dcopy.copy` → `store %dcopy.result123` chain in `@visit`), and every element cloned by `karac_string_clone` carries `cap == len > 0` (runtime/src/clone.rs allocates len+1 bytes — hence the 4-byte region for a 3-char code — and sets cap = len), so the `cap > 0` guard on that copy is TAKEN. Every entry `route` receives should therefore be a fresh `malloc` from `@visit`, yet ASan reports `main` reading a block allocated by `karac_string_clone`. One of those three statements is false: either some `route.push` path bypasses the copy, or `route` is written by something other than that push, or the freed/read block reaches `main` by a route other than `route[i]`. Resolve THAT before touching codegen — printing the element pointers at each push and at each drop is the cheapest discriminator. || RESOLVED 2026-07-25 (session 3) — fix 7ae1e2e. ROOT CAUSE (confirmed by ASan before and after, and by a four-variant discriminator matrix): an OWNED `String`/`Vec` param consumed TWICE in one function. Owned Vec/String params are CALLER-RETAINS — the callee registers no `FreeVecBuffer` for them (hence `owned_vecstr_params`, not `track_vec_var`) and each retaining consume deep-copies via `maybe_defensive_copy_param_arg` — so the param's buffer is never moved out and there is NO cleanup to suppress. But `suppress_source_vec_cleanup_for_arg_ex` (src/codegen/call_dispatch.rs, the Identifier/`move.cap.p` arm) zeroed the param header's `cap` anyway. That zero is the ownership bit the NEXT consume reads: with `cap == 0` the second consume treats the param as a borrowed view, SKIPS its defensive copy, and stores a raw alias. In the repro `cursor.insert(airport, used+1)` is consume #1 (zeroes cap) and `route.push(airport)` after the recursive descent is consume #2 (stores an alias into the caller's map-derived `Vec[String]` element, freed the moment the recursive call returns). FIX: skip the cap-zero when the root identifier is in `owned_vecstr_params`. RESOLVES THE ARITHMETIC TENSION recorded above — the defensive copy at `route.push` IS emitted and `karac_string_clone` DOES set cap = len > 0, but by the time the push runs the SLOT's cap has been overwritten with 0 by the earlier insert, so the guard reads 0 and the copy is skipped. RE-READING THE ORIGINAL ABLATION: the 'four required ingredients' were real but mostly staging. Recursion + a map-derived source Vec + use-after-descent are what make the aliased buffer actually DIE before it is read; the Map mattered only because `cursor.insert(airport, ...)` supplied the FIRST of the two consumes. The true minimal trigger is 'owned heap param consumed twice, second consume outliving the first consume's source' — much smaller than the shape the ablation suggested. LESSON: an ablation matrix bounds where a bug MANIFESTS, not what causes it; every ingredient there was necessary for the crash and only one was necessary for the defect. GATES: memory_sanitizer 852/852 green on x86 Linux (LSan live — the fix closes the UAF without converting it to a leak), codegen E2E 2576/2576, cli 532/532, fmt + clippy --all-targets clean. The repro now prints SFO ATL SFO JFK ATL JFK identically under all four surfaces (interp / LLJIT run / build / KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0 build). REGRESSION TEST: `asan_owned_string_param_consumed_twice_no_uaf` in tests/memory_sanitizer.rs. LeetCode #332 is unblocked. COLLATERAL: the full-suite run also caught `run_value_corrupting_cast_aborts` (tests/cli.rs) failing — NOT from this fix but from this session's earlier B-2026-07-24-3 `u8 as char` carve-out, which made that test's premise obsolete; repinned to an `i64` source in the same commit. SEPARATE PRE-EXISTING FAILURE, not caused by either fix and left open: `coro_e2e::coroutine_method_handler_services_connection` fails identically on a clean tree in this container ('could not connect to 127.0.0.1:<port> to trigger accept') — looks environmental (sandbox networking), needs confirmation on CI.

title: Match-arm type unification does not bind an unsolved type variable inside a generic: `match m.get(k) { Some(d) => d, None => Vec.new() }` is rejected with "match arms have incompatible types: 'Vec<String>' and 'Vec<?T0>'" instead of solving `?T0 := String` from the sibling arm. An explicit annotation on the enclosing `let` propagates correctly, so only the arm-to-arm direction is missing.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: hit while authoring LeetCode #332 (same kata as B-2026-07-25-1). MINIMAL REPRO: `let mut m: Map[String, Vec[String]] = Map.new(); let got = match m.get("k") { Some(d) => d, None => Vec.new() };` → error[typecheck] match arms have incompatible types: 'Vec<String>' and 'Vec<?T0>'. CONTROL: adding the annotation (`let got: Vec[String] = match …`) typechecks and runs correctly on every surface, so expected-type propagation INTO the arms works; only sibling-arm unification is missing. MECHANISM: the arm fold (src/typechecker/patterns.rs ~line 297, `join_branch_types`) gates on `types_compatible_with_projections`, and `types_compatible` (src/typechecker/types.rs) has a permissive wildcard arm for `Type::TypeParam` (line 1273) but NO corresponding arm for `Type::TypeVar` — despite the comment directly above it claiming the rule is "Equivalent to the `TypeVar` handling below" (that handling does not exist in the function). So `Vec<String>` vs `Vec<?T0>` fails the invariant generic-arg check and the join returns None. Note `merge_branch_types` ALREADY prefers the concrete side over a TypeVar, so once the compatibility gate admits the pair the result type would come out `Vec[String]` correctly. FIX OPTIONS: (a) narrow — in `join_branch_types`, admit pairs that are equal modulo unsolved TypeVars and let `merge_branch_types` pick the concrete side (contained to branch joins: match arms + if/else); (b) broad — add a `TypeVar` wildcard arm to `types_compatible` mirroring `TypeParam`, which is what the stale comment implies was intended, but that weakens a core predicate used across the typechecker and needs care. Prefer (a). SEVERITY low: fails closed (a rejection, never a miscompile), and the annotated form is already the established Kāra idiom since every bare `Vec.new()` requires an annotation anyway.
resolution: Added `same_shape_modulo_typevars` (src/typechecker.rs) and a second arm in `join_branch_types`: when the two branch types are structurally identical except at unsolved `TypeVar` positions, admit the pair so `merge_branch_types` (which already prefers the concrete leaf) solves the slot from the sibling arm. Scoped to the branch join rather than loosening the global `types_compatible` predicate, so no other check is weakened. Fails closed — different head (Vec vs Map), different arity, or two concrete leaves (String vs i64) all still rejected. Tests: match_arms_bind_typevar_from_sibling_arm + match_arms_with_different_generic_heads_still_rejected. Suite green: lib 990, typechecker 2091, codegen E2E 2576, clippy+fmt clean.

title: SELFHOST EMITTER (codegen.kara, Phase-12 port): statement-position `v.pop()` was a NO-OP — a non-push statement method call fell through to `emit_method_value` (which does nothing for `pop`), so the vec never shrank. Not harmless: the port's own `self.loop_cont.pop()` / `loop_break.pop()` maintain the loop-label stacks, so a no-op pop leaves stale entries and mis-resolves `break`/`continue` for subsequent loops.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: found by real-shape differential probing (Vec-method sweep) vs the seed `karac run` oracle. IN-SURFACE: all 12 `.pop()` sites in the port are `self.loop_cont.pop()` / `self.loop_break.pop()` in STATEMENT position (return discarded) on Vec[String] — the loop-label stacks the emitter pushes/pops around each loop; a no-op pop corrupts `break`/`continue` target resolution for later loops. FIX (Slice 57, 21a6eed): a `pop` arm in emit_stmt's MethodCall handling that loads {ptr,len,cap} and, GUARDED by `len > 0` (empty pop = no-op, matching the seed; the guard also prevents a wild element-free and a len underflow), writes back {ptr, len-1, cap}. Vec[String] (kind 4) loads+frees the popped element buffer first (leak-clean under the oracle's valgrind leg); Vec[i64] (kind 3) just decrements. Vec-of-struct/enum pop has no port site; VALUE-position pop (consuming the returned Option[T]) is out of surface — the port never reads a pop result.
resolution: Fixed in Slice 57 (21a6eed): guarded pop arm shrinking {ptr,len,cap}, Vec[String] frees the popped element. Selfhost oracle (corpus 172) + valgrind green.

title: USE-AFTER-FREE under codegen (sibling of B-2026-07-25-1, NOT closed by it): the natural LeetCode #332 Hierholzer walk over a `Map[String, Vec[String]]` whose KEYS are heap `String`s read out of a `ref Vec[String]` param corrupts the accumulated route. Interior entries are freed-buffer garbage under `karac build`; `karac run` (LLJIT) aborts inside `karac_string_clone`. The tree-walk interpreter is correct, so it is also a run-vs-build divergence.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: surfaced immediately after B-2026-07-25-1 was fixed, while adding the LeetCode #332 kata that bug had been blocking — the fix made the minimal repro pass but NOT the full kata. COMMITTED REPRO: kara-katas/oracle/itinerary-heap-map-key-uaf/repro.kara with oracle.py alongside. Expected (interp, and oracle.py): `JFK -> MUC -> LHR -> SFO -> SJC` / `JFK -> ATL -> JFK -> SFO -> ATL -> SFO` / same / `JFK -> AAA`. Observed under `karac build` (and KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0, identical): first case prints `JFK -> JFK -> JFK -> JFK -> SJC` — first and last entries survive, the interior collapses; later cases print raw freed bytes. `karac check` is clean apart from one perf[rc-fallback] note on `airport` (direct re-use after consume) — see INVESTIGATION.
investigation: NARROWED, root cause NOT yet identified. Each piece is CORRECT in isolation under `karac build`; only the whole chain fails: (a) the graph build alone (`adj.get(froms[i])` -> `d.push(tos[i])` -> `adj.insert(froms[i], d)` in a loop) is correct; (b) the sort pass alone (read each key's Vec, `sort()`, write back through `adj.insert(keys[k], d)`) is correct; (c) the B-2026-07-25-1 repro — the SAME recursive `visit` — is correct since that fix. LOCALIZATION: `route` is already corrupt INSIDE `find_itinerary`, immediately after `visit` returns and before the reversal loop, so neither the reversal (`out.push(route[j])`) nor the `show` string concat is implicated; the damage happens during the recursive walk. THE ONE STRUCTURAL DIFFERENCE from the fixed sibling: that repro seeded its map from string LITERALS in `main` (`adj.insert("JFK", a)`) — rodata keys with `cap == 0`, which every cap-guarded defensive-copy and free path treats as a borrowed view — whereas here the keys are `froms[i]`, HEAP `String` elements read out of a `ref Vec[String]` param, so `cap > 0` and those paths all take their live arms. That is the LEADING HYPOTHESIS, explicitly not a conclusion: it is the difference between the passing and failing programs, but no experiment yet shows it is the cause. NOTE FOR THE NEXT ATTEMPT: the ownership checker already emits `perf[rc-fallback]` for `airport` ("direct re-use after consume; consume at the `cursor.insert` line, other use at the `route.push` line") — it SEES the double-consume shape that caused B-2026-07-25-1, so cross-checking what codegen does with that hint is a cheap first move. Method that worked for the sibling and should be reused: drive the repro through `run_under_asan_with_full_pipeline` in tests/memory_sanitizer.rs for a sanitizer verdict (Linux, LSan live) rather than reading IR, and remember the attribution trap recorded on B-2026-07-25-1 — a `free` credited to a Kara function may be a tail call from the runtime's `karac_free_buf`. Dump IR with `cargo run --features llvm --example dump_ir` (it runs `lower_program`; a hand-rolled phase chain that skips lowering produces IR the compiler never emits). CONSEQUENCE: LeetCode #332 remains held out of the kata corpus — shipping it would violate the corpus's A/B run==build invariant. || RETRACTED 2026-07-25, same session, one commit after filing. THIS BUG DOES NOT EXIST. The LeetCode #332 program matches its Python reference BYTE-FOR-BYTE under all four surfaces (`karac run --interp`, `karac run` LLJIT, default auto-par `karac build`, and `KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0 karac build`) once compiled by a correctly built `karac`. The kata is now in the corpus at kara-katas/leetcode/301-400/332-reconstruct-itinerary/ and the oracle probe has been deleted. WHY THE FALSE POSITIVE: the ephemeral cloud container REWOUND the local `kara` checkout to an old commit (8ee88f5) mid-session — three separate times — while the session's commits remained safe on origin. A rebuild that happened while the tree was rewound produced a `target/debug/karac` WITHOUT the B-2026-07-25-1 owned-param cap-zero fix. Every measurement taken with that binary — the '#332 kata still fails' finding, the heap-vs-literal map-key ablation, and the h1/hA/hB narrowing that appeared to implicate heap map keys — was reproducing the ALREADY-FIXED bug, not a sibling of it. After `git reset --hard origin/main` plus a full `cargo build --features llvm`, all of those variants pass. LESSON (the operational sibling of the dump_ir lesson on B-2026-07-25-1): a measurement is only as trustworthy as the toolchain that produced it. In an environment where the checkout can move underneath you, verify BEFORE measuring — `git rev-parse HEAD` against `origin/main`, and confirm the fix under test is actually present in the source (`grep` for its marker comment) — then rebuild. A green-then-red flip with no intervening source edit is a toolchain-provenance signal, not a new bug.
resolution: INVALID — filed against a STALE COMPILER BINARY, retracted the same day.

title: `for k in m.keys()` (and `.values()`/`.entries()`) STILL eagerly materializes an owned `Vec` per evaluation when either map half is a HEAP type (`Map[String, _]`, `Map[_, Vec[_]]`). B-2026-07-24-2's inline bucket walk and its lazy keys() routing are both gated to SCALAR halves, so the originally-reported malloc + full-set copy + free — plus a DEEP CLONE of every heap key — is unchanged for the heap case, which is if anything the more expensive one.
resolution: Did step (a) exactly as this entry's FIX DIRECTION prescribed, and it was indeed the bulk of the win. The two concerns that had gated heap halves out are both answered by the DESTINATION path rather than by the gate: (1) registration — `compile_for_map_var` calls `register_for_loop_bindings`, whose Tuple arm registers the key half from `map_key_type_exprs` and the value half from `var_elem_type_exprs`, the same tables the eager path installs, so `k.bytes()`/`k.len()` still dispatch; (2) owned-vs-borrow — the same call does `mark_for_loop_borrow_if_heap`, putting the binding in `for_loop_borrow_vars`, the defensive-copy-at-consume machinery every other heap for-loop element already uses. `map_place_is_iterable` now requires the half TYPE-EXPR tables instead of scalar LLVM types, so a map codegen cannot describe still fails closed to the eager path. Step (b) (extending the inline BUCKET WALK to heap halves) was deliberately NOT done: that walk keeps its own separate scalar gate because a heap half needs the runtime iterator's per-element clone/drop, so a heap-halved map lands on the LAZY `karac_map_iter_new`/`_next`/`_free` walk — no Vec and no per-key deep clone, which is the win — while the zero-call bucket walk stays a scalar-only optimization. SECOND DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED IN THE SAME SLICE: a SINGLE binding over `.entries()` (`for e in m.entries() { … e.0 … }`, what `#[derive(Message)]` emits for a Map field) must NOT be rewritten — it wants one tuple VALUE per step, which only the eager materializer produces; routing it to the pair-binding path bound `e` to the value half and left `e.0` unregistered, reproducing this entry's predicted 'no handler for method bytes' failure. Only a real 2-tuple pattern is rewritten now; that condition is type-independent, so it also closes the same latent hole for a scalar-halved map. MEASURED (fresh probe, not the scalar one — per this entry's instruction): hot `keys()` walk over a 170-entry `Map[String, i64]`, 20k non-hoistable evaluations — 0.148s -> 0.034s, ~4.3x, identical output; IR shows `@malloc` / `@karac_map_len` / `@karac_clone_String` / `@karac_free_buf` all gone from the loop. GATES (all the ones this entry named): cli 532 green INCLUDING `test_run_derive_message_repeated_string_and_map_roundtrip`; 4-backend agreement (interp/JIT/AOT-O2/AOT-O0) over heap key, heap value, both-heap struct FIELD, a consuming sink (`owned.push(k)`), an early `return` out of the loop body, and the source map intact afterwards; codegen 2586 (3 new tests: an IR guard asserting the materializer is ABSENT, a behavioural sweep over every heap shape, and a guard pinning the single-binding `entries()` shape), memory_sanitizer 854, par_codegen 200, interpreter 1307, typechecker 2091, lib 990, selfhost_codegen oracle; clippy (both feature sets) + fmt clean. LEAK CHECK: valgrind on the heap-shape sweep is BYTE-IDENTICAL before and after this change (1 byte definitely lost, 9 contexts, both builds), i.e. leak-neutral; that residual is a separate PRE-EXISTING bug filed as B-2026-07-27-2. NOT DONE (arm64): only the x86 leg was run in this container — the entry asked for arm64 memory_sanitizer too, which the CI `memory-sanitizer-arm64` job covers.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: split out of B-2026-07-24-2 when closing it, after verifying the residual rather than assuming the scope note covered it. IR EVIDENCE (`examples/dump_ir`, commit 09dfeb6): for `fn total(m: ref Map[String, i64]) { for k in m.keys() { s = s + k.len(); } }` the emitted `@total` still contains `@malloc`, `@karac_map_len`, `@karac_map_iter_new`/`_next`/`_free` and two `@karac_free_buf` — i.e. the complete eager build-then-iterate-then-free, with the second `free_buf` being the per-element String drop. A scalar-halved map at the same commit emits none of those (bucket walk inlined, zero calls).
investigation: WHY IT IS GATED OUT (deliberate, not an oversight): both B-2026-07-24-2 legs fail closed on a heap half for DIFFERENT reasons, and each has to be answered separately. (1) The lazy keys() ROUTING (ea6b875) rewrites `for k in m.keys()` to `for (k, _) in m`; for a heap key that loses the side-table registration the eager path installs under the loop variable's name — caught immediately by `tests/cli.rs::test_run_derive_message_repeated_string_and_map_roundtrip`, which failed with "no handler for method 'bytes'" — and it would hand the body a BORROW where the eager `keys()` Vec gave it an OWNED deep clone, changing move semantics. (2) The inline BUCKET WALK (bef6bbc) loads each half with a plain typed load; a heap half needs the per-element clone/drop the runtime path performs, which is the entire reason the eager materializer exists. FIX DIRECTION, in the order that de-risks it: (a) teach the tuple-rewrite path to register a heap half in the String/Vec side tables under the loop variable's name, which is what the eager path already does — that alone makes `for k in stringMap.keys()` lower to the existing LAZY runtime-iterator entries path (no Vec, no deep clones) without touching the inline walk; (b) only then consider extending the inline bucket walk to heap halves, which additionally requires deciding borrow-vs-clone semantics for the binding and carrying the per-element drop. Step (a) is the bulk of the win and is much cheaper than (b). GATES: the registration change is exactly the class `test_run_derive_message_repeated_string_and_map_roundtrip` polices, so run the cli suite first; then codegen E2E + memory_sanitizer on x86 AND arm64, since moving a heap key from owned-clone to borrow is an ownership change (see B-2026-07-25-1 for how that class fails). MEASUREMENT: reuse kara-katas/oracle/map-keys-walk-probe/ with a `Map[String, i64]` variant — do NOT quote the scalar probe's numbers for this case.

title: SELFHOST EMITTER (codegen.kara, Phase-12 port): statement-position `s.push_str(arg)` was a NO-OP — it fell through to `emit_method_value`, which does nothing for push_str, so the receiver String never grew. push_str is the port's DOMINANT string-building primitive (700+ call sites across codegen/ast_render/lexer/resolver/typechecker), so every incremental string build silently produced the empty seed — a hard self-hosting blocker.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: found by real-shape differential probing (String-method sweep) vs the seed `karac run` oracle. By far the most-used unimplemented method (737 `.push_str(` sites; the runners-up `.pop()` at 12 and `.last()` at 2 are tiny by comparison). All receivers are plain LOCAL String identifiers (`out` 517x, `line` 168x, `s`, `text`, …) — none are `self.field` — so only an Ident receiver is handled. FIX (Slice 58, bd6af74): an in-place append in emit_stmt's MethodCall arm — load the receiver slot's {ptr,len}, eval the arg {aptr,alen}, `realloc(ptr, len+alen)` (preserves [0,len); realloc(null,·)=malloc for the empty `"".to_string()` seed), `memcpy` the arg bytes at ptr+len, store {newptr, len+alen} back. Every push_str'd local is an OWNED `.to_string()` buffer, so realloc is safe. A heap-temp arg (a fresh `a + b` concat) is freed after its bytes are copied (leak-clean); a borrowed arg (literal global / ident load) is not. NOTE ON DISCOVERY: a `push_str`-in-a-loop probe with `i += 1` first appeared to crash (runaway realloc), but that was a STALE LOCAL BASE lacking the compound-assign fix (B-2026-07-23-22) — on the correct base both `i = i + 1` and `i += 1` loop-builds match. Value-position push_str result (it returns unit) is irrelevant; statement position is the only shape.
resolution: Fixed in Slice 58 (bd6af74): in-place realloc+memcpy append; heap-temp arg freed after copy. Selfhost oracle + valgrind green.

title: Indexed-receiver method call on a MAP element (`m[k].push(x)`) type-checks and runs correctly under the tree-walk interpreter but is REJECTED by codegen with `indexed-receiver method 'push' on '<m>' — outer is not a Vec/Slice/Array`. A `Vec` outer (`vv[0].push(x)`) works in codegen, so the gap is specific to Map outers, and it reproduces for BOTH heap-keyed (`Map[String, Vec[_]]`) and scalar-keyed (`Map[i64, Vec[_]]`) maps.
resolution:
Fixed in 4416d33 by adding `lower_indexed_elem_ptr_map` to src/codegen/calls.rs and routing a Map outer to it from `compile_indexed_receiver_method`. The gap was narrower than the report implied: `var_elem_type_exprs` is ALREADY populated with the map's VALUE TypeExpr at every Map-registering site (types_lowering.rs and stmts.rs both insert it alongside `map_key_type_exprs`), so the element-TypeExpr resolution already worked for maps — only the element-POINTER lowering was missing. The new helper resolves `m[k]` to the value half of the key's bucket via `karac_map_lookup_slot`, the same runtime entrypoint already backing `entry(k).and_modify(...)`, so no new runtime contract was needed. That pointer aliases the map's kv buffer, which is what MR3 requires for a mutating method to propagate; `karac_map_get` could not serve because it copies the value out into a caller-provided slot. Missing key panics, matching both the `m[k]` read path and the interpreter (the lookup variant never inserts). Key ownership deliberately mirrors `compile_map_index` and does NOT free the key buffer: `lookup_slot` does not adopt it, and the key may be a live binding, where an unconditional free would be a use-after-free rather than a leak fix. Regression test `asan_map_indexed_receiver_push_no_leak` (tests/memory_sanitizer.rs) pins the aliasing shape most likely to double-free or leak — 200 pushes across 7 heap keys, forcing reallocs of the in-bucket Vec, with the key read from a live Vec[String] element — plus a scalar-keyed sibling. Gates: fmt, clippy --all --all-targets --features llvm, codegen 2576, memory_sanitizer 853 (LSan live on Linux), cli 532, non-llvm 8184.

PREDICTION CORRECTED AFTER THE FIX LANDED (2026-07-25). The pre-fix estimate above -- ~52% of kara's #332 deficit attributable to this bug, derived from a graph-shape discriminator (same edge count, max degree 40 -> 1) -- was TOO OPTIMISTIC. Measuring the real fix, both binaries built from the same compiler and run in one hyperfine session (50 runs, warmup 10): copy-back 229.4ms +/- 10.6 (median 227.6) vs in-place 200.7ms +/- 5.5 (median 199.1), against rust 129.9ms. That is ~12.5% wall-clock and ~25% of the gap to Rust closed (23-28% depending on median vs min) -- roughly HALF the predicted improvement. WHY THE DISCRIMINATOR OVERESTIMATED: reshaping the graph removes the O(sum deg^2) copies outright, whereas the fix TRADES them for an extra `contains_key` probe per edge -- the old `get` did double duty as presence check AND value fetch, so the in-place form pays one additional String hash+probe per edge and only recovers part of the copy cost. FOLLOW-UP: a single-lookup `entry(k).or_insert(...).push(x)` chain would avoid the second probe; entry_chains.rs already lowers or_insert/and_modify, so the missing piece is method-chaining off the entry result. Also note absolute times on this container are not stable across sessions (an unmodified rust binary measured 164.1ms and later 123.7-138.1ms), so only same-session A/B comparisons are valid.

title: Overflow check on a BOUNDED loop-accumulator (`cnt = cnt + 1` guarded by an if, inside a counted loop) is not elided, and because a checked add can trap it cannot be speculated — which blocks LLVM's if-conversion of `if bit { cnt += 1 }` into the branchless `cnt += bit`. On random data the surviving conditional branch mispredicts ~50% of the time, costing 7.9x on a per-bit counting loop.
resolution:
Fixed in 762865a. New src/codegen/accum_overflow.rs recognizes the bounded counting loop and emits a plain add for the accumulator increment; the trap is provably dead so the elision is semantics-preserving.

MEASURED on kata #137 (four 120,001-element arrays, 40 punches, 30 runs / 5 warmup): kara 281.3ms -> 23.9ms +/- 1.1, an 11.8x improvement, sink unchanged at 79998760. Same program, other lanes: c -O3 -march=x86-64-v3 22.1 +/- 2.5 (kara 1.08x behind -- PARITY at equal ISA baseline), c -O3 34.0 +/- 1.3, rust -O 36.7 +/- 1.2, rust -O -C overflow-checks=on 270.3 +/- 12.8. So kara went from 'ties equal-safety Rust, 7.9x behind C' to 'parity with equal-baseline C, 11.3x AHEAD of equal-safety Rust' while still checking every other arithmetic operation in the program. That exceeds the success criterion this entry pre-registered (~281ms -> ~40ms, level with rust -O / clang -O3).

SOUNDNESS. The admitted pattern is `let acc = 0; let i = <lit >= 0>; while i < <bound> { ... acc = acc + 1 (EXACTLY ONE site) ... i = i + <lit >= 1> (one ascending step) }`. i starts non-negative and increases while i < bound, so trip <= bound; bound is an i64 VALUE so bound <= i64::MAX; acc starts at 0 and rises by 1 at most once per iteration, so acc <= trip <= i64::MAX at every point, including after the final increment. No platform assumption is needed (no reasoning about .len()'s range or address-space size). Site uniqueness and the zero initializer are both load-bearing: two sites give acc <= 2*trip and a non-zero start gives acc <= init + trip, either of which can overflow, so both are rejected. The counter's OWN check is deliberately retained. Every unmodelled shape fails closed, including any closure in the loop body.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTE worth carrying forward: codegen runs on the LOWERED AST, where `i < n` and `a + b` are trait-method Calls rather than ExprKind::Binary. The first cut matched only the surface forms and silently never fired on the target kata -- the same trap control_flow_bce.rs's guard_counter_var already documents. Both forms are matched now, and the analysis scans the whole block tree from one entry so hook placement in compile_block is not load-bearing either.

NOT HANDLED (deliberate, each breaks a step of the proof): the `acc += 1` compound form, steps other than 1, non-zero initializers, multiple increment sites, `for` loops, and accumulators that are fields / elements / captures.

Tests: 5 unit tests pinning each precondition individually; two E2E tests, one for semantics and one confirming a non-zero-init accumulator STILL traps with `integer overflow`. Corpus sweep over 30 counting-loop katas, all outputs unchanged (3 whose interpreter run exceeded the sweep timeout were verified against their Python oracles instead). Gates: fmt, clippy --all --all-targets --features llvm, codegen 2579, memory_sanitizer 853 (LSan live on Linux), non-llvm 8184.
investigation:
NOT a kara-specific defect and NOT a miscompile — kara and rustc-with-overflow-checks lose the same 7.9x to the same cause, so this is a MISSED OPTIMIZATION shared with rustc, filed because kara's checked-by-default arithmetic makes it the DEFAULT experience here rather than an opt-in one.

MECHANISM, ISOLATED IN THREE STEPS (all on the Rust mirror so the variable is exactly one statement):

1. IT IS THAT ONE CHECK, NOT CHECKED ARITHMETIC IN GENERAL. Making ONLY `cnt += 1` unchecked (`cnt.wrapping_add(1)`) while `overflow-checks=on` still applies to `i`, `b` and every expression in main: 277ms -> 30ms. One statement accounts for the whole gap.

2. IT IS NOT VECTORIZATION. Rebuilding that same unchecked variant with LLVM's loop and SLP vectorizers off (`-C llvm-args=-vectorize-loops=false -C llvm-args=-vectorize-slp=false`): still 40ms. The fast path is fast SCALAR code. (Independently confirmed on the C side: `clang -O3 -fno-vectorize -fno-slp-vectorize` stays at 40ms.)

3. IT IS BRANCH MISPREDICTION. Replacing the LCG-generated values with a constant, so `(nums[i] >> b) & 1` is uniform per bit position and the branch is perfectly predicted, collapses BOTH checked builds: rust_ovf 277 -> 45ms, kara 281 -> 50ms.

So: a checked `cnt + 1` can trap, therefore it cannot be speculated, therefore SimplifyCFG cannot if-convert the guarded increment into branchless `cnt += bit`. What remains is a real data-dependent branch on a ~50%-random bit over 154 million elements.

WHY THE CHECK IS REMOVABLE: `cnt` starts at 0 and is incremented at most once per iteration of a loop whose trip count is `nums.len()`, so `cnt <= len <= i64::MAX` holds by construction. The bound is provable by the same monotone-induction-variable reasoning the descending-loop BCE work (B-2026-07-17-1) already does for indices. Eliding the check restores if-conversion and, per step 1, recovers the entire 7.9x.

SCOPE: this is the general shape `acc = acc + <small constant>` where acc is a loop-local accumulator with a loop-bounded increment count — histogramming, counting, summing small bounded values. It is not specific to bit counting; #137 just makes it 32x hotter than usual by nesting the count inside a per-bit loop.

NEXT STEP: teach the overflow-check emission an accumulator-bound analysis — for an i64 local whose only writes in a loop are `x = x + K` with K a non-negative constant, and whose enclosing loop has a computable trip-count bound T, elide the check when `init + K*T` cannot overflow. Verify with the #137 bench: success is kara moving from ~281ms to ~40ms and pulling level with `rust -O` / `clang -O3` rather than with `rust_ovf`.

title: Map/Set probes called `eq_fn` on EVERY occupied bucket they walked past, because the status byte carried no hash information — one cold key dereference per probed slot, which for a `String` key was 77% of the #127 kata's L1-D read misses. Fixed by a hashbrown-style 7-bit hash tag in the control byte.
resolution:
FIXED 2026-07-28 (58412d9). The status byte now carries a 7-bit fragment of the key's hash: EMPTY = 0x00, TOMBSTONE = 0x01, OCCUPIED = 0x80 | tag7 where tag7 is bits 57..63. Both sentinels are below 0x80, so a lookup compares the bucket byte against the SEARCHED key's own control byte and gets occupancy and hash tag in ONE instruction, rejecting a non-matching key without touching it. The tag comes from the HIGH bits because the bucket index takes the low ones — a tag sharing them would be invariant along a probe chain and reject nothing.

MEASURED, with BOTH lanes built in one session. That qualifier is the finding worth carrying forward: the first A/B here read as a 12% REGRESSION because it compared against a binary another session had left in the bench directory. Rebuilding both arms from source reversed the sign. This is the third ledger entry spent on a stale bench binary; the standing note that `bench.sh`'s cache key should include the compiler that produced the binary is now overdue.

  * L1-D read misses 6,620,800 -> 2,135,000 (-68%), which puts kara BELOW the Rust lane's 2,931,820. cachegrind, so deterministic.
  * `karac_eq_String` alone 5,124,890 -> 1,189,583 (-77%) — 88% of the entire reduction. Everything else is unchanged to within noise: hash 205,202 -> 209,282, map-free 82,427 -> 82,427 exactly, malloc_consolidate 147,241 -> 147,039. That ISOLATES the mechanism rather than inferring it from the total.
  * Wall time 0.948x min / 0.915x median over 25 interleaved runs (interleaved so machine drift hits every lane equally).
  * I refs 2,314,631,913 -> 2,291,401,424 — slightly fewer.

THE ENTRY'S EARLIER 'INSTRUCTION PARITY' CLAIM DOES NOT REPRODUCE, and is retracted here rather than left standing. It recorded kara 1.782G vs rust 1.790G. Building both lanes fresh in one session measures kara 2.315G (pre-fix) against rust 1.830G — 1.25x, not parity. The Rust figure is close to the old one; kara's is 30% higher, so the old kara number is the suspect half, and the most likely explanation is the same stale-binary trap described above. What survives from the earlier round is the ATTRIBUTION (eq dominates the misses), which this fix confirmed directly and then removed.

STILL OPEN AFTER THIS, stated because the entry should not read as 'kara now matches Rust here': wall time is 1.50x the Rust lane (was 1.59x). Two things are visibly left. (1) Conditional branch mispredicts, 18.26M vs Rust's 11.13M — this fix moved them only slightly (from 20.40M) and the delta is NOT attributed, because Rust inlines its lookup into `main` and cannot be split against kara's out-of-line probes. (2) Instruction count, still 1.25x. Neither is a map-probe problem, so neither belongs to this entry.

SCOPE LIMIT, deliberate: the tag compare is on the LOOKUP probes (`Map.get`, the String-key `get`, `Set.contains`). The INSERT probes reach their occupied arm by elimination — not EMPTY, not TOMBSTONE — which stays correct verbatim under the new encoding, so they store the control byte but do not take the early-out. The measured cost was on the lookup side; adding the gate to inserts is a further slice.

THIS IS A CODEGEN/RUNTIME ABI. `src/codegen/mono.rs` emits its own probe loops and `control_flow_for.rs` / `runtime.rs` walk occupied slots, so all of them must agree with `runtime/src/map.rs`. Disagreement is a lookup that misses a present key — a silent wrong answer, not a crash or a link error. `ctrl_of` / `is_occupied` are the single source of truth on the runtime side, mirrored by `emit_map_ctrl_of` / `emit_map_is_occupied`, and two tests pin it: `control_byte_encoding_matches_codegen` (the literal values and the invariants codegen depends on) and `tagged_probe_survives_tombstones_and_resize` (2,000 keys through tombstones and several resizes, asserting both that live keys are found with the right value and that absent keys still miss). The E2E sibling `map_control_byte_tag_survives_resize_and_tombstones` drives all three EMITTED probe families the same way. The probe test was verified to BITE: dropping the tag on the resize path fails it.

NOTE for anyone changing the archives: the encoding change makes any previously built runtime archive an ABI mismatch, so all five (lean, full, arrow, wasm, wasm-threads) were rebuilt. A stale archive here would not fail to link — it would answer lookups wrongly.
detail:
SOURCE NOTE: found while benchmarking the #127 Word Ladder kata (kara-katas leetcode/101-200/127-word-ladder/bench), whose BFS is ~390k freshly built 5-byte Strings and ~390k String-keyed map lookups per punch and almost no arithmetic.

HEADLINE (x86-64 container): kara 293.6ms +/- 19.0 is LAST among the compiled languages -- rust 212.4 +/- 15.2, go 260.7 +/- 19.8, c 78.5 +/- 7.9. Correcting for the hash-fairness axis makes it WORSE, not better: kara's Map[String,_] hashes with FxHash (rotl5 ^ byte, * 0x517cc1b727220a95) while Rust's DEFAULT HashMap uses SipHash-1-3, so an equal-hash Rust lane (word_ladder_fasthash.rs, same FxHash constants) runs 177.3 +/- 22.6 against kara's 287.5 +/- 33.0 in one hyperfine session -- 1.62x, up from 1.38x at default hashers. SipHash was only costing Rust 1.18x.

ISOLATION (two focused microbenchmarks, both cross-checked to equal sinks):

1. STRING CONSTRUCTION IS NOT THE PROBLEM. The kata's `replace_char` (build a fresh String char-by-char with `push`) run 104,000 times, no map involved: kara 5.5ms +/- 0.7, rust 5.4ms +/- 0.6 -- a dead tie (1.03x, inside sigma). This CORRECTS the standing framing in kara-katas/BENCHMARKS.md, which attributes the corpus's residual string deficit to '1-byte push_str loops'. On this shape the push loop is at parity.

2. THE STRING-KEYED MAP IS. Build a Map[String,i64] of 3,125 five-byte words and look every one up, 60 rounds, against an equal-hash (FxHash) Rust HashMap doing the same: kara 37.9ms +/- 2.9, rust 15.5ms +/- 1.2 -- 2.45x. That single ratio accounts for the whole #127 deficit. RE-MEASURED 2026-07-28, and the headline finding changed: THE INSTRUCTION-COUNT GAP IS GONE. x86-64 container, `word_ladder.kara` vs `word_ladder.rs` (rustc -O -C overflow-checks=on, a faithful port — same linear `nth_letter`, same `replace_char`, verified by reading both), callgrind Ir: kara 1,782,104,538 vs rust 1,789,977,743 — kara 0.4% FEWER instructions. The entry's standing '1.235x whole-program I-ref ratio' is stale; B-2026-07-28-2's ASCII-const chars lowering closed it. WALL TIME STILL DIFFERS: 15 runs each, kara min 227.9ms / median 243.1ms vs rust min 179.1ms / median 184.5ms — 1.27x on min. Equal instructions and 1.27x time means the residual is now ENTIRELY IPC, which is a different problem from the one this entry was opened on and wants different tools. CACHEGRIND (cache-sim + branch-sim): D1 misses kara 8,896,520 vs rust 3,919,982 (2.27x); D1 read miss rate 2.1% vs 1.0%; conditional mispredicts kara 20,883,828 vs rust 11,064,910 (1.89x). Those two are the whole IPC story — LL misses are negligible on both (29K vs 24K), so everything is L2-resident and the cost is L1-miss latency, not DRAM. ATTRIBUTED, which is what this entry has been missing: `cg_annotate` on a KARAC_DEBUG_INFO build puts 5,988,829 of kara's 8,483,251 D1 READ misses (70.6%) in `karac_eq_String` ALONE — more than Rust's entire program (3,594,102). The kata's own `neighbors` accounts for 956,738 (11.3%) and malloc for 646,204 (7.6%). MECHANISM: `KaracMap::lookup` (runtime/src/map.rs) probes a status byte that is only BUCKET_EMPTY / BUCKET_OCCUPIED / BUCKET_TOMBSTONE — it carries NO hash information — so every OCCUPIED slot on the probe chain calls the full `eq_fn`, which dereferences the stored key's `{ptr,len,cap}` and then its heap bytes. With 3,125 individually malloc'd 5-byte keys those bytes are scattered, so each comparison is a pointer chase into a random line. Rust's hashbrown stores a 7-BIT HASH FRAGMENT in its control byte and rejects a non-matching slot without touching the key at all. QUANTIFIED, and one hypothesis was REFUTED on the way: `karac_eq_String` is called 4,348,884 times against `karac_hash_String`'s 4,003,331 — i.e. 1.09 eq per lookup, NOT the 2.5-4 a long-probe-chain story would predict (the map sits at ~38% load, so miss probes are short). The cost is not probe length; it is that kara dereferences a cold key on ~4.35M occasions where Rust does so only on hits plus a ~1/128 false-positive rate — roughly 0.85M. A 7-bit tag should therefore remove ~80% of eq calls and with them ~4.8M of kara's 8.9M D1 misses, landing at ~4.1M against Rust's 3.9M. HONEST LIMIT ON THAT PROJECTION: it accounts for the MISS delta, which is fully attributed. The MISPREDICT delta (kara 20.9M vs rust 11.1M conditional) is NOT attributed — Rust inlines the whole lookup into `word_ladder::main`, so its 9.79M mispredicts cannot be split against kara's `neighbors` 16.1M + `karac_eq_String` 3.0M. Do not assume the tag fixes both.
